

===== PAGE: about_clinical_data_studio | About Clinical Data Studio =====
## About Clinical Data Studio
 Medidata Clinical Data Studio is a complete data management and quality experience that provides seamless access to integrated data from Medidata and non-Medidata sources. Built with a user-friendly, no/low code environment, Clinical Data Studio uses AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows so that multiple users can act on real-time data in ways that reduce burden, shorten review timelines, increase quality, reduce risk, and improve patient safety.
## What Is Clinical Data Studio?
 Medidata Clinical Data Studio is a unified platform solution, which provides the following offerings: 
- Medidata Data Surveillance – Includes the following capability suites:
- Data Surveillance – Provides a drag-and-drop listings builder, automated query generation for Medidata Rave-sourced data, issue management for non-Medidata sourced data, AI-powered data reconciliation, patient profiles, and visualizations. 
- Data Connect – Enables self-service data ingestion and no/low-code data transformation capabilities.  
- Medidata Data Quality Management – Includes all the Data Surveillance capabilities above, plus the following additional capability suites: 
- RBQM – Provides  risk surveillance capabilities supporting a holistic risk-based quality management (RBQM) approach to data quality. 
- Cross Study Metrics – P rovides a   portfolio -level view of relevant data from upstream experiences, such as RBQM and Data Surveillance, across your studies. 
 Leveraging the Medidata Platform—the industry’s leading clinical research platform—and enabled by a scalable, flexible, open, and real-time streaming data architecture, Clinical Data Studio uniquely delivers a unified data management and analytics experience—powered by automation, AI, and advanced analytics—for all clinical data and multiple roles. With Clinical Data Studio, you can get started quickly and get value faster without extensive implementation timelines and ongoing managed service fees.
## What Is the Purpose of Clinical Data Studio?
 Built with a user-friendly, no/low code environment, Clinical Data Studio uses AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows so that multiple users can act on real-time data in ways that reduce burden, shorten review timelines, increase quality, reduce risk, and improve patient safety. Clinical Data Studio provides:
- Streamlined self-serve ingestion to manage non-Medidata data transfer. 
- Low/no-code transformation and standardization engine to minimize technical resource burden. 
- Comprehensive data quality, risk, and safety management capabilities. 
- Embedded AI and smart analytics to automate manual, error-prone tasks and accelerate time to insight. 
- Dynamic, fit-for-purpose visualizations and dashboards for a total view of the patient and study. 
 Clinical Data Studio unlocks efficiencies and accelerates clinical discovery by supporting a wide variety of use cases for clinical data managers, clinical operations, medical monitors, clinical programming, and other data stakeholders.
 With its Data Surveillance and Data Quality Management offerings, Clinical Data Studio delivers a comprehensive data quality solution, including accelerated review of data and patient profiles, easy-to-configure on-demand visualizations, AI-assisted data reconciliation, risk management, site performance monitoring, collaborative issue management, anomaly detection, and patient safety overview.
## Who Uses Clinical Data Studio?
 Clinical Data Managers and Clinical Data Scientists 
- Automate data review and query management. 
- Identify data patterns with advanced analytics. 
- Reconcile complex data with AI. 
 Clinical Operations and Safety 
- Identify site and study risks sooner with real-time dashboards. 
- Explore patient safety issues comprehensively. 
- Predict and monitor SAEs with AI. 
 Clinical Programmers and IT 
- Eliminate manual data integration activities.
- Ingest-Transform-Extract datasets in low code environment. 
- Accelerate data mapping for submission. 
 C-Suite and Executives 
- Break operational silos 
- Generate high quality and submission-ready data faster
- Increase visibility and make decisions faster 
## How Does Clinical Data Studio Work?
 Clinical Data Studio   ingests your team's study data from:  
- Rave 
- Third-party vendor data—for example, protocol deviations, lab data, or any data not uploaded through Rave—which gets uploaded through Data Connect's Imports capability  or through Ingestor . 
 Note : New studies will import external, third-party data using Imports. However, legacy studies that have previously ingested data through Ingestor can continue to import data through Ingestor.
 In Data Surveillance and RBQM, study data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave, and activated datasets from Data Connect are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM.
 Once Clinical Data Studio pulls the study's data sets and variables into your study environment, you can use the following apps and their capabilities: 
- Data Connect: 
- Datasets – R eview existing datasets that you have access to including from Rave, external data sources, and transformed data sets. 
- Imports – M anage and import data from external sources. 
- Exports – Create and manage export jobs to extract your data from the Medidata platform. 
- Transformations – C reate data sets, and transform them depending on your needs: 
- Data Surveillance: 
- Task Oversight – A dashboard that shows study metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) from Patient Profiles, Vendor Queries, Listings, AI Reconciliation, and Data Connect. It  allows you to track and monitor in one centralized location the progress of patient data in your study that requires vetting and review. 
- Clean Patient Tracker – View a  dashboard that visualizes, lists, and prioritizes the outstanding patient data cleaning tasks across Data Surveillance that require vetting and review. 
- Data Sets – M onitor high-risk, critical, or complex study data from Rave and third-party data vendors to mitigate and prevent issues to data quality or integrity. 
- Open EDC Queries –  V iew in one consolidated location the detailed list of all open and answered queries raised against patient data in your study. 
- Vendor Queries – Report and track external data issues with vendors. 
- Listings – Create conditional expressions that parse your study data to identify and report patient data records within a specified variable that may indicate a study risk. 
- AI Reconciliation – View automated reports that use built-in algorithms to reconcile site data and identify anomalies within adverse event (AE), concomitant medication (CM), and medical history (MH) data sets. 
- Patient Profiles – Build patient profile designs using tables, flags, graphs, and timelines to identify safety signals and ensure patient data consistency. 
- Custom Graphs – A self-serve data visualization and reporting tool that enables you to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data on demand. 
- Oncology - RECIST 1.1 – View auto-generated visualizations that produces  the treatment response and disease progression metrics for patients based on the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1 methodology. 
- Data Surveillance Configuration – Enables you to:
- Map the specific   study data that you want Data Surveillance and RBQM to report on and visualize. 
- Configure: 
- Automation of data refreshes across Data Surveillance. 
- Vendors to which you want to communicate vendor data issues. 
- Derived variables. 
- Stacked datasets. 
- Review reports. 
- RBQM: 
- Data Quality Hub   – A dashboard view of RBQM-related key performance metrics and list of 25th sites based on site impact score.. The Data Quality Hub enables you to identify areas of study risk and directly access the RBQM capabilities you need address the identified risks. 
- Risk Assessment – A highly collaborative, continually iterated workspace that cross-team study members use to document identified areas of risk. Risk Assessment enables teams to Identify and address high priority risks, evaluate risk performance, as well as review and approve risk plan reports. 
- Risk Inventory – A real-time, comprehensive list of all study risks and associated QTLs and KRIs documented in the Risk Assessment. You can track, monitor, and manage risks from the Risk Inventory. 
- Plan Documents –  Build and publish integrated data quality plans and   add components to your plan—i ncluding functional plans— to review and monitor data throughout a study. 
- Protocol Integrity Report – A centralized dashboard that enables you to capture, track, review, and manage protocol deviations. It centralizes protocol deviations from multiple sources into a single view. The system aligns identified deviations with the Protocol Deviation Assessment Plan (PDAP). 
- KRI Dashboard – A dashboard view of the key risk indicators (KRIs) that your study monitors and their respective KRI values at each site or country. Monitoring KRI metrics from the KRI Dashboard enables teams to monitoring site and country performance and compliance. 
- QTL Dashboard –  A dashboard view of the performance metrics associated with the quality tolerance limits that your study monitors. The QTL Dashboard enables study teams  to c learly, quickly, and confidently evaluate the health and performance of study-level parameters that are critical to study quality. 
- Statistical Monitoring – A data analysis and visualization solution that applies advanced statistical analytics on clinical study data to detect risks, anomalies, and trends. Statistical Monitoring includes the following capabilities: 
- Data Anomaly Detection – View AI-powered visualizations of RBQM's analysis for a single variable or pair of variables in your study data. You can use Data Anomaly Detection to determine outliers, anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data, and further investigate or report your data findings as necessary. 
- Trends – Show a single variable's data at each site side by side using a box-and-whisker plot or stacked bar chart. You can use trend plots to pinpoint sites with abnormal or incorrect data that may warrant investigation. 
- Weekend and Holiday Visits – View patient visit listings that break down at the study or country level how many scheduled patient visits occurred on each day of the week throughout the study. Viewing the scheduled patient visits that occurred on weekends or holidays can help you investigate whether falsified or erroneous patient records exist in your study data. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients – View on an interactive heatmap the site locations in your study that RBQM identifies as having potential duplicate patients. Identifying and investigating sites with potential duplicate patients helps ensure data integrity and improves the chance of study success. 
- Rounding and Propagation – View heatmaps to identify potentially unreliable data or noncompliant sites, and then further investigate or report your data findings as necessary. 
- Event Incidence – Shows the reported events and the incidence rate in which those events occurred within a domain at the site and study level. You can use the Event Incidence Plot to determine sites whose reporting of events may require further investigation or corrective action as well as whether a drug should be discontinued. 
- Under-Over Reporting Events – Visualizes event reporting patterns across adverse events (AE), concomitant medication (CM), and medical history (MH) at the site and country level. The Under-Over Reporting Events Plot helps you identify potentially noncompliant sites and countries whose event reporting patterns significantly differ from the study norm. 
- History – Schedule data refreshes or manually trigger refreshes in Statistical Monitoring's capabilities and view historical data snapshots. 
- Signals – Identify, track, and take action on potential study data issues by creating automated and manual threshold-based signals. 
- Audit Trail Review – Ask questions into a chat interface and use Large Learning Models (LLMs) and Generative AI to explore and create audit data sets from complex Rave study data. Users with permissions can save and publish audit data sets and for use in KRIs and Listings. 
- RBQM Configuration – Enables you to:
- Map the specific   study data that you want Data Surveillance and RBQM to report on and visualize. 
- Configure the risk scoring scale and data you want to capture in the risk assessment. 
- Create and manage: 
- KRIs and QTLs 
- Derived variables 
- Stacked datasets 
- Review reports 
- Configure the Clinical Data Studio capabilities that Data Surveillance and RBQM use to produce signals for. 
- RBQM Template Library – Enables you to:
- Create and manage Critical Data, Critical Processes, and Risk Categorization templates. 
- Platform Library –  P rovides  centralized   access to the global template library to view and manage :
- Listings, KRIs, QTLs and Custom Graphs Templates – Store and reuse common data listing, QTL, KRI, and Custom Graphs configurations that your organization is likely to include in multiple study configurations. 
- Transformation Templates – Create standardized, reusable, and version-controlled templates that capture and apply the transformation logic from source projects in Data Connect.  
- Cross Study Metrics :
- Data Management Quality Metrics – dashboards with preset and organized visuals pertaining to   Data Surveillance   and  RBQM   data such as KRI data across your studies. Dashboards include: 
- KRIs – You can view metrics about key risk indicators across your studies based on data from RBQM. 
- QTLs – You can view metrics about   quality tolerance limits  (QTLs) across your studies based on data from  RBQM .   
- Clean Patients – You can view metrics about patients with clean data across your studies based on data from Data Surveillance. 
 To learn more, see:
- Data Connect 
- Data Surveillance 
- RBQM 
- Cross Study Metrics 
 Important : Clinical Data Studio supports a limited range of numeric values. The exists between 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 and -9,223,372,036,854,775,807. Any number that falls outside this range appears as null in Clinical Data Studio.

## What Are the Benefits of Clinical Data Studio?
 Clinical Data Studio enables study teams to:
- Ingest and integrate all study data from multiple data sources.
- Access data from Medidata data sources, including Rave, and easily import data from any non-Medidata source, such as labs or another EDC system. 
- Data transfer agreements can be configured into Clinical Data Studio to validate ingested data automatically. 
- Transform data with minimal effort.
- Transform and prepare data in any way needed for review and analysis with no or little programming required. 
- Reduce the burden on technical teams and domain experts by simplifying transformation activities with a no/low code environment. 
- Perform data review, safety surveillance, and risk monitoring using the same real-time data within a unified data management and analytics experience. 
- Data acquired on or ingested into the platform is streamed to data transformation and quality management tasks in real time. This: 
- Centralizes all your data’s lifecycle in one consistent experience for all clinical data, multiple roles, powered by automation, AI, and advanced analytics. 
- Ensures that everyone on the study team is working with the latest data. 
- Breaks operational and data silos, increasing efficiency, visibility, and driving better informed and faster decisions 
- Moves your RBQM strategies closer to the data and bridge the gap between data management and risk monitoring initiatives 
- Achieve high-quality data faster.
- Automate data review, bulk query management, data reconciliation, and surveillance with AI/ML and dynamic tracker dashboards. 
- Use AI-powered workflows to simplify, accelerate, and gain faster data surveillance and risk management insights. 
- Alleviate bottlenecks by enabling parallel workflows to clean, monitor, and transform data at the same time. 
- Enhance study and participant safety.
- Optimize patient profile reviews with visualizations and drill-downs to easily reveal patient safety issues. 
- Optimize patient safety monitoring activities with holistic data and predictive analyses 
- Reduce study risk and improve site performance.
- Enhance study oversight, mitigate risk, and ensure compliance with advanced analytics.

===== PAGE: access_and_reuse_data_listing__qtl__and_kri_templates_across_multiple_client_divisions | Access and Reuse Data Listing, QTL, and KRI Templates Across Multiple Client Divisions =====
## Access and Reuse Data Listing, QTL, and KRI Templates Across Multiple Client Divisions
## What Is New?
 In previous releases, you could only build, access, and reuse data listing, QTL, and custom KRI templates within a single client division (CD) . Now can you build, access, and reuse templates across multiple client divisions.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Members of your organization who build studies can save and store data listing, QTL, and custom KRI configurations as templates in your organization's template library. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 In previous releases, some customers—like CROs who may have multiple clients, for example—were unable to build, access, and reuse templates across multiple clients. The ability to reuse templates across multiple client divisions enables you to: 
- Share templates more widely study collections for broader study teams. 
- Standardize your templates across clients. 
- Reduce the amount of templates you may need to build. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In:
- Data Surveillance > Listings page > Draft Listings tab > Import Template dialog > Template Group menu 
- Data Surveillance > Listings page > Manage Listings page > Export as Template dialog > Template Group menu 
- RBQM > Configuration > Key Risk Indicators page > KRI Configurations tab > Import Template dialog > Template Group menu 
- RBQM > Configuration > Key Risk Indicators page > KRI Configurations tab > Customer Number KRI window or Customer Percentage KRI window > Export as Template dialog > Template Group menu 
- RBQM > Configuration > Quality Tolerance Limits page > Import Templates dialog > Template Group menu 
- RBQM > Configuration > Quality Tolerance Limits page > Quality Tolerance Limit window > Export as Template dialog > Template Group window 
 the list of template group names shows in parentheses the client division name that the template group belongs to. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature
- Add Listings as Templates to Template Groups 
- Add and Store Custom KRI Configurations as Reusable Templates 
- Add and Store Custom QTL Configurations as Reusable Templates 
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs 
- Add and Edit Custom QTLs 
## What Else Should I Know?
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

## Access to Rave EDC Source Data Only Available for Rave EDC-Derived Patient Profile Data
## Description
 Authorized Rave EDC users can access Rave EDC from the Patient Profiles user interface by selecting a patient ID in the Patient Selector and then clicking View in Rave EDC . The View in Rave EDC  button appears only if all or some of the patient data originates from Rave EDC.
## Affected Roles
 All Detect users with access to Rave EDC.
## Advantages
 Accessing Rave EDC from Patient Profiles allows profile reviewers and Detect users to investigate patient records associated with data points in Patient Profiles.
## User Impact
 See Description.

 The Patient Profiles Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support the enhancement: 
- Rave EDC Data Integration

 All.

 You can quickly find the user assistance directly pertaining to the page in Medidata Detect you are working in with one click rather than opening up the Medidata Detect Knowledge Space Home page and navigating to the article you need.
## User Impact
 The Medidata Detect Help menu now includes the "Help on this Page" option, which when clicked, directs you to the specific knowledge space article pertaining to the current Medidata Detect page you are working in.

## Access User Assistance Pertaining to a Specific Page or Field With One Click
## Description
 The user interface provides progressive user assistance (PUA) in select locations indicated by a clickable icon. 
 PUA may include hyperlinks that open a new browser tab to related product content on the Knowledge Hub. PUA implementation is ongoing and does not affect product functionality. You can expect new PUA to coincide with or follow product releases.         
 Affected Roles 
 All.
## Advantages
 Providing progressive user assistance directly on a page or field ensures that you find the help information you need faster and easier than searching through online help.
## User Impact
 You can access progressive user assistance by c licking a Help icon  on any Detect page. When you click a Help icon, user assistance pertaining to the directly associated page or field automatically displays in a popover. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: action_taken_enhancements_for_risks | Action Taken Enhancements for Risks =====
## Action Taken Enhancements for Risks
## Description
 The Risk Management 2022.2.0 release lets you add multiple actions for a risk, so that you can track the actions associated with the action taken date. 
## Affected Roles
 Study Users
## Advantages
 Before the Risk Management 2022.2.0 release, you entered dates and text related to actions together in the same field when you added a risk. This release allows you to create multiple actions with target start and completion dates so you can more easily track upcoming actions. 
## User Impact
 When adding a risk, you can click next to Action Taken to enter one or more actions to take when reviewing the risk:
- Action Taken date (required). If the user hovers the mouse over the Last Action Taken Date column of Risk Inventory, then the description of the latest action taken appears. 
- Action Completion date (optional) 
- Action Taken description (required)  
 In addition, you can:
- Save an action or cancel it 
- Delete an action if not required later 
- View the latest action associated to the risk in the Risk Inventory section of the Risk Plan Report. For example: 
 The Action Taken  column is renamed as Last Action Taken Date in the Risk Inventory and on the Critical Data, Critical Processes, and Risk Categorization pages. Sorting is by date, and the format is DD-MMM-YYYY. You can only edit the   Last Action Taken Date   on the Risk Details or Add Risk pages. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Risk Management Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
- Risk Inventory 
## Special Considerations
 None.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: activate_and_deactivate_kris_in_rbqm_configuration_manager | Activate and Deactivate KRIs in RBQM Configuration Manager =====
## Activate and Deactivate KRIs in RBQM Configuration Manager
## Description
 You can activate custom KRIs  so   that data gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, and displayed in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicator table . If a custom KRI no longer requires analysis, you can deactivate that KRI so that the KRI's data no longer gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, or displayed in Medidata Detect. 
## Affected Roles
 RBQM Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Tracking custom KRIs helps your organization target and track unique and specific facets of your study that you want to monitor for risk.
## User Impact
 On the KRIs page > Key Risk Indicators list > Activate column, you can click   in the corresponding row of the KRI you want to activate. To deactivate, you can click  . 
## Special Considerations
- Allow one business day after activating custom KRIs to allow Detect to refresh the analytics and render the custom KRIs' data in the Key Risk Indicators table. 
- RBQM Configuration Manager only stores the most recent deactivation note for deactivated KRIs.

===== PAGE: activate_and_deactivate_qtls_in_rbqm_configuration_manager | Activate and Deactivate QTLs in RBQM Configuration Manager =====
## Activate and Deactivate QTLs in RBQM Configuration Manager
## Description
 You can activate custom QTLs  so   that data gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, and displayed in: 
- Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicator table 
- Risk Management's Risk Inventory page and Add Risk page 
 If a custom QTL no longer requires analysis, you can deactivate that QTL so the data no longer gets filtered, analyzed, calculated, or displayed in Medidata Detect or Risk Management. 
 When you deactivate QTLs, you must enter the reason for deactivation in the Deactivation Note dialog box. 
## Affected Roles
 RBQM Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Activating and tracking custom QTLs helps your organization  target and monitor the greatest risks to  a study's: 
- Safety 
- Conduct 
- Performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
 Deactivating custom QTLs:
- Removes from Medidata Detect's Quality Tolerance Limits page the QTL data that you have no need to track or analyze. 
- Yields a cleaner QTL table view by displaying only data that is relevant to your study. 
- Optimizes your QTL data analysis speed and efficiency. 
 Documenting deactivation notes for deactivated QTLs enables you to track QTL status and to further target analysis.
## User Impact
 On the QTLs page > Quality Tolerance Limits list > Activate column, you can click   in the corresponding row of the QTL you want to activate. To deactivate, you can click  . 
 When you deactivate a QTL, you must describe the reason for deactivating the QTL in the Deactivation Note dialog box. 
 You can then  View Audit Details for Deactivated QTLs . 
## Special Considerations
- Allow one business day after activating custom QTLs to allow Detect to refresh the analytics and render the custom QTLs' data in the Quality Tolerance Limits table. 
- RBQM Configuration Manager only stores the most recent deactivation note for deactivated QTLs. 
- You can reactivate previously deactivated QTLs using the same process you would to activate. To learn more, see Activate and Deactivate QTLs .

===== PAGE: add_and_edit_custom_kris_in_rbqm_configuration_manager | Add and Edit Custom KRIs in RBQM Configuration Manager =====
## Add and Edit Custom KRIs in RBQM Configuration Manager
## Description
 Within a given study environment , you can define and add custom KRIs   that target specific facets of your study data that you want to monitor for risk. After creation, you can update the custom KRI name and description, if necessary. 
## Affected Roles
 RBQM Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Defining custom KRIs in a single, centralized location helps your organization consistently target and track unique and specific facets of your study that you want to monitor for risk.
## User Impact
 On the KRIs page, you can click Add Custom KRI to define and save a custom KRI within a study environment.
 You can also click a custom KRI listed on the KRIs page to edit the custom KRI's name and description.
## Special Considerations
- Medidata develops and maintains a standard  list of risk categories to which custom KRIs get assigned. 
- When adding a custom KRI, the KRI's risk category is defined as "Other" by default. However, once created and saved, the KRI's risk category is updated according to the risk category associated with the KRI's selected data set .

===== PAGE: add_and_edit_custom_percentage_kris | Add and Edit Custom Percentage KRIs =====
## Add and Edit Custom Percentage KRIs
## Description
 Within a given study environment, you can define and add custom percentage KRIs to target and monitor specific study data for risk. With custom percentage KRIs, you can build functional expressions to query your study database to assess if subjects meet certain conditions or criteria.   For example, you can build a percentage KRI that reports the percentage of all study subjects who  experienced  a systolic blood pressure over 140. Or you can build a percentage KRI that calculates the percentage of all study subjects who reported experiencing a specific adverse event. 
 Medidata Detect  produces an incidence analysis on the custom percentage KRI, which you can view  in Detect's Key Risk Indicators table  and Contributors list. 
 After creation, you can update the custom percentage KRI name and description. 
## Affected Roles
 RBQM Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Custom percentage KRIs provide you greater control and flexibility of the specific data and metrics that you want Medidata Detect to analyze and report. Therefore, you can better target your study data analysis on areas that most require your attention to optimally monitor and investigate risk. 
## User Impact
 On the KRIs page, you can click  Add Custom KRI  > Percentage , which navigates you to the new Custom Percentage KRI page. 
 Tip : Click image to enlarge.
 On the Custom Percentage KRI page, you can define and save a custom percentage KRI within a study environment. You define custom percentage KRIs by building functional expressions. The expressions consist of one or more conditions. You build conditions using date, numeric, or text variables from the list of data sets available within a study environment. You then select a comparator for the variable, such as: =, !=, >, <, >=, <=, One Of, Missing, Not Missing, or Contains. You then apply a comparator value that serves as the conditional threshold based on selected comparator. Values can be dates selected from a calendar date picker, a date or numeric variable from the list of data sets, manually entered text or values, or one or more patient-reported terms selected from a dropdown. 
 You can then add additional conditions to build an expression with a jointed condition set using the following operators:  .
 Activating a custom percentage KRI triggers the KRI's data to get filtered, analyzed, calculated, and displayed in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table and Contributors list. 
 You can also click a custom percentage KRI listed on the KRIs page to edit the custom percentage KRI's name and description. 
 For details about adding and editing custom percentage KRIs, see  Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs . 
## Special Considerations
- The list of selectable comparators and comparator value options differ based on whether you are working with a variable of date, number, or text data type. For more information, see  Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs . 
- When using a variable as the comparator value, the originally selected variable and comparator variable must come from the same data set. 
- When using parentheses to build a condition comprised of multiple operations, you must properly encapsulate the condition with a left paren and right paren. Otherwise, you cannot save the customer percentage KRI. Errant parens also prevent you from saving. 
- If you build a percentage KRI's expression using multiple data sets from different risk categories (for example, endpoints and safety), then the percentage KRI is assigned the Other risk category.

===== PAGE: add_and_edit_custom_qtls_in_rbqm_configuration_manager | Add and Edit Custom QTLs in RBQM Configuration Manager =====
## Add and Edit Custom QTLs in RBQM Configuration Manager
## Description
 Within a given study environment , you can define and add custom QTLs that target specific facets of your study data that you want to monitor for risk. If necessary, you can also edit the details of the custom QTLs that you create. 
## Affected Roles
 RBQM Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Defining custom QTLs in a single, centralized location helps your organization  target and monitor the greatest risks to  a study's: 
- Safety 
- Conduct 
- Performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
 QTLs that reach or exceed a a pre-identified data quality threshold indicate that the QTL's target study parameter may warrant investigation and mitigation. Tracking QTLs helps: 
- Ensure the study conduct operates as planned. 
- Identify as well as prevent or mitigate systematic issues early on in the study that may: 
- Threaten subject safety or study efficacy. 
- Invalidate the reliability of the study findings. 
## User Impact
 On the QTLs page, you can click Add Custom QTL  to define and save a custom QTL within a study environment.
 You can also click a custom QTL listed on the QTLs page to edit the custom QTL's details .
## Special Considerations
 You cannot configure site-level QTLs. You must create QTLs to monitor thresholds for specific site-level parameters.

===== PAGE: add_custom_risk_categories_to_templates_and_associated_studies | Add Custom Risk Categories to Templates and Associated Studies =====
## Add Custom Risk Categories to Templates and Associated Studies
## What Is New?
 You can now create a custom category when you select Custom in the Select Category dropdown, while creating a Risk Categorization Template, Critical Data, or Critical Process at client division level. You can also add these templates to their study and the categories associated with them.
- You can now create multiple custom risk categories to a risk categorization template, and 
- Create custom categories to use the templates at study-level for Critical Data and Critical processes. 
## What Is the Impact?

===== PAGE: add_flags_to_designs_patient_profiles | Add Flags to Designs Patient Profiles =====
## Add Flags to Designs Patient Profiles
## Description
 Flags are conditional expressions that highlight important, high-level study information about patients. Reviewers use flags to quickly gauge a patient's status and the study's progress. For example, when reviewing a patient's report, you can quickly see whether a patient died, had a serious adverse event (SAE), and so on.  You build flag condition using variables from any data set to create expressions.  Designs require at least one flag.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Flags allow report reviewers to quickly gauge a patient's status and the study's progress.
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- add flags; 
- edit flag names, operators, values, and expressions; and 
- remove flag rows. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: add_headers_to_designs_patient_profiles | Add Headers to Designs Patient Profiles =====
## Add Headers to Designs Patient Profiles
## Description
 The header is the top section in the profile design. Designs can have only one header. Headers comprise one or more rows that are three or six columns wide. These columns hold flag information and individual variable information. Profiles require at least one flag; therefore, profile designs must also include a header to contain the flag. The Header section remains fixed at the top of the page when a you scroll down when viewing the patient profile in CSA.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Headers identify the information contained in a section within the profile. Headers also hold flag and variable information. Rows without headers—such as patient information tables, which contain information only—benefit from having headers atop the row to label and define the table.
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- Add headers, 
- Name and rename headers, 
- Add header rows, 
- Rename header variables, 
- Change the placement of a header row, and 
- Remove header rows. 
## Special Considerations
 Headers are heavily weighted during the CSA analytics process. Therefore, we encourage you to use headers for information that CSA can analyze. For example, you do not want to add a Study Name variable to a header since the same variable applies across all subjects .

===== PAGE: add_notes_to_elements_and_layout_sections_to_provide_insight_on_profile_data | Add Notes to Elements and Layout Sections to Provide Insight on Profile Data =====
## Add Notes to Elements and Layout Sections to Provide Insight on Profile Data
## Description
 Patient profile designers can add a single note to an element or layout section.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Adding a note to display at the end of an element or layout section gives patient profile reviewers added insight into the profile's study data. Notes are especially useful with regards to the Highlight Condition functionality for explaining the conditions that result in data displaying in a particular color. For example:
 “Red Text is Lab Value Above Normal Limits and Blue Text is Lab Value Below Normal Limits” or “Yellow Highlight = Serious AE; Light Orange Highlight = Severe AE; Pink Highlight = Both”
## User Impact
 Tip : Click to enlarge images below.
 On the Elements tab, a Note link displays at the top of all elements with exception to flag elements. Click the Note link to add note text .
 On the Layout tab, a Note link displays at the top of all sections with exception to the Header Section. Click the Note link to add note text.
 On the Profiles tab, any notes you add in the Elements tab or Layout tab display at the bottom of the corresponding element or layout section in the patient profile. Notes display in the patient profile with a yellow background and italicized font.
## Special Considerations
 You cannot add notes to flag elements on the Elements tab.
 You cannot add notes to the Header Section on the Layout tab.

===== PAGE: add_timelines_to_designs_patient_profiles | Add Timelines to Designs Patient Profiles =====
## Add Timelines to Designs Patient Profiles
## Description
 Timelines allow you to visually compare specific data points over the duration of a study in a single output. For example, you can view visit dates, study days, adverse events, con meds, and so on in a single visual element. 
 Timelines can include randomization and visit data, drug data, event tables, or individual date variables.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Timelines allow you to: 
- effectively compare data against each other, and  
- view correlations in one output rather than having to cross-reference multiple data sets. 
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- Add timelines to designs; 
- Add variables and event tables to timelines; 
- Assign colors to variables display in the timeline; 
- View and edit value labels; 
- Set element display conditions; 
- Edit visit variable labels; 
- Edit timeline details; 
- Remove variables and events; and 
- Delete element display conditions. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: add_transposed_tables_to_designs_patient_profiles | Add Transposed Tables to Designs Patient Profiles =====
## Add Transposed Tables to Designs Patient Profiles
## Description
 Transposed tables allow for multiple values that may be separate lines of data to display in a single table row. You can create transposed tables for data that is structured in a long, skinny format to display in a wide table format. Generally, that is lab data, physical exam data, questionnaires, and so on. Transposed tables also display the same test name in a single column to allow you to easily view the data over time.  
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- Add transposed tables to designs;

- Configure transposed table display and highlight conditions; 
- Edit transposed table details:
- Rename transposed tables, 
- Add variables to tables, 
- Rename variables, 
- Remove variables from tables, and 
- Select, view, and remove test values. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

 A wide table allows for up to 12 columns of data. You create wide tables for data that you do not need to display in a timeline, such as medical history. All data in a wide table must come from the same data set.

 See the Description section.

- Remove display and highlight conditions.

===== PAGE: assess_overall_study_performance_using_the_overview | Assess Overall Study Performance Using the Overview =====
## Assess Overall Study Performance Using the Overview
## Description
 Medidata Detect now includes the Overview page. The Overview is the initial landing page when you launch Medidata Detect . The Overview provides Medidata Detect's summarized analysis of your study data by reporting: 
- An overall study performance assessment based on an  A-F grading scale . 
- The percentage of discrepant data in your study data at the overall study level. 
- The average discrepancy score for all data points in the study. 
- The most discrepant, high-risk individual study factors at the following perspectives: 
- Risk Categories 
- Domains 
- Countries 
- Sites 
 The Overview serves as a clear starting point in your study data review process by:
- Reporting the overall health and level of discrepant data in the study. 
- Presenting the worst to best performing aspects within each data perspective based on percentage of discrepant data. 
- Providing guided navigation, which allows you to easily drill down and investigate the aspects and specific data most requiring your attention. 
## Affected Roles
 All Medidata Detect users use the Overview. Based on your role in a study, you may want to focus on specific data perspectives or aspects within a perspective. 
## Advantages
 The Overview: 
- Provides a clear and natural starting point in your study data review process. 
- Navigates you on the optimal path to find and investigate the data that's most important and relevant to you. 
- Provides quick and easy access to the error plots. 
- Ensures you are always clearly oriented within Medidata Detect . 
- Expedites the data review process. 
- Leads to higher-quality study data. 
## User Impact
 The Overview is the initial landing page when you launch Medidata Detect .   You can  navigate to the Overview page from any other Medidata Detect page. To learn more, see   Overview . 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: audit_trail_review__verify_audit_trail_chat_questions_using_sql_query | Audit Trail Review: Verify Audit Trail Chat Questions Using SQL Query =====
## Audit Trail Review: Verify Audit Trail Chat Questions Using SQL Query
## What Is New?
 You can now view the underlying SQL query that Audit Trail Review (ATR) uses to retrieve audit data from your study.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All study team members.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow processes.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can validate whether the audit data shown matches the question you asked in the chat option. You can further edit the question as required based in the formatted SQL query text. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the RBQM tab > Audit Trail Review > new audit review section, type your question into the chat option, and ATR shows the audit data in the Data Preview section on the right of the page. Then if you click the More icon ( ), then click View SQL , you can view the underlying SQL code that retrieves audit data based on your question from the study.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement.
- Audit Trail Review 
## What Else Should I Know?
 Permissions 
- You must have the  View Audit Trail Review t o ask questions and save prompts, whereas to publish audit data sets you need the Manage Audit Trail Review building block added respectively to your role in Cloud Administration.  
 ATR Behavior 
- No blinded data sets are shown as part of audit trail review data. 
- You can only publish a maximum of 10 audit data sets in any study.  
- The audit workflow runs every day. The published data set is available in the study 30 minutes after it was published. 
- You cannot publish and download a data set if the Data Preview shows no records. 
 ATR Limitations 
- Audit trail review does not support: 
- Any aggregations. For example, a question like Give audits for AE form where a data point was modified more than 10 times, may produce a data set that was modified just once. 
- Complex computations, or calculating differences in timestamps. For example, a question like Give audits where a datapoint was modified 10 days after it was entered. may not produce a result. 
- Results at any level other than data points. For example, a question like Give me all sites in the data, does not produce a result. 
- Filtering on data point values. 
- Question prompts asking for all audits in the study. 
- Filtering in the published audit data set is limited to the following fields:  
- audit user, audit date/date range, form oid, field oid, audit subcategories, patient ID, country, and site. 
- Published audit data listings do not support the following functionality: 
- Submit queries. 
- Submit vendor queries. 
- Cross-dataset listing creation 
- Missing records 
- The ATR functionality times out if the learning model takes longer than five minutes to process a request. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

## Browse Data Sets and Add Variables to Elements More Efficiently
## Description
 When working in the Design page > Elements tab, the Data Options tab—which contains your list of data sets and variables—now offers the following improvements:
 Tip : Click any image to enlarge.
 Description 
 Image 
 | A green border displays to the left of data sets that contain at least one variable that is currently applied to the design.
 | 
 | A blue border displays to the left of data sets that contain no variables that are currently applied to the design. 
 | 
 | 
 A green border displays on all sides of a variable that is currently applied to the design.
 Note : Unused variables display without any border.
 | 
 | 
 When working with wide tables and transposed tables:
 If the table already contains a selected variable, then you cannot click and drag any other variables from the Data Options tab.
 Notes:
- You can still view the variables within the data sets in the Data Options tab. But you cannot actively click-and-drag any variables. 
- You can view the variable settings for disabled variables. But you cannot change the data type of a disabled variable. 
- If you remove a variable from a wide or transposed table, then you can once again actively click-and-drag variables from the Data Options tab. 
 | 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The usability improvements to the Data Options tab include:
- Data sets that display with green and blue left-hand borders. Colored borders allow you to quickly identify which data sets contain variables, flags, or event tables that are currently used in the design. 
- Variables that display with green borders on all sides. The green borders allow you to quickly identify which variables are currently applied to the design. 
- Variables that become disabled when working with wide tables or transposed tables that already contain a variable. For wide tables and transposed tables, all variables in the table must come from the same data set. Therefore, when a table already contains a variable, disabling your ability to click-and-drag variables from the Data Options tab prevents you from adding variables from another data set. 
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 The data sets and variables in the Settings page > Design Options tab do not include the improvements described in the Description section above.

===== PAGE: build_listings_by_selecting_variables_from_multiple_data_sets | Build Listings By Selecting Variables From Multiple Data Sets =====
## Build Listings By Selecting Variables From Multiple Data Sets
## Description
 The Listings submenu and page no longer exist separately in Data Reviewer. Instead, you can access listings and data sets on the Data Reviewer page. The Listings functionality now allows you to select a maximum of 10 data set variables from six different data sets.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
- You can create listings based on complex search criteria that compares data across multiple data sets . For example, female patients below age 50 who have had a serious adverse event.  
- You can navigate less to find data sets and build listings as you access listings and data sets from the same page. 
## User Impact
 New Listing 
 The Listings submenu and page are no longer available in Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) > Data Reviewer. Instead, you can create and access listings on the Data Reviewer page on the Listings panel. If you click New Listing , drag-and-drop variables from data sets, complete the expression builder workflow, you can then save the listing. The expression builder includes a new dropdown with two options to compare two data set variables of the same type:
- Variable – You can drag-and-drop a data set variable into the Variable field. The variable can be a string, data, or numeric variable. 
- Numeric / Text / Date Value – The field appears depending on the variable you drag-and-drop into the expression builder. For example, if you drag-and-drop a Date value, the field appears as a Date Value and you can enter or select a date to compare. However, you cannot drag-and-drop time variables into the expression builder. 
- The comparison operators available are: Equals to, Not Equals to, Greater than, Less than, and Contains . 
 You can select a maximum of 10 different data set variables from six different data sets to build a listing. You cannot save a listing until you preview the search results. A listing can also have empty values in the search results.
 Preview a Listing 
 While building a listing, if you click Preview: 
- The listing shows entries as per the expression builder conditions without any column filters, and a maximum of 100 records of the total records. The total number of records in the listing appears at the bottom of the page. 
- If the number of records exceeds a preconfigured threshold, a warning message appears. You can then edit the expression builder so that the listing shows records less than the preconfigured threshold.  
- The Patient ID, Site, and Country columns always appear for the listing. 
 Saved Listing 
 Clicking a saved listing shows all the data set variables used the expression builder and the Object Identifiers (OIDs) for each variable. If you hover your cursor over next to the listing name, a tooltip shows the expression used to build the listing. The  Last Updated By  and  Last Updated date and time appear next to the listing name. You cannot edit or delete a saved listing; however, clicking the Show History link at the top the saved listing page shows the list of changes made to the listing. 
 The following simulation shows building a listing with variables from two different data sets. 
 Tip : Click the image to enlarge.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Data Reviewer Knowledge Space provides updated content to support the feature: 
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- Refresh And Get Listings History 
## Special Considerations
- You can use a maximum of six data sets and 10 different variables in the expression for listings. 
- For listings that use complex expressions with OR and AND, you must use parenthesis (()) to combine and separate the conditions. For example, the expression AE.AEPT equals COUGH AND DEM.AGEIC greater_than 50 OR AE.AEPT contains RES returns different results as compared to ( AE.AEPT equals COUGH AND DEM.AGEIC greater_than 50 ) OR AE.AEPT contains RES .

===== PAGE: calculation_method_updated_for_six_system_kris | Calculation Method Updated for Six System KRIs =====
## Calculation Method Updated for Six System KRIs
## Description
 The calculation logic for threshold limits for six system KRIs has changed. See User Impact . 
## Affected Roles
- Risk managers 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 Defining and tracking system KRIs helps your organization target and track unique and specific facets of your study that you want to monitor for risk. 
## User Impact
 The threshold limits for Percent out of window visit and Missing visit percentage system KRIs, calculated based on percentage KRI values in Detect Configuration Manager, appear as follows in the Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) > Key Risk Indicators Dashboard: 
- KRI values between 0 -10% appear Green 
- KRI values between 10 - 20% appear Orange 
- KRI values >= 20% appear Red 
 Similarly, the threshold limits for AE Entry Delay , Visit Entry Delay , System Query Delay and Non-System Query Delay system KRIs, calculated based on the number of days KRI values in Detect Configuration Manager, appear as follows in the Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) > KRI Dashboard: 
- KRI values < = 7 days appear Green 
- KRI values between 7 -14 days appear Yellow 
- KRI values >= 7 days appear Red 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None. 
## Special Considerations
- System KRIs are always available and activated in the Key Risk Indicators table. 
- System KRIs and Custom KRIs with errors display as grayed out with no KRI values in the Key Risk Indicators table.

===== PAGE: case_insensitive_derived_variable_name_validation | Case Insensitive Derived Variable Name Validation =====
## Case Insensitive Derived Variable Name Validation
## Description
 The derived variable creation workflow now expands Name field validation to be case insensitive. Within a given data set, derived variables cannot share a name with any standard data set variable or derived variable.
## Affected Roles
 Any role with the Manage Derived Variables building block.
## Advantages
 The expanded validation ensures that you do not accidentally name derived variables with similar names such as derived_variable and derived_Variable. The change also guards you from accidentally creating new derived variables from a typo. 
## User Impact
 An error message appears when you attempt to save a derived variable that has a name similar to a standard data set variable or derived variable in the Name field.
## Special Considerations
 You can have derived variables with the same name in different data sets. For example, you can have a derived variable named DV1 in the Demographics dataset and a derived variable also named DV1 in the Chemistry data set.

===== PAGE: case_insensitive_expression_builder_text_calculations | Case Insensitive Expression Builder Text Calculations =====
## Case Insensitive Expression Builder Text Calculations
## Description
 While using the expression builder to build derived variables, calculations that compare data set text variables or text fields are now case insensitive. For example,  If (Analyte = ‘Chloride’) can match with "Chloride", "CHLORIDE", and "chloride". 
## Affected Roles
 Any role with the Manage Derived Variables building block.
## Advantages
 The case insensitivity gives you more flexibility in building expressions, allowing to focus on the general logic of your expressions rather than trying to catch every spelling case with OR operators.
## User Impact
 When using the expression builder in the Derived Variables tab, logic that compares text is case insensitive.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: centralized_statistical_monitoring_releases_history | Centralized Statistical Monitoring Releases History =====
## Centralized Statistical Monitoring Releases History
 The following lists all Centralized Statistical Monitoring releases (starting with the initial release to up to the 2022.2.0 feature release) and the features and enhancements introduced in each. All Centralized Statistical Monitoring features and enhancements released after Centralized Statistical Monitoring 2022.2.0 are listed in the Clinical Data Studio Releases History .
 Code Continuity Across Releases
 Note : All Centralized Statistical Monitoring releases are cumulative. That is, each release or software update is built on the prior releases as noted in the release notes. For example,  Software Update 2016.2.1  includes all of the release  2016.2.0  code, which in turn is based on the  release  2016.1.0  code and so on. Any updates between releases or s oftware updates (urgent or otherwise)  are described in the release notes. 
## Centralized Statistical Monitoring 2022.2.0 (Jul 2022)
 This release provided the following new features: 
- View Under- and Overreporting Event Trends at the Site and Country Level 
- View Current and Historical QTL Value Trends 
- Preview and Export Comprehensive QTL Reports 
- Export and Download Customizable KRI Table Snapshots 
- Perform Data Refresh from the KRI Dashboard Page 
 This release also provided the following enhancements: 
- View and Create Issues on the Weekend and Holiday Visits Page 
- QTL-related Technical Enhancements 
- KRI-related UI Updates and Technical Enhancements 
 For information about the defects resolved in this release, see: 
- Centralized Statistical Monitoring 2022.2.0 Resolved Issues List 
## Centralized Statistical Monitoring (formerly Medidata Detect) 2022.1.1 (May 2022)
 This release provided the following enhancements: 
- Filter Scheduled Patient Visits By Visit Name 
- New KRIs and QTLs Knowledge Spaces 
 For information about the defects resolved in this release, see: 
- Centralized Statistical Monitoring (formerly Medidata Detect) 2022.1.1 Resolved Issues List 
## Centralized Statistical Monitoring (formerly Medidata Detect) 2022.1.0 (Apr 2022)
 Note : As of this release, the product name has been changed from "Medidata Detect" to "Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM)". Going forward, Medidata Detect will refer to the overall family of products covering data and risk surveillance tools. See https://learn.mdsol.com/display/DETECTLPprd for details. 
 This release provided the following new features: 
- Improved Navigation and Rebranding in Centralized Statistical Monitoring 2022.1.0 
- Identify Potentially Falsified Visit Data By Viewing Scheduled Patient Visits That Occurred on Non-business Days 
- Uncover Potential Duplicate Patients 
 This release also provided the following enhancements: 
- Error Plots Streamline Navigation to View a Specific Patient's Profile 
- Filter Study Risks By Sites And Countries In The Key Risk Indicators Dashboard 
- Calculation Method Updated for Six System KRIs

===== PAGE: chinese_characters_display_in_patient_profile_reports_and_pdfs | Chinese Characters Display In Patient Profile Reports and PDFs =====
## Chinese Characters Display In Patient Profile Reports and PDFs
## Description
 Chinese characters appear in profiles reports and PDFs you generate for profile designs with elements or variables created using Chinese fonts.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Chinese characters that you enter in Patient Profiles display throughout the user interface and in the profile exports. 
## User Impact
 On the Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) > Patient Profiles > Patient Profile Designs > Elements tab, if you use Chinese characters while working with elements or variables, Chinese characters appear in the profile reports and the PDF exports you generate on the Profiles tab. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Detect Knowledge Space provides updated content to support the enhancement: 
- Review and Export Patient Profiles 
- Add and Manage Elements 
## Special Considerations
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: clean_patient_tracker__aggregated_count_of_outstanding_tasks_by_patient_chart_replaces_patients_in_progress_by_site_and_outstanding_tasks_charts | Clean Patient Tracker: Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient Chart Replaces Patients in Progress By Site and Outstanding Tasks Charts =====
## Clean Patient Tracker: Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient Chart Replaces Patients in Progress By Site and Outstanding Tasks Charts
 Important :
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history. 
- For a summary of all features released, the   released features index .
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Enhancement (Updated Functionality) 
 Functionality or Module 
 | Clean Patient Tracker
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 Clean Patient Tracker no longer includes the following charts:
- Patients in Progress By Site 
- Outstanding Tasks 
 Clean Patient Track now includes the Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient horizontal stacked bar chart, which shows the counts of outstanding tasks per patient. The chart includes outstanding tasks by listings, vendor queries, and page statuses, AI Reconciliation reports, and Rave EDC queries. 
 Benefit to Users 
 | The Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient chart shows all patient-level outstanding tasks enabling you to clean patient data and ensure study data integrity and accuracy.
 Clinical Data Studio's Task Oversight Dashboard includes the Patients in Progress By Site and Outstanding Tasks charts. To avoid duplication across the Clinical Data Studio experience, these charts are removed from Clean Patient Tracker.
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Data managers. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 You can view the Patients in Progress By Site and Outstanding Tasks charts in Clinical Data Studio's Task Oversight Dashboard instead of in Clean Patient Tracker.
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact to other applications.
 Impact on Interface 
 Clean Patient Tracker no longer includes the following charts:
- Patients in Progress By Site 
- Outstanding Tasks 
 Clean Patient Track now includes the Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient horizontal stacked bar chart, which shows the counts of outstanding tasks per patient.
 Tip : Click image to enlarge.
 You can:
- Sort the chart in ascending, descending, and alphabetical order (default is alphanumeric) based on total count per patient. 
- Scroll the chart vertically. 
- Hover your cursor on any patient row in the chart to display a tooltip that shows the following details:
- Patient ID 
- Listings count 
- Vendor queries count 
- page statuses count 
- AI Reconciliation count 
- Rave EDC Queries count 
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 No impact to existing data or settings. 
 User Impact Assessment 
 | High 
 Learning Resource Updates 
 | The following lists any new or added resources that support this change: 
- Updated Article: Track and Clean Patient Data 
 Special Considerations 
 | The metrics that appear in the Aggregated Count of Outstanding Tasks by Patient are based on the configurations set in  Clean Patient Tracker Configuration .
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, see the   Medidata Validation Portal.

## Clean Patient Tracker: Monitor Vendor Queries Data In Clean Patient Tracker
 Important: 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the  released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Enhancement (Updated Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Clean Patient Tracker 
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 Data Surveillance > Clean Patient Tracker now includes vendor queries. You can view vendor query sets with status as Submitted, In Progress or Completed by patient or by site directly from the Clean Patient Tracker page.
 Benefit to Users 
 |      Data managers gain better oversight within the CPT dashboard, allowing them to: 
- Track Progress: Instantly identify pending or unaddressed vendor queries per patient. 
- Validate Resolutions: Spot false positives where vendors claim a resolution, but the listing discrepancies remain. 
- Refine Reporting: Ensure readiness metrics only show accurate data by removing records already reviewed in listings. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Data managers.
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 The count hyperlink for any vendor query set column in Clean Patient Tracker shows the corresponding vendor query set page filtered by site or patient. Similarly, the count hyperlink under any AI Reconciliation report column opens the corresponding report page filtered by Patient ID.
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact to other applications.
 Impact on Interface 
- On the Data Surveillance > Clean Patient Tracker page, if you click any hyperlinked number in a vendor query set column, the corresponding vendor query page opens in a new browser tab. It shows the vendor query filtered by Patient ID. If you click the vendor query count in the in Progress Patients By Site chart, the vendor query page opens in a new browser tab, showing all open vendor query sets for patients at the site. The Patient table in Clean Patient Tracker also includes a hide empty columns button that you can toggle on to hide columns with zero counts. .csv files you download from the Clean Patient Tracker page also include vendor queries. 
- On the Data Surveillance > Listings page, for any approved listing, if you select records and click Submit Vendor Queries , the EDC fields to include and Vendor fields to include lists show fields from your selected EDC source, and field names from the external data source, for example lab data, respectively.  
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 No existing data changes; no configuration or permission updates required.
 User Impact Assessment 
 | High

 | The following lists any new or added resources that support this change: 
- Updated Article: Track and Clean Patient Data.

===== PAGE: clean_patient_tracker__track_up_to_twenty-five_listings_in_clean_patient_tracker | Clean Patient Tracker: Track Up To Twenty-Five Listings In Clean Patient Tracker =====
## Clean Patient Tracker: Track Up To Twenty-Five Listings In Clean Patient Tracker
## What Is New?
 Previously, you could only track 15 listings in Data Surveillance > Clean Patient Tracker. You can now track up to 25 listings.
 Based on how you configure form statuses in Data Surveillance > Configuration > Clean Patient Tracker , the form status column in Clean Patient Tracker shows the following. By default, all form status fields are enabled. If you clear the selected field, they do not appear in Clean Patient Tracker. 
- The total count of forms configured for a patient. 
- The count of each form status, in the following order:
- Incomplete 
- Non Conformant 
- Requires Freeze 
- Requires Lock 
- Requires Review 
- Requires Signature 
 The TSDV Required column in Clean Patient Tracker is now renamed to Requires TSDV/SDV.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact on the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 With the increased number of listings, you can track in Clean Patient Tracker:
- Enables your organization to seamlessly incorporate more listings data into Data Surveillance for tracking and analysis. 
- Ensures Clean Patient Tracker analyses the most recent and correct listings data. 
- Ensures data analysis quality by reducing data entry errors.   
## Where Do I See the Change?
 See What's New?.

===== PAGE: clean_patient_tracker_metrics_and_table_improvements | Data Surveillance: Clean Patient Tracker Metrics and Table Improvements =====
## Data Surveillance: Clean Patient Tracker Metrics and Table Improvements
## What Is New?
 Clean Patient Tracker includes the following improvements:
- The high-level outstanding data cleaning metrics at the top of the Clean Patient Tracker page show in a larger format. 
- The Patient in Progress card shows the percentage of enrolled patients that are reviewed and currently have no outstanding data clean tasks. 
- The Sites to Review card shows the percentage of sites in the study that are reviewed and currently have no outstanding data clean tasks. 
- The Outstanding Tasks cards shows the percentage of all data cleaning tasks across the entire study that are  in progress or unreviewed . 
- You can sort the Patients table by:
- Patient ID 
- Site 
- Country 
- In Progress Patients 
- Enrolled Data 
- Missing Pages 
- You can sort the In Progress Patients By Site - Detailed View > Sites table by:
- Site 
- Country 
- In Progress Patients 
- Missing Pages 
- Open Queries 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
- The high-level outstanding data cleaning metrics at the top of the Clean Patient Tracker page are easier to read. 
- Showing the percentage of patients in progress, percentage of sites to review, and percentage of outstanding tasks:
- Informs you of the volume of data cleaning work across the study that is complete and still needs to be completed. 
- Help you monitor your current data cleaning progress across the study to ensure that tasks are being completed an a healthy, expected pace. 
- Sorting the Patients table and In Progress Patients By Site - Detailed View > Sites table helps you better find, manage, and analyze the data cleaning metrics you need. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In RBQM > Clean Patient Tracker:
- The metrics cards at the top of the Clean Patient Tracker page show in larger text. 
- The Patients in Progress card now shows % Reviewed . 
- The Sites to Review card now shows % Reviewed . 
- The Outstanding Tasks card now shows % Outstanding . 
- In the Patients table, you can click the Patient ID , Site , Country , In Progress Patients , Enrolled Data , Missing Pages column headers to sort the table by header. 
- In the In Progress Patients By Site - Detailed View > Sites table, you can click the  Site , Country , In Progress Patients ,  Missing Pages, Open Queries column headers to sort the table by header.

===== PAGE: clinical_data_studio_homepage | Clinical Data Studio =====
## Clinical Data Studio
 Medidata Clinical Data Studio is a complete data management and quality experience that provides seamless access to integrated data from Medidata and non-Medidata sources. Built with a user-friendly, no/low code environment, Clinical Data Studio uses AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows so that multiple users can act on real-time data in ways that reduce burden, shorten review timelines, increase quality, reduce risk, and improve patient safety.  
 Clinical Data Studio provides the following offerings:
- Medidata Clinical Data Studio is a unified platform solution, which provides the following offerings: 
- Medidata Data Surveillance – Includes the following capability suites:
- Data Surveillance – Provides a drag-and-drop listings builder, automated query generation for Medidata Rave-sourced data, issue management for non-Medidata sourced data, AI-powered data reconciliation, patient profiles, and visualizations. 
- Data Connect – Enables self-service data ingestion and no/low-code data transformation capabilities.  
- Medidata Data Quality Management – Includes all the Data Surveillance capabilities above, plus the following additional capability suites: 
- RBQM – Provides  risk surveillance capabilities supporting a holistic risk-based quality management (RBQM) approach to data quality. 
- Cross Study Metrics – P rovides a   portfolio -level view of relevant data from upstream experiences, such as RBQM and Data Surveillance, across your studies.

===== PAGE: clinical_data_studio_releases_history | Clinical Data Studio Releases History =====
## Clinical Data Studio Releases History
 The following lists all Clinical Data Studio releases (up to and including the current release) and the features or enhancements introduced in each.
 Important: Release Notes Title Update
 As of 23-May-2025 , the Clinical Data Studio release notes document title format is changed from:  Clinical Data Studio <Month> <Year> Release Notes to: Clinical Data Studio <Release Version Number> <Release Type> Release Notes. 
 Important: Clinical Data Studio Release Notes Rebrand and Structure
 Clinical Data Studio comprises three capability suites: 
- Data Surveillance
- RBQM
- Data Connect
 The former Medidata Detect Release Notes previously documented updates to the capabilities that are now provided in Data Surveillance and RBQM capability suites. Therefore, as of Jun-26-2024, the former Medidata Detect Release Notes are now rebranded to the Clinical Data Studio Release Notes. Meanwhile, updates provided in the Data Connect capability suite are documented in a separate release notes document, the Data Connect Release Notes. 
 Important: All Former Detect Module Release Information Previously Consolidated in One Release Notes Document
 Prior to the Medidata Detect November 2022 release, the former Detect modules of Detect Landing Page, Patient Profiles, Data Reviewer, Centralized Statistical Monitoring, and Detect Configuration Manager were each released as separate products with their own sets of release notes. As of Nov-18-2022, all release notes content for all former Detect modules—that is, Detect Landing Page, Patient Data Surveillance, Centralized Statistical Monitoring, Quality Tolerance Limits, Key Risk Indicators, Utilities, and Detect Configuration Manager—became documented under one release notes document per release beginning with the Medidata Detect November 2022 Feature Release Notes. 
 To view released features prior to the Medidata Detect November 2022, see:
- Detect Landing Page Releases History 
- Data Reviewer Releases History 
- Patient Profiles Releases History 
- Centralized Statistical Monitoring Releases History 
- Detect Configuration Manager Releases History 
 Prior to the Medidata Detect March 2023 release, Risk Management was released as a separate product with its own set of release notes. As of Mar-14-2023, all release notes content for Risk Management became documented under the consolidated release notes beginning with the Medidata Detect March 2023 Release Notes.
 To view released features prior to the Medidata Detect March 2023, see:
- Risk Management Released Features 
 Code Continuity Across Releases
 All Clinical Data Studio releases are cumulative.  That is, each release or software update builds on prior releases as noted in the release notes. For example, Software Update 2020.2.1  includes all of the release   2020.2.0 code, which in turn is based on the  release  2020.1.0 code and so on. The release notes describe any updates between releases or s oftware updates (urgent or otherwise)
