===== PAGE: clinical_data_studio_s_data_pipeline | Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline =====
## Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline
 For Clinical Data Studio to properly ingest, analyze, and visualize your study data, study teams must first: 
- For sites in use in any study, ensure a country is added to their Cloud Administration address. 
- Create study forms in Rave Study Builder . 
- Tag the following fields in Rave Tagging :
- Enrolled Date or Randomization Date
 Important : You must only select one variable for the Enrolled Date and one variable for the Randomization Date. Otherwise, Clinical Data Studio cannot appropriately process study data, which will affect certain features abilities to analyze and visualize data.
 Notes:
- For Medidata Rave studies, you must tag the Enrolled Date or Randomization field in Rave Tagging. However, f or studies that consist of  third-party study data that is fully ingested and incorporated into Clinical Data Studio outside of Rave by way of the Data Connect >  Imports  capability, y ou must map the Enrolled Date or Randomization field using Clinical Data Studio's Data Mapping capability . 
- Patient milestone data mappings configured in Clinical Data Studio override patient milestone data mappings configured in Rave. 
- If you configure multiple patient milestone data mappings in Rave, but do not configure patient milestone data mappings in Clinical Data Studio, then Clinical Data Studio will fail to refresh data. 
- Clinical Data Studio does not support Rave Publish-in-Place. To ensure that your Rave data works correctly in Clinical Data Studio, you must create new eCRF versions after updating data types or formats instead of performing a Publish-in-place. For more information, see Publish In Place . 
- AE Start Date 
- AE Serious (AESER)
 Note : The AE Start Date and the AE Serious (AESER) fields must be configured from the same form.
- Define the Target, Start Window and End Window for study visits in Rave Architect to enable RBQM to calculate the following system KRIs:  Percent Missing Visit and Percent Out of Window Visit. 
- Ensure the study environment has a Set Time Zero edit check that coincides with the Day Zero in the Rave folder structure. 
- Ensure that at least one form in the visit structure (typically the visit date form) has a date field marked as the Observation Date of Folder. This helps drive the expected dates in the study.
 Tip : To learn more updating the visit structure, see  Configure Fields (see "Field in Step 5). See Manage Field Properties   for a description about the Observation Date of Folder. 
- Ensure that a Medidata representative enables Rave Coder to show AE/CM terms within Statistical Monitoring for the study. 
 Sites then enter study data:
- Directly in Rave, or 
- Through third-party data vendors; for example, protocol deviations, lab data, or any data not uploaded through Rave. You can then import that external data using Data Connect's Imports capability  or through Ingestor .
 Note : New studies will import external, third-party data using Imports. However, legacy studies that have previously ingested data through Ingestor can continue to import data through Ingestor.
 Important : Clinical Data Studio does not support study data containing multiple patients with the same Patient ID. This is true even if the Patient IDs come from different sites. If Clinical Data Studio does consume data with duplicate Patient IDs, then you may experience inconsistent results in CDS's data analyses and outputs.
 Medidata's platform data workflow enriches and transforms all tagged study data for use and analysis in Clinical Data Studio. 
 Note : Study teams should exclude unblinded data in the initial study enablement request.
## Data Refresh Frequency
 In Data Surveillance and RBQM, s tudy data automatically refreshes four times daily at approximately 9:00am (EST), 3:00pm (EST), 9:00pm (EST) and 3:00am (EST), and the data presented within the user interface is current as of 11:00 pm (EST) the previous day, 5:00 am (EST) the same day, 11:00 am (EST) the same day, 5:00 pm (EST) the same day, respectively. Each study data refresh produces a data snapshot. Updated data from Rave, and activated datasets from Data Connect are available in 6 to 12 hours within Data Surveillance and RBQM.  
 Note : Queries submitted from Listings and AI Reconciliation to Veeva EDC takes approximately 3 hours to reflect on Clinical Data Studio. 
 The following table outlines how data refreshes and appears in various Clinical Data Studio capabilities.

## How Data Refresh Affects Data Flow - An Example
 In addition, you can:
- Refresh data listings to produce results based on the latest study data . 
- Refresh AI Data Reconciliation to produce reports based on the latest study data. 
- Refresh published patient profile designs to show and reflect data based on the latest study data 
- Refresh the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard to visualize and report on the latest study data . 
- Trigger Clean Patient Tracker to recalculate outstanding records based on the latest study data . 
 Note : You can refresh data in AI Reconciliation and RECIST 1.1 up to two times a day, based on Rave refresh schedules.
 In RBQM after the data refresh, you can: 
- View published audit data sets in the Data Surveillance > Data Sets capability, or 
- Use p ublished audit data sets to create data listings and build custom KRIs. 
 In addition, the KRI Dashboard, QTL Dashboard, and Statistical Monitoring capabilities enable you to refresh the modules to render analyses based on RBQM's most recently ingested study data. You can schedule data refreshes to occur and on a preset frequency or manually trigger data refreshes ad-hoc. See: 
- Schedule or trigger KRI Dashboard to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
- Schedule or trigger QTL Dashboard to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
- Schedule or trigger Statistical Monitoring to refresh and output the latest study data analysis . 
 Important: Data Quality Preparedness
 Prior to performing a study migration, confirm that any changes made will or will not affect any Clinical Data Studio configurations. To learn more, see   Review Pre-Migration Plans . If you experience issues when migrating studies or ingesting datasets,   we recommend that you confirm that the datasets have not been affected in Clinical Data Studio. You can review and update any   activated datasets ,   and, if necessary, reconfigure any datasets   imported from external sources .

## Interpolated Variables Behavior in Data Surveillance and RBQM
 In Data Surveillance and RBQM, variables with the suffix_TXT, _INT, _DTC indicate enriched fields from Data Connect.
 Note : Variables in Data Surveillance and RBQM are labelled "fields" in Data Connect. For consistency, this section will use "fields" giong forward.
 Source fields refer to the original source of a data point, while enriched fields add extra information or context to the source data. Clinical Data Studio shows enriched fields to provide more detail about the about source fields, or to add derived information that is not directly present in the original source. If the source dataset fields include unknown values, additional interpolated (enriched) fields with the suffixes _INT, _TXT, etc are added to the source dataset . For example, if the source date is missing the day, the enriched _INT field (integer) interpolates the 1st day of the month, and the _DTC field (datetime) drops the unknown value. The values in the enriched fields differ when dates have unknown (UN or  UNK ) values. If the source field uses dictionary terms, the enriched _TXT field shows the coded terms. For example, AESer and AESer_TXT. 
- Patient Profiles – If you use _TXT values, you see end user strings rather dictionary coded values, that is, No/Yes rather than 0/1 in your patient profile design. If you use a dataset with datetime operations, then you should use the date field and its enrichments, for example: _INT,  DT , _DTC—from the source Rave dataset to ensure data accuracy in the patient profiles. 
- Listings and Data Sets – Interpolated fields such as _INT and _DTC appear as-is in Data Connect. But these fields do not appear for selection in the Datasets pane in Listings as they show as the Rave source field, and are consumed implicitly within the date field. 
- Interpolated fields in derived datasets and derived fields – For Rave-enabled listings containing derived datasets built in Data Connect , you can submit queries only for derived datasets where source fields originate from a Rave dataset. That is, the Submit Query button remains disabled if  the listings contains derived datasets where the source fields does not come from a Rave dataset.  
 Similarly, for Rave-enabled listings containing derived fields, you can submit queries for derived fields  where source fields originate from a Rave dataset.  Otherwise, we recommend you select the form field from the Rave form in the Add Column option, and edit the listing.

===== PAGE: close_date_no_longer_required_in_review_reports | Close Date No Longer Required In Review Reports =====
## Close Date No Longer Required In Review Reports
## Description
 The Close Date field in Review Reports on the Detect Landing Page is no longer mandatory.   
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 You can still create a review report even if you are not sure about the end date for the review cycle.
## User Impact
 You can save a new on the Medidata Detect > Configuration and Reporting > Review Reports page, even if you leave the Close Date field empty.
## Knowledge Hub Updates
 The Detect Knowledge Hub provides new and updated content to support this enhancement: 
- Review Reports 
## Special Considerations
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: column_header_tooltip_in_key_risk_indicators_table_shows_kri_details | Column Header Tooltip in Key Risk Indicators Table Shows KRI Details =====
## Column Header Tooltip in Key Risk Indicators Table Shows KRI Details
## Description
 The KRIs Dashboard, available from the Detect Landing Page, now shows a tooltip when you hover your cursor over column headers in the Key Risk Indicators table on the Key Risk Indicators page.   
## Affected Roles
- Risk managers 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 You can search and view specific data and metrics you want to analyze and report by scanning the tooltip in the column headers of the KRI table. 
## User Impact
 On the Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) module > Key Risk Indicators Dashboard > Key Risk Indicators page, you can hover your cursor over any column header in the Key Risk Indicators table to view the: 
- KRI Label - KRI name and description as defined in Detect Configuration Manager 
- KRI Type - Custom or System KRI 
- KRI calculation method  - KRI calculation that uses a statistical or a user set threshold in Detect Configuration Manager. For KRIs calculated using user-set threshold limits, color-coded threshold values and ranges also appear in the tooltip.  
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None. 
## Special Considerations
 The user set, color-coded threshold values and ranges that appear in column header tooltips in the Key Risk Indicators table, depend on whether one or both user set threshold limits exist in Centralized Statistical Monitoring (formerly Medidata Detect). 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

## Concatenate Derived Variable Expanded to Multiple Concatenation
## Description
 You can concatenate multiple text data set variables with the Concatenate derived variables workflow. Additionally, the text entered into the Prefix and Suffix fields now each appear once in the derived variable.

 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables permission.

 You can create more robust text derived variables to use in MEDS Data Viewer and other applications.
## User Impact
 The concatenation workflow now accepts multiple text data set variables. When you add variables into the available fields, another row of fields appear.
 Additionally, the text entered in the Prefix field only appears once at the beginning of the derived variable. Likewise, the text entered in the Suffix field only appears once at the end of the derived variable.

 None.

===== PAGE: conditional_options_in_tables_restored | Conditional Options In Tables Restored =====
## Conditional Options In Tables Restored
## Description
 In Medidata Patient Profiles 2021.1.0, the conditional options feature is reinstated for tables. This applies to wide tables, transposed tables, patient information tables, and event tables. 
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Setting conditions to display data allows Patient Profile reviewers to easily identify patient data that matches specific criteria (for example, pregnant patients) in a study. 
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab > when you are working on an element > Table Options > Conditional Options: 
 When you set up an expression to only display the element based on specific criteria, such as the value of a data variable in the data set: 
- If the patient data meets the criteria, the table and graph (as appropriate) display. 
- If the patient data does not meet the criteria, the table and graph (as appropriate) do not display.
- If you configure the element to display both the table and graph, and also select Table Options > General Options >  Hide "No Data" Elements : 
- The graph and table do not display when patient data does not meet the criteria. 
- The graph and the table display when patient data meets the criteria. 
- If you configure the element to display only the graph, then select Table Options > General Options >  Hide "No Data" Elements :  
- The graph does not display when patient data does not meet the criteria. 
- The graph displays when patient data meets the criteria.  
- If you configure the element to display only the table, then select Table Options > General Options >  Hide "No Data" Elements :  
- The table does not display when patient data does not meet the criteria. 
- The graph displays when patient data meets the criteria.  
 When you set up an expression using a variable used in configuring a table, as the display criteria for the element: 
- If the patient data meets the criteria, the element displays. 
- If the patient data does not meet the criteria, the element does not display. 
 When you set up an expression using a variable not used in configuring a table, as the display criteria for the element: 
- If the patient data meets the criteria, the element displays. 
- If the patient data does not meet the criteria, the element does not display. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

 Tip: Click the image to enlarge.
 Number 
 Description

 You must also select the dataset, the missing page count field, or the expected page count, and entered page count fields.

 | If you click the Download Report button from the top right corner of the page, the Clean Patient Tracker Configuration page downloads as a PDF. The report includes the form status calculations fields, and the missing pages source fields.

- MRPP to SRPP 
- MRPP to MRPP 
 If you view or copy an existing merge type derived variable, the Type of Merge field appears disabled. You can edit only the derived variable label.

===== PAGE: configuration_and_reporting__merge_multiple_datasets_with_common_variables_into_one_dataset | Configuration and Reporting: Merge Multiple Datasets with Common Variables into One Dataset =====
## Configuration and Reporting: Merge Multiple Datasets with Common Variables into One Dataset
## What Is New?
 Study data can sometimes contain datasets that share numerous common variables. For example: 
- Rave EDC may include variations of the same type of eCRF, or 
- Study data may come from multiple sources such as a Rave EDC vitals dataset and an external vitals dataset, or 
- Screening data and study collection data may have similar data points. 
 You can now merge datasets with common variables into one dataset called a stacked dataset. Stacked datasets include all variables from all the source datasets, even variables without any common matches across the source datasets. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers
## Workflow Process
 On the Configuration and Reporting > Stacked Datasets page, you can select the datasets you want to use to create stacked datasets. You can use s tacked datasets in: 
- Data Reviewer > Data Sets page 
- Data Reviewer > Data Listings page 
- Data Reviewer > Visualizations page 
- Patient Profiles > Design page 
- Configuration and Reporting > Detect Mapping 
- Configuration and Reporting > QTL Configuration 
- Configuration and Reporting > KRI Configuration 
- Configuration and Reporting > Derived Variables 
- Configuration and Reporting > Oncology Mapping 
## Other Applications
 See the Workflow Process section.
## How Do I Benefit?
 In instances where multiple datasets have numerous shared variables, merging the datasets into one stacked dataset: 
- Simplifies the organization of your study data. 
- Enables you to review your study data, create data listings, build patient profiles, and create derived variables faster and easier by streamlining the datasets you must access, review, and work with. 
- Simplifies the configuration process when mapping the data sets and variables that Detect uses to consume and produce the statistical analysis and visual output for:
- Data anomaly detection  and  trends . 
- Event incidence and under-over reporting events . 
- Potential duplication patients . 
- Rounding and propagating vital sign records . 
- AI Data Reconciliation reports . 
- Data visualizations . 
- RECIST 1.1 analytics . 
- Optimizes the statistical analysis and visual outputs that Detect produces on your study data to be as clean and accurate as possible. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Configuration and Reporting module now includes the Stacked Datasets tab in the left-hand navigation, which you can click to access the Stacked Datasets page. The Stacked Datasets page includes the functionality to allow you to create, view, and manage the stacked datasets in your study. 
 On the Data Reviewer > Data Sets page, Data Listings page, and Visualizations page, the list of available datasets appends stacked data set names with the green DERIVED icon. Note that Data Reviewer appends derived variable names with a blue DERIVED icon.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Stacked Datasets 
## What Else Should I Know?
 When creating stacked datasets, there must be at least one common variable OID that exists across all source datasets that you want to create a stacked dataset from.
 You can use up to 10 datasets to create a merged dataset.
 You require the View Detect CSM Configuration building block to access the Stacked Datasets page. You require the Manage Detect CSM Configuration building block to create stacked datasets. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: configure_all_csm-related_data_mappings_on_the_csm_configuration_page | Configure All CSM-related Data Mappings on the CSM Configuration Page =====
## Configure All CSM-related Data Mappings on the CSM Configuration Page
## Description
 In previous Detect Configuration Manager releases, the left-hand menu contained a CSM Configuration tab. When you clicked the CSM Configuration tab, the left-hand menu would expand to show two subtabs: Event Analysis Configuration and Duplicate Patient Configuration. Clicking each tab directed you to the Event Analysis Configuration page and Duplicate Patient Configuration page, respectively.
 Now clicking the CSM Configuration tab navigates you to the CSM Configuration page. The CSM Configuration page contains four embedded tabs: Error Plots, Event Analysis, Potential Duplicate Patients, and Rounding and Propagation. You can click each tab to access the workspace containing the configuration functionality for each respective CSM analysis tool.
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 The new CSM Configuration page simplifies navigation and usability by logically consolidating all CSM-related configuration functionality in one clear, centralized workspace.

===== PAGE: configure_custom_kri_thresholds | Configure Custom KRI Thresholds =====
## Configure Custom KRI Thresholds
## Description
 On the Key Risk Indicators page, you can configure user-defined, custom KRI thresholds to identify KRI outliers. 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Administrators. 
## Advantages
 For Custom Numeric and Custom Percentage KRIs, you can set your own threshold to determine moderate risk and high risk categories and study data issues that meet your data monitoring requirements. 
## User Impact
 On the Medidata Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) module > KRI Configuration > Key Risk Indicators page, the Custom Numeric KRI dialog box and the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box now include the following new fields: 
-  Threshold Type – Select KRI threshold as User Defined or System Defined. Selecting User Defined displays the following fields:   
- Moderate Risk Threshold – Enter the value that represents the lowest risk limit for the KRI. 
- The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100. 
- The Custom Numeric KRI value must be a positive number less than the High Risk Threshold value. 
- High Risk Threshold – Optional. Enter a value that represents the highest risk limit for the KRI.   
- The Custom Percentage KRI value must be between 1 and 100. 
- The Custom Numeric KRI value must be a positive number more than the Moderate Risk Threshold value. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None. 
 Special Considerations

- If you update an existing user defined KRI, new changes will affect all calculations and analytics that consume the user defined KRI.  
- If activated, the updated custom KRI details appear in Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) (formerly Medidata Detect) after the Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) (formerly Medidata Detect) next data refresh. 
- If you hover your cursor over a Percentage KRI in the Type column of the KRI table, a tooltip indicates if the KRI's threshold calculation is User Defined or System Defined.

===== PAGE: configure_display_conditions_for_elements_patient_profiles | Configure Display Conditions for Elements Patient Profiles =====
## Configure Display Conditions for Elements Patient Profiles
## Description
 You can configure tables and timelines to display on a conditional basis. We provide this functionality because sometimes there are situations where an element is created to display data that may not apply to all subjects. For example, if an element is created to display pregnancy status data points, then you would want the element to only display data that applies to female subjects. 
 Therefore, you can create conditions—such as “dem.gender=Female”—so that Medidata Patient Profiles knows to hide this particular element in reports for male subjects. As a result, taking the aforementioned example, the report will not display an empty timeline for male subjects. This yields a cleaner, more aesthetic looking report. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 When working with tables or timelines on the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- Configure element display conditions; 
- Remove element display conditions. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: configure_display_conditions_for_table_rows_patient_profiles | Configure Display Conditions for Table Rows Patient Profiles =====
## Configure Display Conditions for Table Rows Patient Profiles
## Description
 When designing profiles, there may be times when you need to display the same data in two tables, but you need to apply opposing conditions to the rows containing that data. For example, if you want to show significant adverse events (AE) in one table and non-significant adverse events in another table. In such case, you can build two tables with the same exact AE data set variables. On the first table you can build a condition with ae.SAE=Yes. On the second table, you can have the condition of ae.SAE=No.
 Another example of applying row display conditions is if you know an adverse event table will have empty records, but it is unnecessary to display "No Data." You can create a condition where:
 "ae.AE Term = is not missing AND ad.AE Start Date = is not missing" . 
 As a result, empty rows do not display in the report.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 When working with wide tables or transposed tables on the Design page > Elements tab, you can:
- Configure transposed table row display conditions; 
- Remove transposed table row display conditions. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: configure_potential_duplicate_patient_data_mappings | Configure Potential Duplicate Patient Data Mappings =====
## Configure Potential Duplicate Patient Data Mappings
## Description
 Duplicate patients are patients who enroll in clinical trials for financial gain or for extra dosages of medication. Duplicate patients threaten both participant safety and the integrity of research findings. Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) (formerly Medidata Detect) uncovers potential duplicate patients by analyzing six demographics: date of birth, gender, height, weight, race, ethnicity. Additionally, CSM analyzes the physical distance within 100 miles of site location of each patient to find patients that look very similar. 
 CSM Configuration Manager allows you to map the six demographic parameters: date of birth, gender, height, weight, race, and ethnicity to the corresponding reference variables from data sets in your study environment and save the configuration, which CSM's data science microservice algorithms consume. Based on the analytics, CSM automatically generates the configuration data analysis and renders the visualization output as a global heat and site level map. 
## Affected Roles
- CSM Configuration Manager Admin. 
- CSM users. 
## Advantages
 Identifying and removing potential duplicate patients from the study. 
## User Impact
 Tip: Click image to enlarge. 
 | 1 
 | The Medidata Detect > Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) > CSM Configuration application has a new CSM Configuration tab. 
 | 2 
 | Duplicate Patient Configuration subtab under the CSM Configuration tab.  
 | 3 
 | Duplicate Patient Configuration page, where you can first select data sets from the Data Set column, then variables from the Mapped Variable column to map to each Reference demographic: Date of Birth, Weight, Height, Gender, Race, and Ethnicity. You can save or update the configuration only after mapping each reference variable.  
- The Mapped Variable column remains disabled until you select a data set in the Data Set column. You can select variables, including derived variables, from any data set to map to reference variables. 
- The Mapped Variable for weight and height references become enabled after you select a data set and the corresponding weight and height units. 
 Knowledge Space Updates 
 None. 
 Special Considerations 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: configure_secondary_day_0_date_for_studies_without_a_primary_day_0_date | Configure Secondary Day 0 Date For Studies Without a Primary Day 0 Date =====
## Configure Secondary Day 0 Date For Studies Without a Primary Day 0 Date
## Description
 Patient profile designers can now define a primary day zero date and a secondary day zero date. Therefore, if a patient does not reach the primary day zero date, then CSA's analytics references the secondary day zero date, if configured. All date-related analyses are then accounted for based on the patient's secondary day zero date.
## Affected Roles
- Patient profile designers 
## Advantages
 In previous Patient Profiles Cloud releases, patient profile designers could only configure a single day zero date when defining a design's date settings. Consequently, if a patient did not reach the day zero date, then CSA's analytics would not account for and analyze date-related data from that patient's profile. Such data may include visit dates, min AE start, max CM end, slope, intercept, and so on.
 Now you can configure a primary day zero date and a secondary day zero date. So even if a patient does not reach the primary day zero date, CSA's analytics still accounts for and analyzes date-related patient profile data for patients based on the secondary day zero date, if configured.
 For example, in previous releases, you may have designed a study so that Visit 1 was set as your study's day zero date. Your study may also have had a Screening Visit that occurred before Visit 1. Therefore, a patient may have attended the Screening Visit and not Visit 1. In which case, CSA's analytics would not have accounted for and analyzed date-related data in that patient's profile because the patient did not reach the day zero date (Visit 1).
 Now you can configure Visit 1 as your primary day zero date and the Screening Visit as the secondary day zero date. So if a patient does not reach Visit 1 but participated in the Screening Visit, that patient's date-related profile data still gets accounted for and analyzed by CSA's analytics.
## User Impact
- The Settings page > Design Options tab now includes a Primary Day Zero Date section and a Secondary Day Zero Date section. 
- If you configure a secondary day zero date, the secondary day zero date and its corresponding visit name display on the design report on the Reports page. 
## Special Considerations
- You still must configure a primary day zero date for your study design. However, configuring a secondary day zero date is not required. 
- You cannot configure a secondary date zero date without first configuring a primary day zero date.

## Description
 You can now configure within Detect Configuration Manager the data sets and variables that Detect uses to consume and produce the statistical analysis and visual output for event incidence and under-over reporting events.
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Event analysis configuration:
- Simplifies CSM configuration by requiring only the key variables for Detect to perform its study data analysis.  
- Optimizes CSM configuration by consolidating the configuration and mapping tasks in one centralized location. 
 This helps ensure Detect analyzes the correct terms and saves hours of configuration time.

- Concomitant Medication Terms 
- Medical History Terms 
- Medical History Ongoing

## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Detect Configuration Manager Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
- Map Event Analysis Data 
## Special Considerations
 Within the event analysis configuration, we strongly recommend that you pick your preferred terms for adverse event, concomitant medications, and medical history terms. This enables Detect to provide the most accurate event incidence and under-over reporting events analysis. 
 Also, the data variable values captured for the Medical History Ongoing variable must conform to one of the following data formats: 
- Y/N 
- Yes/No 
- T/F 
- True/False 
- on/not(etc) 
- 1/0 
- Ongoing/Not Ongoing

===== PAGE: configure_the_vital_sign_data_used_for_csm_s_rounding_and_propagation_analysis | Configure the Vital Sign Data Used for CSM's Rounding and Propagation Analysis =====
## Configure the Vital Sign Data Used for CSM's Rounding and Propagation Analysis
## Description
 You can configure the vital sign data sets and collection date variables that Detect consumes to analyze and visually output the sites that may be rounding and propagating vital sign records. To learn more about rounding and propagation, see Rounding and Propagation Analysis .
 You can also optionally further specify and configure the procedure name, procedure value, and category that Detect analyzes.
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Rounding and Propagation Configuration provides a simple, centralized workspace where you can quickly configure the specific vital sign data that you want Detect to analyze.
## User Impact

You can use this table to select enter or select the following information, which Detect uses to run its vital sign rounding and propagation analysis on:
- Reference Name – A custom name to help you easily identify the data set configured for analysis. Detect does not include the Reference Name in its analysis. 
- Data Set – The vital sign data set that you want Detect to use to run its rounding and propagation analysis on. 
- Collection Date – The date variable for the date in which the vital sign collection took place that you want Detect to run its rounding and propagation analysis on. 
- Procedure Name – Optional . The name of the test done that collected the vital sign records. Procedure Name is only selectable when you toggle the Pivot button on. 
- Procedure Value – Optional . The values collected in the procedure name's fields. Procedure Value is only selectable when you toggle the Pivot button on. 
- Category – Optional . A subset of the vital sign being collected, such as respiratory vital signs, body vital signs, and so on. Category  is only selectable when you toggle the Pivot button on. 
 You can also choose to pivot the data that Detect analyzes. Toggling the Pivot button on enables Detect to consume and analyze and Procedure Name, Procedure Value, or Category selections you optionally choose.
 You can click Add Vital to configuration additional vital sign data that you want Detect to analyze.

- Map Vital Sign Data for Rounding and Propagation Analysis

===== PAGE: corrected_text_field_rendering_in_expression_builder | Corrected Text Field Rendering in Expression Builder =====
## Corrected Text Field Rendering in Expression Builder
## Description
 While building conditional expressions for derived variables using the IF-THEN-ELSE block, if you compare a text field in the IF block, and if the text field has the same name as the source data set variable, then the THEN and ELSE blocks use the value of the entered text from the text field instead of the source variable. For example, you select source variable "ASIAN" in the IF block and enter uppercase “ASIAN” in the THEN and ELSE blocks, then the entered text – "ASIAN" – appears instead of the values of the "ASIAN" data set variable.  
## Affected Roles
 All roles with Manage Derived Variables permission. 
## Advantages
 With the correct text field names rendered for conditional expressions, you can have more precision over the derived variables you create in MEDS Data Viewer.  
## User Impact
 See Description. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: create_rave_queries_directly_from_listings | Create Rave Queries Directly from Listings =====
## Create Rave Queries Directly from Listings
## Description
 You can create Rave queries directly from listings in Data Reviewer. You can select and submit Rave queries for all or some of the records in listings.
## Affected Roles
 All Detect users with access to Rave and Data Reviewer.
## Advantages
 You can save time by creating and posting queries in Rave directly from Data Reviewer. For example, you can now create multiple queries to submit to Rave manually in under a minute, compared to five to seven minutes previously. Similarly, you can review data and generate queries per review cycle in less than one day per person compared to one to two weeks by multiple reviewers.
## User Impact
 On the Data Reviewer > Listings tab, you can build listings.

===== PAGE: csm__potential_duplicate_patients_analysis_accounts_for_sites_without_recognizable_addresses | CSM: Potential Duplicate Patients Analysis Accounts for Sites Without Recognizable Addresses =====
## CSM: Potential Duplicate Patients Analysis Accounts for Sites Without Recognizable Addresses
## What Is New?
 In previous releases, Potential Duplicate Patients could not run its analysis on sites whose addresses were not recognized by the address search plugin that Medidata uses . Therefore, those sites and associated patients were not accounted for in the overall potential duplicate patient analysis. Now, Potential Duplicate Patients runs its analysis sites without recognizable site addresses at the country level. In addition, t he Sites card reports the number of sites with and without recognizable site addresses. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Central monitors
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 The Patient Duplicate Patients analysis is now more comprehensive and truly reflective of the patient population.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring > Data Veracity > Potential Duplicate Patients.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- Investigate and Identify Potential Duplicate Patients In Your Study 
## What Else Should I Know?
 On the Summary - Sites table, if you click a site without an address, the Potential Duplicate Patients heatmap remains on the Global view and does not zoom to the Site view.

===== PAGE: csm__rounding_and_propagation_heatmap_improvements | CSM: Rounding and Propagation Heatmap Improvements =====
## CSM: Rounding and Propagation Heatmap Improvements
## What Is New?
 On the Rounding and Propagation > Sites with Rounding table, when you hover your cursor on a table cell, a dialog shows:
- Site – The site ID. 
- Patient Counted – The number of patients at the site. 
- Patients Rounded – The number of patients at the site with at least three rounded records. 
- Rounded Records Counted – The number of rounded records at the site. 
- Total Records – The total number of records for the vital sign at the site. 
 In addition, you can click a table cell to view in a separate dialog a list of patients with recorded events at the site and rounded record details. In the dialog, you can also click a patient ID to view that patient in Patient Profiles.
 Similarly, on the Sites with Propagation table, when you hover your cursor on a table cell, a dialog shows:
- Site – The site ID. 
- Patient Counted – The number of patients at the site. 
- Patients Propagated – The number of patients at the site with at least three propagated records. 
- Propagated Records Counted – The number of propagated records at the site. 
- Total Records – The total number of records for the vital sign at the site. 
 Likewise, you can click a table cell to view in a separate dialog a list of patients with recorded events at the site and propagated record details. In the dialog, you can click a patient ID to view that patient in Patient Profiles.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Central monitors
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 In the dialog that shows the list of patients with recorded events, you can click a patient ID to access and view that patient in Patient Profiles.
## How Do I Benefit?
 The updated heatmap pop-ups are cleaner and easier to read and contain more pertinent information. The ability to view individual patients with recorded events and access those patients' profiles enables you to more efficiently investigate patient data.

 Centralized Statistical Monitoring > Data Veracity > Rounding and Propagation, on the Sites with Rounding and Sites with Propagation heatmaps.

===== PAGE: custom_graphs__rebranded_visualizations_includes_on-demand_and_scheduled_data_refreshes | Custom Graphs: Rebranded Visualizations Includes On-Demand And Scheduled Data Refreshes =====
## Custom Graphs: Rebranded Visualizations Includes On-Demand And Scheduled Data Refreshes
 Important :
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the   released features index .   
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality) 
 Functionality or Module 
 | Custom Graphs 
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 The Data Surveillance > Visualizations page is renamed to Custom Graphs . This rebranding holds true throughout Clinical Data Studio, including the Templates Library and downloaded reports. Custom Graphs also includes a refresh option where you can start on-demand or scheduled data refreshes. You can further manage scheduled refreshes on the Unified Scheduler page.
 Benefit to Users 
 | Data managers can obtain the latest study data using on-demand and scheduled refreshes, and conduct study data review and reconciliation using the most recent data. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Data managers and study team members must possess both building blocks; capability-specific, and Unified Scheduler related, to view and manage data refresh schedules . For On-demand refreshes, users need the Refresh Custom Graphs building block. 
 Data Surveillance Capability 
 Building Block Required 
 User Action pertaining to refreshes 
 | Unified Scheduler 
 | View Data Refresh Scheduler 
 | View  
 | Manage Data Refresh Scheduler 
 | Create or Edit 
 | Scheduled Refresh from Custom Graphs
(previously known as Visualizations) 
 | View Data Refresh Scheduler AND
View or Manage Data Reviewer 
 | View 
 | Manage Data Refresh Scheduler AND 
 Refresh Custom Graphs AND
View or Manage Data Reviewer
 | Create or Edit 
 | On Demand Refresh from Custom Graphs 
 | Refresh Custom Graphs AND  View or Manage Data Reviewer.  
 | View or Start Refresh 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
- Scheduled refreshes for custom graphs on the Unified Scheduler page operate on daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, bimonthly, and quarterly cadences . 
- Custom Graphs allow up to four successful refreshes per day per custom graph . 
- Conflict prevention rules block multiple on-demand refreshes for the same custom graph on the same snapshot, and block on-demand refreshes while scheduled refreshes run . That is, a record selected for a scheduled refresh is not available for on-demand refresh selection. 
- You can export current refresh configurations into a downloadable PDF report through the Notification Center . 
 Impact to Applications 
- Unified Scheduler updates data for Custom Graphs through scheduled refreshes. 
 Impact on Interface 
 In Data Surveillance, you can find the following Custom Graphs updates.
 Number 
 Description 
 | 1 
 | Left-Hand menu – In the Data Surveillance tab, Visualizations no longer appears in the left hand-menu. It is renamed to Custom Graphs.  
 | 2 
 | Page Heading – If you click Custom Graphs in the left-hand menu, the Custom Graphs page appears which lists all the custom graphs (previously known as visualizations) in the study. The Last refreshed date and time details no longer appear under the Custom Graphs summary page heading.
 | 3 
 | Refresh – If you click the Refresh button on the top right corner of the Custom Graphs, you can select a maximum of 15 custom graphs for an on-demand refresh. You can refresh any custom graph up to a maximum of 4 times per day. The On-demand refresh page does not show custom graphs that currently have a refresh in progress, or are part of a scheduled refresh ,or has been recently refreshed and has the most updated data snapshot.
 Note : Custom graphs selected for a scheduled refresh are not available for on-demand refresh.
 | 4 
 | Scheduled Refreshes – If you click  , More icon, next to the Refresh button on the top right corner of the page, and then click View Schedule , the Unified Scheduler page shows all the custom graphs refresh schedules. For more information, see  Data Surveillance Configuration: Schedule Data Refreshes Using Unified Scheduler . 
 Note : On the Data Surveillance > Custom Graphs page, if you select any custom graph, and then click   More icon, and then click Refresh History , the page shows both on-demand and scheduled refreshes. The refresh table shows the following fields:
- Refresh Date 
- Refresh Type 
- Snapshot Date 
- Refreshed By 
 If a custom graph has not been refreshed, there may not be details ion the Refresh History page. In such instances, the Please refresh graph data to generate a snapshot message appears.
 | 5 
 | Included in Scheduled Refreshes – The Custom Graphs page includes a new Included in Scheduled Refreshes column, which shows a tick mark if the custom graph is part of a scheduled refresh. 
 The Details page displays the current refresh status of any custom graph. It shows  In Progress while the custom graph refreshes, Refresh Successful when the refresh completes, and Refresh Failed if the refresh fails 
 For any custom graph, the last refreshed date and time in the user's local timezone appear under the page title.
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings

- For custom graphs, records selected for a scheduled data refresh do not appear for selection in on-demand refreshes. The reverse is also true.

===== PAGE: customize_study_specific_risk_assessment_using_risk_assessment_configurations | Customize Study Specific Risk Assessment Using Risk Assessment Configurations =====
## Customize Study Specific Risk Assessment Using Risk Assessment Configurations
 What Is New? 
 RBQM > Configurations includes a new Risk Assessment Configurations page where you can set up fields for risk assessment specific to your study. You can now use a five-point scale, in addition to the three-point scale for assessing the risk factors for your study. The risk assessment details you configure appear on the Assessment Details page, where you can edit or customize your current risk assessment.  
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Risk managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Risk managers can configure specific details relevant to the study risk, monitor values associated with the risk throughout the study using the risk evaluation scale adopted, and determine the data points required to complete the risk assessment and mitigation.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The left hand panel in the RBQM > Configuration > Risks tab, includes a new Risk Assessment Configuration page. The page includes the following fields:
- Risk Study Scale
- Risk scoring scale 
- 3 point scale (default) 
- 5 point scale 
- Risk Expected Fields
- Risk Details
- Score 
- Response 
- Owner 
- Category 
- Status 
- Description 
- Source 
- Include in risk plan report 
- Risk Actions
- Action Required 
- Action Taken 
- Closed Date 
 The 5 point risk scoring scale includes the following values:
- Probability
- 1 – Low 
- 2 – Medium 
- 3 – High 
- Impact 
- Detectability
- 1 – High 
- 3 – Medium 
- 5 – Low 
 Color coding for the 5 pointer scale is as follows:
- Green – Total risk score range is between 1 and 5. 
- Yellow –Total risk score range is between 5 and 25. 
- Red – Total risk score range is between 25 and 125. 
 If the risk assessment pointer scale changes from 3 to 5 or 5 to 3 in the duration of the study, risk scoring for existing risk updates accordingly. By default, the 3 point risk scoring scale appears selected. 
 If you select the from the above fields and click Save Changes , the updates and fields save to the RBQM > Risk Assessment > Details > Assessment Details page. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the feature:
- Risk Assessment Configuration 
## What Else Should I Know?
 You must have the Risk Assessment Configuration building block assigned to your role to configure risk assessment.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: customize_the_default_color_of_variable_data_points_in_timelines | Customize the Default Color of Variable Data Points in Timelines =====
## Customize the Default Color of Variable Data Points in Timelines
## Description
 In previous releases, you could configure the color in which you wanted specific variable data points to display in timelines. However, you could not customize a default color for variable data points. Now you can configure a default color for non-customized variable data points in timelines.
 You can also preview the default color for each variable data point in the timeline by selecting a timeline on the Design page > Elements tab.
## Affected Roles
- Patient Profiles Designers 
## Advantages
 Configuring non-customized variable data points to display in a default color of your choosing better enables you to view and scan data in your timelines.
 Previewing the default color for each variable data point in the timeline helps you better understand how to read timelines when viewing patients' profiles.
## User Impact
 When working with wide tables on the Design page > Elements tab, the Table Options tab > Timeline Options section now includes the Point Color selector.
 You must select the Event Table check box to enable the Point Color selector. If you click the color thumbnail to the right of the Point Color label, a color palette displays, and you can select your custom point color.
 Then when you navigate to the Design page > Profiles tab to view patient profiles, any variable data points that are not customized to display in a particular color display in the selected default point color.
 Furthermore, when you navigate to a timeline on the Design page > Elements tab, each variable contains a Display column. The Display column shows you the default point color in which that variable's data points display in the timeline.
## Special Considerations
- The Point Color option only applies to wide tables. 
- You cannot change a variable's default point color from the Display column when viewing a timeline on the Design page > Elements tab.

## Data Loading Performance Fixes
## Description
 MEDS Data Viewer has improved data set loading. Previously, when you create a derived variable, return to the Data Viewer tab, and try to filter a data set variable table, the table may appear blank or display an error as the system tries to load the new derived variable. With this update, you can view and filter the data set table without causing a blank screen or error screen to appear.
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the View Data and View Derived Variables building blocks.
## Advantages
 In the Data Viewer tab, you can load data set variable tables with newly created derived variables without causing a blank or error screen. 
## User Impact
 This performance update does not change how you view data sets or create derived variables.
## Special Considerations
 None.

## Data Mapping Reports Include Lab Measurements And Oncology Options
## What Is New?
 You can configure within Data Surveillance or RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping, the lab measurements and oncology data sets and variables that AI Data Reconciliation uses to produce the statistical analysis and visual output for respective reports. The Data Mapping Report now includes new options: 
- Lab Measurements 
- Oncology 
 If you click Data mapping report , and then select Event Analysis , the downloaded report includes CTCAE grade information.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin, Centralized Statistical Monitor.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 The CTCAE reports in AI Data Reconciliation show the data sets and variables you configure in Data Surveillance or RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping > Lab Measurements. For more information, see About AI Reconciliation Reports .
Similarly, RECIST 1.1 reports show the data sets and variables you configure in Data Surveillance or RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping > Oncology. For more information, see RECIST 1.1 .
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data managers can use the CTCAE and RECIST 1.1 reports to get consistent and accurate rating while reconciling data, and effectively compare treatment outcomes to ensure patient safety.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 See What Is New?
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Map Lab Measurements Data 
- Download Data Mapping Report PDFs 
- Map RECIST 1.1 Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
- To edit the Lab Measurements Mapping table, you need Manage CSM Configuration access, whereas to view the table, you need View CSM Configuration. 
- The CTCAE grade in data you ingest from Rave must be a numeric value. CTCAE reports do not work if the CTCAE grade is in Roman numerals. 
- Data you ingest from Rave must be in Central Lab data format, that is, each row must correspond to a single analyte name. If not, for example, if the data is in Local Lab format, you must use transformations in Clinical Data Studio - Data Connect to pivot lab data. 
- If you resize any tab on the Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping page, based on your browser's screen resolution, the page resizes and becomes scrollable.

===== PAGE: data_oversight__monitor_counts_of_issues__patients__and_study_data_using_data_oversight_dashboard | Data Oversight: Monitor Counts of Issues, Patients, and Study Data Using Data Oversight =====
## Data Oversight: Monitor Counts of Issues, Patients, and Study Data Using Data Oversight
 Important : 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the  released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Data Oversight
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 While conducting studies, Lead Clinical Data Managers (LCDMs) and Clinical Data Team Leads (CDTLs) may need to navigate through multiple systems to gather critical operational data needed to manage their studies effectively. This leads to: 
- Lack of complete visibility – It is time-consuming to get a complete view of Clinical Data Studio (CDS) operational activities, and user work compliance without manually consolidating data from various sources. 
- Increased risk and inefficiency –The necessity to switch between capabilities to check on statuses and risk, introduces unnecessary friction, increasing the time spent on oversight, and potentially delays identifying critical issues. 
- Delayed decision-making – Without centralized metrics, lead data managers struggle to quickly answer fundamental questions about work progress, delaying timely interventions and increasing operational risk for the sponsor. 
 To overcome this, Clinical Data Studio now includes a Data Oversight dashboard.
 The Data Oversight dashboard serves as a singular place to understand key operational activities like set up, data import, refresh, and data review as documented in Data Connect and Data Surveillance.  
 Benefit to Users 
 | Data Oversight provides:
- Complete operational transparency – Lead Clinical Data Managers (LCDMs) and Clinical Data Team Leads (CDTLs) can access critical operational metrics and user work compliance from a single page. 
- Flexibility to select key operational metrics – You can select metrics of interest to display on the Data Oversight dashboard, such as:
- Metrics covering reviewed patient profiles, and last refresh date. 
- Visibility into listings created, last refresh date, and records reviewed/not reviewed per listing. 
- Tracking unreviewed AI Reconciliation data per report. 
- Tracking reviewed vendor queries per query set. 
- Reduced friction and risk – By centralizing information, Data Oversight avoids the need to switch between multiple applications, bringing critical information directly into one page.  
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
- Lead Clinical Data Managers (LCDMs) and Clinical Data Team Leads (CDTLs). 
- All users with the View CDS Data Oversight building block. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 Data Oversight reads data from the following modules based on their latest refresh data snapshot.
- Patient Profiles. 
- AI Reconciliation. 
- Listings. 
- Vendor Queries, and 
- Data Connect. 
 Updates made to records, such as marking listings as reviewed or unreviewed, or similar actions in any of the  modules, reflects in the metrics shown on the Data Oversight dashboard instantly. 
 Impact to Applications 
 Data Oversight reads data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- AI Reconciliation. 
- Listings. 
- Vendor Queries, and 
- Data Connect.

===== PAGE: data_quality_hub__centralized__prioritized_view_of_site-level_data_quality | Data Quality Hub: Centralized, Prioritized View of Site-level Data Quality =====
## Data Quality Hub: Centralized, Prioritized View of Site-level Data Quality
 Important :
- To learn more about changes done to these release notes, see the revision history. 
- To learn more about features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the releases history. 
- To learn more about all features in this release, see the released features index.
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality) 
 Functionality or Module 
 | Data Quality Hub (former called the Risk Based Quality Management Summary page)
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 Data Quality Hub (former called the Risk Based Quality Management Summary page) is expanded to now include interactive metrics and visualizations for:
- Priority Focus - Lists sites in the top 25th percentile of Site Impact Scores. 
- Open Signals - Lists the number of in progress, overdue, and lingering signals 
- Risk Inventory - Lists the number risks with the status of open, closed, watch, and transfer and the number of risks with those statues that consider high risk, moderate risk, low risk, or no risk score. 
- Patients Cleaned By Site - Lists the number of cleaned patients and in progress patients by site. 
- All Signals By Site – Lists all signals per site accompanied with additional signal details. 
 Benefit to Users 
 | The Data Quality Hub provides a centralized, prioritized view of site-level data quality within the Clinical Data Studio workspace to help you efficiently identify, prioritize, and address sites with the highest-impact signals of risks.
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
- Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) and Study Managers use the Data Quality Hub to prepare for risk review meetings and plan targeted operational site interventions. 
- Data Managers and Medical Monitors use the Data Quality Hub to overlay statistical metrics with ongoing data cleaning progress charts. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 There is no impact to the workflow process. However, the Data Quality Hub presents an opportunity to review and monitor your data using the following recommended high-level user journey:
- The Background/Use Case : You are managing a study and you need to prepare for a risk review meeting, but you currently spend hours manually pulling fragmented data from the Signal Report, KRI/QTL logs, and CPT status. 
- The Discovery (Dashboard Interaction) : You log in to the RBQM > Data Quality Hub and immediately identify high-risk sites through the "Priority Focus" spotlight, which highlights sites in the top 25% percentile of risk scores pulled from the Signal Grid. 
- The Analysis (Insight Generation) : You validate these priorities by observing that the high-risk sites also show high KRI/QTL breaches and high counts of lingering signals (>30 days), despite having low Cleaning Progress. 
- The Resolution (Post-Feature Goal) : You exit the Data Quality Hub to direct a site monitor toward specific interventions, leading to the resolution of signals in the source applications and a subsequent drop in the site’s Risk Score. 
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact to other applications.
 Impact on Interface 
 The Risk Based Quality Management Summary page is now renamed to the Data Quality Hub page. The Data Quality Hub page is the default page that initially shows when you open RBQM from the Medidata Global navigation. While working in RBQM, you can click Data Quality Hub in the left-hand menu to access to the Data Quality Hub.
 Tip : Click images to enlarge.
 The Data Quality Hub includes the following cards:
 Card Name 
 Description 
 Image 
 | Priority Focus 
 | The Priority Focus card lists sites in the top 25th percentile of Site Impact Scores.
- Site Score – Sum of impact score associated to a signal. 
- Site Impact Score – (Site Score/ Total Study Impact Score)
- Where Total Study Impact Score = Sum of all site impact score in a given study 
 The Priority Focus card prioritizes and sorts sites by Site Impact Score.
 You can click See More for a particular site to navigate to the All Signals By Site section below on the Data Quality Hub. The All Signals By Site will be filtered to show information only for the corresponding site selected from the Priority Focus section.
 | 
 | Key Risk Indicators (KRI) 
 | Previous existing functionality carried over from the Risk Based Quality Management Summary page. 
 The Key Risk Indicators (KRI) card shows:
- Site-level key risk indicator (KRI) performance metrics, including: 
- Number of sites being tracked for KRIs that are added to the SRI. 
- Number and visual spread of low-, medium-, and high-risk sites. 
 You can hover your cursor on a segment in the Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) card donut chart to: 
- View the number of low-, medium-, or high-risk sites. 
- Click a low-, medium-, or high-risk segment to directly access the prefiltered KRI Dashboard listing all sites, medium-risk sites, or high-risk sites, respective. 
 | 
 | Quality Tolerance Limits (QTL) 
 | Previous existing functionality carried over from the Risk Based Quality Management Summary page .
 The Quality Tolerance Limits (QTL) card shows:
- Study-level quality tolerance limits (QTL) performance metrics, including: 
- Number of QTLs begins tracked in the study. 
- Number and visual spread of QTLs that are considered: 
- In Range – The percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's specified criteria is considered within a healthy range of the expectation . Generally, in range QTLs require no action. 
- Out of Range – The percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's specified criteria have exceeded the tolerance threshold . RBQM considers parameters whose QTL values exceed the threshold as at risk. 
- Above Upper Limit – The percentage of patients that do not meet the study parameter's specified criteria has exceeded the tolerance upper limit . RBQM considers parameters whose QTL values exceed the upper limit as high risk. 
 You can hover your cursor on the Quality Tolerance Limits (QTLs) card donut chart to:
- View the number of study QTLs that are considered in range, out of range, or above the QTL's upper limit. 
- Click the donut chart to directly access the QTL Dashboard. 
 | 
 | Risk Management 
 | Previous existing card carried over from the the Risk Based Quality Management Summary page with modified visualization and functionality. 
 The Risk Management card shows t he total count of identified risks as well as the count of overdue and due soon risks where: 
- Overdue   -- The Current Date is after the Target Review Date, indicating that the risk review is overdue. 
- Due Soon – The Target Review Date for the risk review is within one week of the Current Date. 
 You can click a segment in the Risk Management card to directly access the prefiltered Risk Inventory listing all overdue risk reviews. 
 | 
 | Open Signals 
 | Shows the total number of open signals as well as the number of signals that are:
- In Progress 
- Overdue 
- lingering – Open for over 30 days.

 | Risk Inventory 
 | Shows the count of risks per status based on severity.
 You can:
- Hover your cursor on the bar for any risk status to show the total number of risks by status and the total number of risks based on risk severity for that status. 
- Hover your cursor on a segment representing a risk severity to highlight all segments in the bar chart of the same severity. 
 | 
 | Patients Cleaned By Site 
 | Previous existing card that is moved over from the Clean Patient Tracker page and formerly called the Patients In Progress By Site card . It shows all sites by default now, not just the top 10 sites in progress. 
 The Patients Cleaned By Site card  contains   a bar graph that shows the total number of patients at each site broken down by the number of cleaned patients and in progress patients by site. 
 You can: 
- Hover your cursor on the bar for any site to show the raw metrics for that site. 
- Hover your cursor on a segment representing Clean Patients or In Progress Patients to highlight all segments in the bar chart of the same status. 
 In the graph's upper-right corner, you can click the double-sided arrow to open a separate window to:
- View and compare the top ten sites in your study with the highest in progress patient counts. 
- View the Sites list which provides more detailed information concerning outstanding tasks for all sites in your study and enables you to:
- Directly open and review data listings, vendor queries, and AI Reconciliation reports with unreviewed records. 
- Access the full, detailed list of open EDC queries for a specific site. 
 | 
 | All Signals By Site 
 | The All Signals By Site card shows the list of all sites and associated signals. The card shows raw metrics per site such as:
- Site Number 
- Site Country 
- Site Score 
- Total number of signals associated with the site 
- Number of signals created directly from a specific CDS module (such as KRIs, Patient Profiles, Propagation) or number of user-defined signals in the Signals module. 
- Cleaning progress at the site. 
 You can click to directly access the list of Signals for each module from the All Signals By Site card.
 You can also expand a site to show additional details of the breakdown of the analyses of each signal.

## Definitions
 Acronym Glossary 
 For definitions of the different acronyms that can appear in the Knowledge Hub, see  Global Acronym Glossary .
 User Impact Assessment 
 The impact of the change on system behavior and on the user's interaction with it.
- Low – There is no change to current software behavior.
- Moderate – Change includes corrections or improvements that may change user interaction with the software, such as minor UI or minor functionality changes.
- High – Change includes software changes which require review of existing settings, workflow and/or operational procedures to ensure correct user interaction with the software.

===== PAGE: data_reviewer_enhancements | Data Reviewer Enhancements =====
## Data Reviewer Enhancements
## What Is New?
 Improved listings functionality. You can now:
- Create new comments, and edit/delete your own comments. Also, through Mark Reviewed, you can Mark Review a record, and check the status through the Status column for any approved listing. 
- See the preselected records, so that before submitting queries you can make required changes.
- When you select a listing to submit queries, the Submit Queries button is selectable and present next to the Mark Reviewed button. 
- See accurate data when the view option is changed for a selected approved listing. 
- See a fixed-width status comun for all approved data listings. 
- Select rows within approved listings, so you can bulk Mark Review records.  
- Review one record at a time. 
- Click on a comment icon, and have a comment slide out appear where you can read comments, and make new ones. 
- Have the default query text as a mandatory field,  so that you can enter the query text while creating queries. 
- See an Action By column that displays the user name. 
- See the preselected records and the specific columns, so that you can make changes before submitting queries. 
- See the headers of the selected dataset while scrolling down to see the column values for each variable selected at the top. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 None.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications. 
## How Do I Benefit?
- You can now focus the attention on data that has been reviewed. 
- Through the comments feature, you can now document your review findings. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Detect Landing Page > Data Reviewer > Data Listing > select a listing.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 The Detect Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
 Use Listings 
## What Else Should I Know?
 You must refresh an approved listing to enable comments and review that listing.
 Note : Comments and records marked as reviewed are kept through subsequent refreshes. That is, when a record is marked as reviewed, if the same record result is returned after refresh, Detect keeps the record as reviewed and all the comments associated with that record are maintained.  Detect does not clear out the "reviewed" status or the comments after a data refresh.

===== PAGE: data_reviewer_identifies_rave_and_external_data_sets_in_a_study | Data Reviewer Identifies Rave And External Data Sets In A Study =====
## Data Reviewer Identifies Rave And External Data Sets In A Study
## Description
 Data Reviewer 2022.1.1 distinguishes between and identifies data sets from Rave EDC and external sources in a study.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Identifying the origin of data sets enables you to group data set variables of interest from a study and investigate anomalies or discrepancies.
## User Impact
 The Data Set tab on the Medidata Detect >Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) > Data Reviewer > Data Viewer page or Listings page now includes a Rave or External label to identify the origin of the data set. You will also see similar labels for data sets on the Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) > Data Reviewer > Derived Variables page.

===== PAGE: data_set_pre-filtering_by_site_or_subject | Data Set Pre-Filtering By Site Or Subject =====
## Data Set Pre-Filtering By Site Or Subject
## Description
 In the Data Viewer tab, you can now pre-filter data set variable data by Site Number or Subject ID. The filtering works on full or partial number strings, and shows corresponding study data for data sets with over 50,000 records. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the View Data building block. 
## Advantages
 With the the updated filtering options, you can efficiently locate records of interest from a study. 
## User Impact
 In the Data Viewer tab, after a selected data set with over 50,000 record loads, you can use the View menu to pre-filter by Subject ID or Site Name. The filter response differs slightly depending on the selected parameter: 
- If you select Subject ID in the View field and enter the first three characters in the field, the list shows records that include study data with the Subject ID. For example, if you enter 100, the list shows 11371001, 10031023 and so on. You can apply the Column Filter to all columns, except Subject ID. The data set shows records corresponding to the Subject ID you select. 
- If you select Site Name in the View field and enter the first three characters in the   field, the list shows records that include study data with the Site Name. For example, if you enter 100, the list shows 1001, 3100 and so on. You can apply the Column Filter to all columns, except Site Name. The data set shows records corresponding to the Site Name you select.  
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: data_surveillance__configure_clean_patient_tracker_to_autopopulate_missing_page_counts | Data Surveillance: Configure Clean Patient Tracker to Autopopulate Missing Page Counts =====
## Data Surveillance: Configure Clean Patient Tracker to Autopopulate Missing Page Counts
## What Is New?
 To track missing page counts in the Clean Patient Tracker > Patients table > Missing Pages column, you can configure in Data Surveillance whether you want to:
- Manually enter missing page counts, or 
- Autopopulate missing page counts derived from externally ingested and mapped missing page count report datasets. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
- If you configure Data Surveillance to autopopulate missing page counts from an external dataset, then you cannot manually edit entries in the Missing Pages column. 
- For external datasets to be made available for use in the Data Mapping capability's Missing Pages tab, you must first ingest the dataset using Data Connect's Imports capability or using Ingestor. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Configuring Data Surveillance to autopopulate missing page counts in Clean Patient Tracker: 
- Enables your organization to seamlessly incorporate your missing page report data into Data Surveillance for tracking and analysis. 
- Ensures Clean Patient Tracker analyses the most recent available missing page counts to produce the most accurate data analysis. 
- Reduces the time and effort to track missing page counts. 
- Ensures data analysis quality by reducing data entry error. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping capability includes a new Missing Pages tab. In the Missing Pages tab > Missing Pages Source section, you can select one of the following:
- Manual – Manually enter page counts in the Clean Patient Tracker > Patients table > Missing Pages column. This is the default selection. 
- External – Map to an externally ingested dataset from which you want to derive and autopopulate missing page counts in the Clean Patient Tracker > Patients table > Missing Pages column.  
 If you select External, you can then select: 
- Dataset – The externally ingested dataset from which you want to derive and autopopulate missing page counts.
 Note : The dataset must be ingested using Data Connect's Imports capability or Ingestor to be made available for use in Data Surveillance.
 You can then select:
- Missing Page Count – Select the specific column from the selected dataset from which you want to derive and autopopulate missing page counts. 
 OR 
- Expected Page Count and Entered Page Count – Select the specific column from the selected dataset containing the expected page count and then the column containing the entered page count. Data Surveillance calculates the difference between the expected and entered page count and autopopulates those numbers in Clean Patient Tracker. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Configure Manual or Automatic Missing Page Count Entry 
## What Else Should I Know?
- After mapping missing page count report datasets, we recommend triggering Clean Patient Tracker to recount the number of outstanding patient data cleaning tasks to ensure Clean Patient Tracker reports the correct metrics.  
- If the missing pages mapping changes from manual to external, or external to manual, then the data in the Clean Patient Tracker > Patients table > Missing Pages column is overwritten to match the newly selected source. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: data_surveillance__configure_the_data_sets_and_variables_used_in_ctcae_reports | Data Surveillance: Configure The Data Sets And Variables Used In CTCAE Reports =====
## Data Surveillance: Configure The Data Sets And Variables Used In CTCAE Reports
## What Is New?
 The Clinical Data Studio June 2024 release includes two new AI Data Reconciliation reports built on the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v 5.0 grading. 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE Grading  
- Invalid CTCAE Grade  
 You can configure within Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping the lab measurement data sets and variables that AI Data Reconciliation uses to consume and produce the statistical analysis and visual output for CTCAE reports.   
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin, Centralized Statistical Monitor.
 Workflow Process 
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 The CTCAE reports in AI Data Reconciliation show the data sets and variables you configure in Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping > Lab Measurements. For more information about CTCAE reports, see Data Surveillance: Reconcile Oncology Data With CTCAE Grading Reports . 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Lab Measurements provides a simple workspace where you can quickly configure the specific CTCAE data you want AI Data Reconciliation algorithms to analyze.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping page, a new Lab Measurements tab appears where you can configure the data sets and variables that appear in the two CTCAE AI Data Reconciliation reports. If you click the Lab Measurements tab, the Lab Measurements Mapping table appears. You can use the table to enter or select the following information, which AI Data Reconciliation algorithms use to run CTCAE grading analysis on: 
- Dataset 
- Collection Date 
- Sample Type 
- Analyte Name 
- Analyte Value 
- Analyte Unit 
- Upper Limit 
- Lower Limit 
 You can click   Add Lab Measurements   to configure additional lab measurements data that you want the AI Data Reconciliation algorithms to analyze. You can also edit existing lab measurements. 
 You can map multiple data sets in the Lab Measurements Mapping table. However, you can configure a data set only once while configuring lab measurements. 
 Additionally, you must also select CTCAE grade while mapping conditions o n the RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping > Event Analysis tab, otherwise AI Data Reconciliation fails to run its analysis on CTCAE reports. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this 
- Map Lab Measurements Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
- To edit the Lab Measurements Mapping table, you need Manage CSM Configuration access, whereas to view the table, you need View CSM Configuration. 
- The CTCAE grade in data you ingest from Rave must be a numeric value. CTCAE reports do not work if the CTCAE grade is in Roman numerals. 
- Data you ingest from Rave  must be in Central Lab data format, that is, each row must correspond to a single analyte name. If this is not the case, for example, if the data is in Local Lab format, you must use transformations in Clinical Data Studio - Data Connect to pivot lab data. 
- If you resize any tab on the Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping page, based on your browser's screen resolution, the page resizes and becomes scrollable.
