===== PAGE: data_surveillance__reconcile_oncology_data_with_ctcae_grading_reports | Data Surveillance: Reconcile Oncology Data With CTCAE Grading Reports =====
## Data Surveillance: Reconcile Oncology Data With CTCAE Grading Reports
## What Is New?
 Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading is used to assess the severity of side effects experienced during medical treatments, typically cancer therapy. It assigns a grade from 1 to 5, with 1 being mild and 5 being death. This consistent rating system enables researchers and doctors to effectively compare treatment outcomes and ensure patient safety.  To know more about CTCAE grading, see CTCAE v 5.0 .
 AI Data Reconciliation includes two new reports based on the CTCAE version 5.0 grading: 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE Grading – The report includes findings where adverse event (AE) grades depend on lab values, and where AEs have the correct CTCAE grades but with no appropriate lab data collected between AE Start Date and AE End Date. 
- Invalid CTCAE Grade – The report includes findings where adverse events (AEs) have grades not acceptable as per CTCAE criteria v5, or where grade is present but not required, or where no grade is present but is required. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers and study managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data managers can use the CTCAE reports to get consistent and accurate rating while reconciling data, and effectively compare treatment outcomes to ensure patient safety.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Data Surveillance > AI Data Reconciliation > Conditions tab, contains two new reports:
- Invalid CTCAE Grade -  which includes the following fields:
- Patient ID 
- Site 
- Country 
- Data set 
- Status 
- Reported Term 
- Preferred Term 
- Start Date 
- End Date 
- Confidence  
- CTCAE Grade 
- Description 
- Feedback 
- Missing Lab for CTCAE Grade, which includes the following fields:
- Patient ID 
- Site 
- Country 
- Data set 
- Status 
- Reported Term 
- Preferred Term 
- Start Date 
- End Date 
- Confidence  
- CTCAE Grade 
- Same Timeframe Lab 
- Outside Timeframe Lab 
- Feedback 
 You can download both reports. A slide out window appears showing additional records if you click the number hyperlink in the Same Time Frame Labs or Outside Time Frame Labs columns in the CTCAE reports.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- AI Data Reconciliation 
## What Else Should I Know?
- Data sets must be mapped in Event Analysis, otherwise the data sets will not appear in the reports or be processed through AI Data Reconciliation's algorithms. 
- CTCAE reports work only if you: 
- Map Grade in Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping > Event Analysis > Condition Mapping.
- Configure lab measurements in Data Surveillance > Configuration > Data Mapping > Lab Measurements. For more details, see Data Surveillance: Configure The Data Sets And Variables Used In CTCAE Reports . 
- To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: data_surveillance__updated_visualizations_include_additional_sort_options_and_better_usability | Data Surveillance: Updated Visualizations Include Additional Sort Options And Better Usability =====
## Data Surveillance: Updated Visualizations Include Additional Sort Options And Better Usability
## What Is New?
 On the Data Surveillance > Visualizations page:
- Shows the count of visualizations and the latest study snapshot date at the top of the page. 
- If you create a bar chart, or open one with color series, and then sort, the visualization shows the visit schedule dates sorted in alphabetical order on the X-axis. 
- If you create a bar chart, or open one with color series, and then sort by the following options, the visualization shows data accordingly.
- Alphabetical 
- Date 
- Low to high 
- High to low 
- For bar and line charts,text appears paginated if legends for the visualizations show over two rows. 
- For a study with no visualization, a New Visualization button replaces the Add Visualization button. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All study team members. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to workflow.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Graphically visualize study data relationships in line chart enables you to accurately: 
- Gain a clearer understanding or perspective of the study data. 
- Identify study trends and patterns. 
- Track study performance. 
- Build and share reports or present on study data metrics using clear, visually appealing graphical renderings.  
## Where Do I See the Change?
 See What Is New?
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Visualizations 
## What Else Should I Know?
- For visualizations with a large amount of data, we recommend that you add chart filters to narrow your results. If the visualization you want to build experiences slow performance, we recommend that you refresh the page, use additional filters, and then regenerate the preview.
 Tip : For visualizations with many data points on the x-axis, we recommend using a bar graph.
- When selecting a date or text variable for a line chart's x- or y-axis, we highly recommend selecting an aggregation.
- If you do not select an aggregation for a text variable on the y-axis, then the line chart does not render. 
- If you do not select an aggregation for a date variable on the x-axis, then the line chart plots the data for every single day in the database.
 Note : Ideally, we recommend that you use date variables on the x-axis to create a timeline or visualize trends.
- When selecting any variable other than a date variable for the x-axis, if you select an aggregation, then you must select a color series. Otherwise, the chart does not render. 
- Saved visualizations update daily based on the latest study data snapshot. 
- The color palette in the Color Series is read-only.

===== PAGE: data_surveillance__vendor_queries_enables_submitting_queries_directly_to_vendors | Data Surveillance: Vendor Queries Enables Submitting Queries Directly To Vendors =====
## Data Surveillance: Vendor Queries Enables Submitting Queries Directly To Vendors
## What Is New?
 You can now submit queries for issues with vendor data directly to external vendors. Vendors can access and respond to the queries through the Notification Centre.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All vendors with the Submit Vendor Feedback role.
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 Data managers review listings to identify issues with vendor data and submit the query set to the vendor. Vendors receive an email with a hyperlink to access the Clinical Data Studio notification centre. Vendors then add comments, update query status, provide clarification for the queries in the notification centre. The query set gets updated with the vendors' response for further data manager review.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Vendors and data managers have a clear, two way communication channel to clarify questions related to external data. Data managers can send queries directly to vendors for clarification and feedback, enabling faster reconciliation for vendor or external data in listings.  
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Listings page 
 On the Data Surveillance >Vendor Queries page, if you select queries and then click Submit Vendor Queries , the query set shows all the selected queries on the Add Vendor Queries page. If you then complete all the query fields and save the query set, and appears on the Vendor queries page.
 Vendor Queries page 
 If you search the query set, then click the query set name hyperlink, the query set shows a list of all the queries added. The query set is in draft state. You can edit the queries in the query set. You can also download the query set. If you add a due date and then click Submit to vendor , the query set is submitted to vendor group you select. The vendor receives an email with a hyperlink to access the query set from the Notification Centre. The query set status changes to submitted once you click Submit to vendor .

===== PAGE: data_surveillance__verify_rave_target_source_data_count_in_clean_patient_tracker | Data Surveillance: Verify Rave Target Source Data Count In Clean Patient Tracker =====
## Data Surveillance: Verify Rave Target Source Data Count In Clean Patient Tracker
## What Is New?
 You can now obtain source document verification and Targeted Source Document Verification record count from Rave data for activated patients at the record level within Clean Patient Tracker in Clinical Data Studio. For more information, see  Rave TSDV . 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data Managers.
## Workflow Process
 The TSDV module in Rave EDC optimizes data validation by randomly and dynamically selecting patients for verification, rather than verifying all patient data in a Rave study. Targeted SDV uses block plans to reduce the volume of verification performed. The TSDV count shows only if TSDV is set up for the study in Rave EDC. When you click Recalculate in Clean Patient Tracker, the TSDV count calculated at the record level for patients in a specific site, shows.  Otherwise, the SDV count appears. 
## Other Applications
 No impact on other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data managers can distinguish between data that has Targeted source data verification (TSDV). Data managers can ensure that they review and verify the correct data before a study is locked. This enables greater data integrity and accuracy. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Data Surveillance > Clean Patient Tracker, TSDV % appears as a column in the patients table.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the feature : 
- Track and Clean Patient Data . 
## What Else Should I Know?
- The TSDV count shown at record level does not account for deleted, hidden, or inactive Rave data.  
- TSDV counts appear if TSDV is established for the study. For studies that require verification in Rave Architect, only the SDV count appears. 
- TSDV is set up after patients are already in Rave, study managers must include those patients in the TSDV plan. Patients who are not part of the TSDV plan show only as part of the SDV count.  
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: data_surveillance_and_rbqm__configure_study_data_source_using_event_analysis_mapping | Data Surveillance and RBQM: Configure Study Data Source Using Event Analysis Mapping =====
## Data Surveillance and RBQM: Configure Study Data Source Using Event Analysis Mapping
## What Is New?
 You can now set up your study data source as  Rave EDC or external. External studies are those with externally coded terms from MEDRA or WHODRUG ingested into Rave.  
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 The Clinical Data Studio workflow analyzes and visualizes your study data depending on the data source you select. For more information, see  Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline .
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Selecting an explicit data source for your study enables data managers to use capabilities like Reconciliation, Event Analysis and analyze data quality and maintain data integrity.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Study Data Source 
 On the Data Surveillance or RBQM tab > Configuration > Data Mapping > Event Analysis tab, if you click Set Data Source from the top right corner of the page, you can select Rave or External as your data source. For new studies, there is no default selection, you must explicitly select one option. However, existing studies map to Rave as a data source by default. When you select a new data source, all previous data mappings for the study are removed. The data source appears in a new Data Source column on the Event Analysis page. For a new study, you must first select a data source before mapping event analysis data. The Event Analysis data mapping PDF report includes all the fields you configure for both external or Rave data sources. 
 Mapping Conditions, Treatments, and History 
 If you select Rave as your study data source, you can only configure datasets in the Conditions, Treatments, and History mappings from studies that use Rave Coder or Coder+.  For external data, see the following: 
 Condition Mapping Treatment Mapping History Mapping 
 Condition Mapping
## Condition Mapping
 If you select an external data source, that is, if your study does not use Rave Coder or Coder+, and then click New Mapping > Condition Mapping to create or edit a condition mapping,  you can configure the following new fields on the Condition Mapping page: 
- Preferred Term Code 
- Preferred Term 
- Optional . System Organ Class (SOC) Name 
 You cannot save the condition mapping unless you configure all the mandatory fields.
 Treatment Mapping
## Treatment Mapping
 If you select an external data source , that is, if your study does not use Rave Coder or Coder+, and then click New Mapping > Treatment Mapping to create or edit a  treatment mapping  with Concomitant Treatment Type as Medication, you can configure the following new, mandatory fields on the Treatment Mapping page:
- ATC 2 Code 
- ATC 2 Name 
- Product Name 
- Product Code 
 If you select an external data source , that is, if your study does not use Rave Coder or Coder+, and then click  New Mapping > Treatment Mapping to create or edit a  treatment mapping with Concomitant Treatment Type as Procedure , you can configure the following new, mandatory fields on the Treatment Mapping page:
- Product Name 
- Product Code 
 History Mapping
## History Mapping
 If you select an external data source , that is, if your study does not use Rave Coder or Coder+, and then click  New Mapping > History Mapping to create or edit an existing history mapping, you can configure the following new fields on the History Mapping page:
- Preferred Term Code 
- Preferred Term 
- Optional . System Organ Class (SOC) Name 
 You cannot save the history mapping unless you configure all the mandatory fields.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Clinical Data Studio's Data Pipeline 
- Map Event Analysis Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
- You can only map one data source at a time for your study. 
- Before selecting an external data source, you must first import that external data using Data Connect's Imports capability  or through Ingestor . 
- You cannot perform reconciliation activities or submit queries for derived datasets in Reconciliation if you do not map to the correct study data source.

===== PAGE: data_surveillance_configuration__schedule_data_refreshes_using_unified_scheduler | Data Surveillance Configuration: Schedule Data Refreshes Using Unified Scheduler =====
## Data Surveillance Configuration: Schedule Data Refreshes Using Unified Scheduler
 Important : 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the   released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Unified Scheduler
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter: 
 In clinical studies, data managers require predictable workflows with regards to study data.  Manual refreshes provide flexibility, but relying solely on manual intervention increases operational overhead and risks data not being ready for governance checkpoints and review windows . Clinical Data Studio includes Unified Scheduler to resolve such issues . Unified Scheduler enables setting up automated refresh scheduling along with the existing on-demand capabilities for: 
- Listings 
- Patient Profiles 
- AI Reconciliation 
- Custom Graphs 
 Benefit to Users 
 | 
 Unified Scheduler provides: 
- Automated scheduling for governance checkpoints and review windows . 
- Reduced operational overhead . 
- A scalable and auditable framework for data refreshes . 
- Support for both scheduled refreshes and on-demand refreshes across the following capabilities: 
- Listings 
- AI Reconciliation 
- Patient Profiles 
- Custom Graphs 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Data managers and study team members must possess both building blocks; capability-specific, and Unified Scheduler related, to view and manage data refresh schedules . For example, if you do not have the Refresh AI Reconciliation permission, you cannot create or edit refresh schedules on either the Unified Scheduler page or the AI Reconciliation page.

 Impact to Workflow Processes 
- Schedules operate on daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, bimonthly, and quarterly cadences . 
- There is no limit to number of refreshes you can schedule to run in a study per day. 
- Conflict prevention rules block multiple on-demand refreshes for the same module on the same snapshot, and block on-demand refreshes while scheduled refreshes run . That is, a record selected for a scheduled refresh is not available for on-demand refresh selection. 
- You can download unified scheduler configurations in PDF format. When the download is complete and available, you get a notification through the Notification Centre. 
 Note : For on-demand refreshes:
- Listings and Custom Graphs allow up to four successful refreshes per day per listing or custom graph . 
- Patient Profiles and AI Reconciliation allow up to two successful refreshes per day . 
 Impact to Applications 
- Unified Scheduler updates data for Listings, AI Reconciliation, Patient Profiles, and Custom Graphs (previously known as Visualizations) . 
- Each Data Surveillance capability included in Unified Scheduler refreshes data independently. Resources already refreshed using the latest available DQM workflow data, or resources currently undergoing refresh, are automatically excluded. 
 Impact on Interface 
 If you click Data Surveillance > Configuration, a new Unified Scheduler page appears as follows:
 Number

You can specify up multiple refresh schedules for listings, patient profiles, and custom graphs. For AI Reconciliation, you can have only one data refresh schedule that includes all the AI Reconciliation reports. For each scheduled refresh, you can click the three dots, More icon ( ) to view Edit, Included Items and Delete options. You can click Edit to edit the scheduled refresh, click Included Items to view all the items, for example, listings or custom graphs in a specific refresh schedule. If you click Delete , you can delete a scheduled data refresh.

The schedule shows the date and time for the refresh. If no refresh schedule exists, a No refresh schedule created yet. message appears.

===== PAGE: deactivate_system_kris_from_displaying_in_medidata_detect | Deactivate System KRIs from Displaying in Medidata Detect =====
## Deactivate System KRIs from Displaying in Medidata Detect
## Description
 You can now deactivate system KRIs so that the system KRIs' data do not get filtered, analyzed, calculated, or displayed in Medidata Detect .
## Affected Roles
- RBQM Configuration Manager users 
- Detect users 
## Advantages
 Deactivating system KRIs:
- Removes from Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table  the key risk indicator (KRI) data that you have no need to track or analyze. 
- Yields a cleaner KRI table view by displaying only data that is relevant to your study. 
- Optimizes your KRI data analysis speed and efficiency. 
## User Impact
 On the KRIs page > Key Risk Indicators list > Activate column, you can click   in the corresponding row of the system KRI you want to deactivate. To learn more, see  Activate and Deactivate KRIs .
## Special Considerations
 You cannot edit a system KRI's configuration.
 You can reactivate previously deactivated system KRIs using the same process you would to activate. To learn more, see  Activate and Deactivate KRIs .

===== PAGE: define_custom_qtls_and_percentage_kris_to_target_specific_data_population_subsets | Define Custom QTLs and Percentage KRIs to Target Specific Data Population Subsets =====
## Define Custom QTLs and Percentage KRIs to Target Specific Data Population Subsets
## Description
 When building or modifying custom QTL or percentage KRI expressions, you can now configure expressions to calculate against specific data population subsets. 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Configuring expressions to target and produce QTL and KRI values for data population subsets allows you to more precisely monitor specific data of interest.
## User Impact
 When you:
- Add or edit custom percentage KRIs on the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box, or 
- Add or edit custom QTLs on the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box 
 each dialog box now includes the Denominator Query section and Denominator Expression section.
 Building an expression in the Denominator Query section works the same as building an expression using the Numerator Query section. Likewise, the Denominator Expression section previews the expression in the same way as the Numerator Expression section. The difference is that the expression in the Numerator Query section targets the entire data set population. Whereas the Denominator Query targets a data set population subset as specified in the query.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Detect Configuration Manager Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement:
- Add and Edit Custom QTLs 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs 
## Special Considerations
 When adding or editing custom QTLs, you must build an expression in the Denominator Query section. However, when adding or editing custom percentage KRIs, building an expression in the Denominator Query section is optional. Leaving the c ustom percentage KRI's D enominator Query section empty results in the KRI calculating against the study's entire patient population. 
 In the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box and Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box, the Expression Builder section and Expression section are renamed to Numerator Query and Numerator Expression , respectively.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: derived_variable_-_expression_builder | Derived Variable - Expression Builder =====
## Derived Variable - Expression Builder
## Description
 You can build a derived variable by using the expression builder to apply mathematical and logical operations on data set variables. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables permission.
## Advantages
 With the expression builder, you can perform robust operations to configure derived variables to see the data you need and take appropriate action. For example:
- Calculate the upper limit of a lab range by scaling from a base normal value. The derived variable can help you detect at-risk patients outside of the clinical range. 
- Conditionally replace literal data such as check box data to make the data human-readable. Check box data appears as binary ones and zeros, so you can use the expression builder to convert the data into meaningful text. 
## User Impact
 You can find the Expression Builder option in the Derived Variable Type dropdown. To build an expression, you must select a combination of data set variables from the Derived Variables > Data Sets tab and operators from the Derived Variables > Operators tab. For details on building expressions, see  Create Derived Variable from Expression .
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: derived_variable_-_merge | Derived Variable - Merge =====
## Derived Variable - Merge
## Description
 You can merge a data set variable from one data set into a target data set. The target data set lists the merged data set variable as a derived variable within the variable list.  Merging options include: 
- Single to Single  – Merge a data set variable containing singular records over multiple visits with another data set containing singular records over multiple visits. For example, merging a Demographics data set variable to the Eligibility Criteria data set. 
- Single to Multiple  – Merge a data set variable containing singular records over multiple visits with another data set containing multiple records over multiple visits. For example, merging a Demographics data set variable to the Adverse Events data set. 
- Multiple to Single  – Merge a data set variable containing multiple records over multiple visits with another data set containing singular records over multiple visits. For example, merging an Adverse Events data set variable to Demographics data set. 
- Multiple to Multiple  – Merge a data set variable containing multiple records over multiple visits with another data set containing multiple records over multiple visits. For example, merging an Adverse Events data set variable to the Chemistry data set. 
 The merge workflow dynamically detects the merge type based on the source and target data sets. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables permission.
## Advantages
 With the merge workflow, you can join two data sets together to:
- Populate values from two different data sets on the same table. 
- Prepare a data set to perform robust calculations with the Expression Builder. 
## User Impact
 You can find the Merge option in the Derived Variable Type dropdown. To merge data sets, you must select the source data variable and target data set. Depending on the type of merge, you must also select additional reference data. For details on the merge workflow, see  Merge Variables to Data Sets .
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: derived_variables_-_check_all_that_apply | Derived Variables - Check All That Apply =====
## Derived Variables - Check All That Apply
## Description
 You can now create the Check all that Apply data set variable. With the Check all that Apply derived variable, you can concatenate multiple Boolean data set variables.  For example, you can concatenate "race and ethnicity" variables to create a single text variable that is a combination of race and ethnicity. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables building block. 
## Advantages
 With the Check all that Apply option, you can configure derived variables to see the data you need and take appropriate action. For more details, see Description. 
## User Impact
 You can find the Check all that Apply option in the Derived Variable > Create Derived Variable > Derived Variable Type menu. To build a single concatenated text variable, you must select a combination of Boolean variables from Derived Variable > Data Sets tab and operators from the Derived Variables > Operators tab.  
 While using the  Check all that Apply  workflow:  
- You can select a concatenation separator. The default separator is a comma (,). The text entered in the Prefix field only appears once at the beginning of the derived variable. Likewise, the text entered in the Suffix field only appears once at the end of the derived variable.  
- You can drag only Boolean data set variables from the data set. 
 The concatenated string appears with labels separated by the specified separator. Labels appear only if Boolean values for a variable are non-null. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The following article has been created in the MEDS Data Viewer Knowledge Space to support this feature: 
- Create Derived Variable with Check All That Apply 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: derived_variables_-_conditional_concatenate | Derived Variables - Conditional Concatenate =====
## Derived Variables - Conditional Concatenate
## Description
 You can now create the Conditional Concatenate derived variable. With the Conditional Concatenate derived variable, you can combine multiple IF-THEN-ELSE expressions to build a text-based derived variable. You can concatenate up to 20 data set variables in a single operation. After creating a Conditional Concatenate derived variable, you can only edit the derived variable's label; all other fields become read-only. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables building block. 
## Advantages
 With the Conditional Concatenate option, you can configure derived variables to see the data you need and take appropriate action.  
## User Impact
 You can find the Conditional Concatenate option in the Derived Variable > Create Derived Variable > Derived Variable Type menu. To build concatenated expressions, you must select a combination of data set variables from the Derived Variables > Data Sets tab and operators from the Derived Variables > Operators tab.  
 When using the Conditional Concatenate workflow: 
- You must include at least two IF-THEN-ELSE blocks in the concatenated expression. 
- You can concatenate up to 20 data set variables and up to 10 rows of dual IF-THEN-ELSE blocks. 
- You can select a concatenation separator. The default separator is a comma (,). The text entered in the Prefix field only appears once at the beginning of the derived variable. Likewise, the text entered in the Suffix field only appears once at the end of the derived variable.  
 After creating the derived variable, you can only edit the variable's label field. 
 For details on building expressions, see Knowledge Space Updates. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The following article has been created in the MEDS Data Viewer Knowledge Space to support this feature: 
- Create Derived Variable with Conditional Concatenate 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: derived_variables_updates_ensure_accurate_data_set_selection_while_merging | Derived Variables Updates Ensure Accurate Data Set Selection While Merging =====

===== PAGE: design_management_patient_profiles | Design Management Patient Profiles =====
## Design Management Patient Profiles
## Description
 Medidata Patient Profiles provides the following design management capabilities:
- Create New Designs  – Initially create and begin working on a new design in the Design page. 
- Find and Access Designs  – Find and access already existing designs for which you have permissions to access. 
- Reassign Master Designs  – The master design is the design that CSA uses for analytics and to generate profiles. If you want track design versions over time, you can copy the prior master design. Then you can make changes to the duplicate and reassign the duplicate copy as the new master design. 
- Rename Designs – Edit the design name from the Design List page. 
- Duplicate Designs  – Duplicate a design to create alternate versions, which you can modify for consumption from audiences with different data interests. For example, you can create a design for a data manager, and then create and modify a duplicate with slightly different design configurations for a site manager. 
- Delete Designs 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 You can perform all design management tasks on the Patient Profile design page. You can also rename designs by accessing a design's Design page and editing the name field.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: designate_designs_as_blinded_or_unblinded | Designate Designs as Blinded or Unblinded =====
## Designate Designs as Blinded or Unblinded
## Description
 In accordance with the new unblinded and blinded user roles , Patient Profiles Cloud also introduces unblinded and blinded designs.
- Unblinded Design  – A design that may contain sensitive data. Only unblinded Patient Profiles Cloud users can access and view unblinded designs. Unblinded designers can also edit unblinded designs. Blinded Patient Profiles Cloud users cannot access and view unblinded designs. 
- Blinded Design  – All Patient Profiles Cloud users can access and view blinded designs. Unblinded designers can also edit blinded designs. 
 New and updated designs are designated as unblinded designs by default. Unblinded patient profile designers can change unblinded designs to blinded designs. Conversely, designers can also change blinded designs to unblinded designs.
## Affected Roles
- Unblinded patient profile designers can mark designs as unblinded or blinded. Designers can also view and edit all designs. 
- Unblinded patient profile viewers can view all designs. 
- Blinded patient profile viewers cannot view unblinded designs. However, blinded users can view blinded designs. 
## Advantages
- Introducing unblinded and blinded designs further restricts which designs users can or cannot view and edit. Doing so ultimately protects blinded data within Patient Profiles Cloud. This enables organizations to confidently and safely run any study in Patient Profiles Cloud without running the risk of voiding the study. 
- Automatically designating new and updated designs as unblinded by default is a safeguard in case the new or updated information in the design is sensitive data. Designers can always manually mark the design as blinded if necessary. 
## User Impact
 On the Patient Profile Designs page, unblinded patient profile designers can change unblinded designs to blinded or change blinded designs to unblinded.
 Tip : Click to enlarge images.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: detect-risk_management_qtl_integration_enhancement | Detect-Risk Management QTL Integration Enhancement =====
## Detect-Risk Management QTL Integration Enhancement
## Description
 Medidata Detect-Risk Management integration is improved so that when adding a custom QTL in QTL Configuration, if you select a pre-populated, Risk Management-derived QTL from the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box > Parameter field, then:
- The Parameter field and Description field automatically populate with the text entered in the corresponding fields in Risk Management. 
- All fields including the Parameter field and Description field in the Quality Tolerance Limits dialog box are editable. 
- The Save button is enabled. 
 Any QTL updates saved in QTL Configuration propagate to the QTL details in Risk Management as well.
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admins
## Advantages
 When adding a custom QTL in previous releases, if you selected a Risk Management-derived QTL from the Parameter field, you could only edit the Parameter field and Description field in the Quality Tolerance Limits dialog box. Now when adding a custom QTL, if you select a Risk Management-derived QTL from the Parameter field, then you can edit all fields in the Quality Tolerance Limits dialog box. This ensures that you can configure all the appropriate QTL details.
## User Impact
 When adding a custom QTL, if you select a Risk Management-derived QTL from the Parameter field, then you can edit and save all fields in the Quality Tolerance Limits dialog box.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this enhancement: 
- Add and Edit Custom QTLs 
## Special Considerations
 None.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: detect_global_template_library_and_template_groups | Detect Global Template Library and Template Groups =====
## Detect Global Template Library and Template Groups
## What Is New?
 You can save and store commonly used listing , custom numeric KRI, or custom percentage KRI configurations as templates in your organization's global template library. You can then import your listing and KRI templates to reuse when creating new listings or KRI configurations within a study. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Members of your organization who build studies can save and store listing and custom KRI configurations as templates in your organization's template library.
 Members of your organization who review data; for example, study managers or data managers, can import and reuse listing and KRI configuration templates in studies.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Adding and using specific listings and custom KRIs as Detect templates:
- Enables you and your team to quickly and easily reapply common listings and custom KRIs as needed across study configurations. 
- Promotes faster study startup time. 
- Ensures consistency and accuracy in listing and custom KRI details across studies. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Tip : Click the images below to enlarge.
 The Detect Landing Page > Configuration and Reporting card now includes a Detect Templates link. 
 Your organization has its own client division (CD) -level global Template Library page in Detect's Configuration and Reporting module. The template library stores and lists the collection of your organization's template groups and associated templates.
 On your organization's Template Library page, you can:
- Click a Group Name from the list of templates to edit the Group Name or Description or view details of the Listing or KRI templates in the group. 
- Click New Template Group and use the Template Group window to create template groups in the template library. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 The Medidata Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature: 
- Detect Templates 
- View, Add, and Manage Template Groups 
- Add Listings, Custom KRIs, and QTLs as Templates to Template Groups 
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- Add and Store Listing Configurations as Reusable Templates 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs 
- Add and Store Custom KRI Configurations as Reusable Templates 
## What Else Should I Know?
- The name of the template group and template name must be unique. 
- Avoid naming groups or wording descriptions in such a way that can unblind or compromise other studies or study users. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: detect_landing_page__template_group_s_kris_template_list_includes_numeric_kri_filter_criteria | Review Reports: Template Group's KRIs Template List Includes Numeric KRI Filter Criteria =====
## Review Reports: Template Group's KRIs Template List Includes Numeric KRI Filter Criteria
 Important : 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the releases history . 
- For a summary of all features released, the released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Enhancement (Updated Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Detect Landing Page > Library > Templates
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter :
 When configuring custom numeric KRIs, you can build an expression to filter for the specific subset of data that you want the KRI to perform statistical analysis on. To learn more, see  RBQM Configuration: Configure Custom Numeric KRIs That Run Statistical Analysis on Specific Data Subsets .
 In accordance with this functionality, when working in the Template Library, when you view a Template Group, the list of KRIs templates now includes a  Filter Criteria column. If there is an expression built for a custom numeric KRI, then the Filter Criteria column presents the expression in the list of KRI templates.
 Benefit to Users 
 | Adding the Filter Criteria column:
- Supports and aligns the Template Library with the current custom numeric KRI configuration functionality. 
- Provides comprehensive KRI details across studies.

## Definitions
 Acronym Glossary 
 For definitions of the different acronyms that can appear in the Knowledge Hub, see  Global Acronym Glossary .
 User Impact Assessment 
 The impact of the change on system behavior and on the user's interaction with it.
- Low – There is no change to current software behavior.
- Moderate – Change includes corrections or improvements that may change user interaction with the software, such as minor UI or minor functionality changes.
- High – Change includes software changes which require review of existing settings, workflow and/or operational procedures to ensure correct user interaction with the software.

===== PAGE: detect_provides_clearer_data_refresh_messaging | Detect Provides Clearer Data Refresh Messaging =====
## Detect Provides Clearer Data Refresh Messaging
 IMPORTANT: THIS FEATURE IS FROM A PRIOR RELEASE AND IS NOW DEPRECATED. IT NO LONGER EXISTS IN DETECT. 
## Description
 On the Overview page, when you click Refresh Analytics, you receive one of the following messages:
- "Detect is currently refreshing to acquire and output your study's most recent data." 
- Displays when the study data you see in Detect is not currently up to date, and Detect initializes the process of updating the analytics. 
- "The study data refresh in Detect is still in progress."
- Displays when the study data you see in Detect is not currently up to date, but Detect is already in the process of updating the analytics. 
- "Detect already contains your study's current data."
- Displays when the study data you see in Detect is currently up to date. In this case, Detect does not initialize a refresh of the analytics. 
## Affected Roles
 Users with Manage Detect permissions granted in Cloud Administration .
## Advantages
 The updating data refresh messaging helps you better understand the current status of the data displaying in Detect and the current status of pending data updates, if any.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: determine_study_data_outliers__risks__and_trends_using_error_plots | Determine Study Data Outliers, Risks, and Trends Using Error Plots =====
## Determine Study Data Outliers, Risks, and Trends Using Error Plots
## Description
 Error plots are graphical representations of Rave CSA's data analysis on a variable or combination of variables in your study data. The data analysis displays in the form of frequency distribution plots, box-and-whisker plots, or scatter plots.
## Affected Roles
- Data managers 
- Central monitors 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 You can use error plots to determine outliers, anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data. 
 Determining the outliers, anomalies, risks, and trends in your study data puts you and your life sciences team in an optimal position to take actions on your study, such as:
- cleaning data, 
- opening issues, 
- opening queries, 
- issuing corrective actions, 
- coordinating additional training, 
- and much more. 
## User Impact
 You can access error plots on the Error Plots page. To learn more, see  Data Anomaly Detection Plots .
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: distinct_element_types_cannot_have_the_same_merge_name | Distinct Element Types Cannot Have the Same Merge Name =====
## Distinct Element Types Cannot Have the Same Merge Name
## Description
 When working in the Settings page > CSA tab, a validation check prevents you from entering the same merge name for two distinct element types.
## Affected Roles
- Patient Profile Designers 
## Advantages
 In previous Patient Profiles Cloud releases, you could enter the same merge name for two distinct element types on the Settings page > CSA tab. However, doing so would cause CSA's analytics to fail. The new validation check prevents you from entering the same merge name for two distinct element types. Thus, preventing human error and improving CSA's analytics success rate. For example, a wide table and event table cannot have the same merge name.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 You can enter the same merge name for multiple elements of the same element type. For example, three wide table elements can have the same merge name.

 Knowledge Space Updates

===== PAGE: duplicate_designs_to_other_study_environments_within_the_same_study_in_patient_profiles | Duplicate Designs to Other Study Environments Within the Same Study in Patient Profiles =====
## Duplicate Designs to Other Study Environments Within the Same Study in Patient Profiles
## Description
 You can now copy a single profile design from a study environment to any other environment that you have access to within the same study.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 In previous Patient Profiles versions, there was no way to duplicate a profile design from one study environment to another environment within the same study. Therefore, any time you wanted to see your design in different study environments, you needed to rebuild the design in each environment. Now you can quickly and easily duplicate a design to any study environment you have access to. This saves you time and effort and also ensures that your designs are initially the same when you migrate to other environments.
## User Impact
 In the Patient Profile Design list: when you click   for any design and then click Duplicate , then the ensuing Duplicate Design dialog box now displays a Duplicate to... dropdown. You can click the dropdown to select any study environment that you have access to that you want to copy your design to.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: edit_kri_details_and_configurations | Edit KRI Details and Configurations =====
## Edit KRI Details and Configurations
## Description
 On the Key Risk Indicators page, you can now edit:
- All custom numeric KRI details 
- All custom percentage KRI including the KRI expression conditions 
 Detect Configuration Manager records: 
- User name  
- Date stamp of the last edit 
- User entered reason for the KRI change 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Administrators. 
## Advantages
 In previous releases, you created a KRI configuration to correct an error or alter a KRI configuration. This resulted in a process that accumulated multiple stale KRI configurations for your study. With the new editing capability, you can edit an existing KRI that is much cleaner in your study.  
## User Impact
 On the Custom Numeric KRI dialog box, in addition to the Name and Description, you can now edit: 
- Data Set 
- Variable 
- Threshold Type 
- Moderate Risk Threshold 
- High Risk Threshold 
- Calculation Type 
- Risk Category 
- Reason for Change (mandatory) 
 On the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box, in addition to the Name and Description, you can now edit:
- Threshold Type 
- Moderate Risk Threshold 
- High Risk Threshold  
- Risk Category 
- Reason for Change (mandatory) 
- The condition or conditions that define the expression 
 You can save Custom Numeric KRIs or Custom Percentage KRIs only if you complete mandatory fields. A warning message in red text shows if you leave fields empty or have an incomplete expression in the Edit dialog box. 
 Note : The Threshold Type, Moderate Risk Threshold, High Risk Threshold, and Reason for Change fields are new as of the Detect Configuration Manager 2022.1.0 release. To learn more about the Threshold Type enhancement, see Configure Custom KRI Thresholds . 
 The Key Risk Indicators page includes the following new columns: 
- Updated By – User name of the user who edited the KRI. 
- Last Updated – Last KRI edit timestamp showing date and time 
 For any updated KRI, the Updated By Column has a Message icon for the associated KRI that shows reason for change by user.  
 Knowledge Space Updates 
 None.
## Special Considerations
- You can only edit inactive KRIs. 
- You can make a KRI inactive at any time to modify the configuration. 
- Reason for Change is a mandatory field. You cannot save a KRI unless you specify the reason for change. 
- High Risk Threshold is an optional field. If you only specify the Moderate Risk threshold, then KRIs appear green if values are below moderate risk, and red if the values are above moderate risk threshold. 
- If you edit KRIs active in the past, the edits will affect the KRIs trending values when you compare values before and after saving the edit. 
- Before editing KRIs, download and archive a PDF of the KRI's original configurations. Detect Configuration Manager does not audit KRI changes. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: element_conditional_display_options_updated | Element Conditional Display Options Updated =====
## Element Conditional Display Options Updated
## Description
 When you set up conditional display options for an element, the Operator field now shows only three options: "=", "not =", and "contains".
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 With fewer operators available for conditional display, Patient Profile designers can filter and locate specific patient data in a study.
## User Impact
 When working with wide tables, transposed tables, or patient information tables on the Design page > Elements tab > TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options section > Display Conditions:
- Element: When you click , the Operator field only shows three options: "=", "not =", and "contains"
- If you select "=" as the operator, the element displays patient data if the variable is equal to the value set up in the expression. Otherwise the patient data does not display. 
- If you select "not =" as the operator, the element displays patient data if the variable is not equal to the value set up in the expression. Otherwise the patient data does not display. 
- If you select "contains" as the operator, the element displays patient data only if the variable in the expression contains  the value set up in the expression. Otherwise the patient data does not display. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: email_users_and_support_team_if_patient_profiles_bulk_pdf_generation_fails | Email Users And Support Team If Patient Profiles Bulk PDF Generation Fails =====
## Email Users And Support Team If Patient Profiles Bulk PDF Generation Fails
## Description
 For failed bulk patient profile design PDF exports, you receive an email displaying: 
- The number of patients who failed bulk PDF generation. 
- An attachment listing the corresponding patient IDs. 
 The Medidata Support Team also receives  this email for further action. 
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 With clear indication about patient IDs that failed bulk PDF generation, Patient Profile design reviewers can reach out to the Medidata Patient Profiles representative for further action. 
## User Impact
 Bulk patient profile PDF generation email now include patient IDs that fail to export. The email is in the following format:  
 The Patient Profiles PDF you requested on <date/time> has encountered an error. A notification has been sent to the Medidata Patient Profiles support team.   For further information, contact your Medidata Patient Profiles representative. 
 The list of patient IDs that failed to export to PDF is in the format :  List of PDF Failures <date & time> . 
## Special Considerations
 Processing times may vary depending on the number of patient profiles in your study. The minimum time taken is one hour.

===== PAGE: enhanced_ability_to_identify_data_sets_and_variables_in_your_design_in_patient_profiles | Enhanced Ability to Identify Data Sets and Variables in Your Design in Patient Profiles =====
## Enhanced Ability to Identify Data Sets and Variables in Your Design in Patient Profiles
## Description
 Patient Profiles 2018.1.0 introduced visual enhancements to the Data Options tab on the Design page > Elements tab to help you identify which data sets and variables are applied to your design. To learn more, see  Browse Data Sets and Add Variables to Elements More Efficiently .
 Patient Profiles 2018.2.0 builds upon these visual enhancements by:
- Displaying the visual indicators in the list of data sets in a stronger, bolder color. For example, a stronger shade of green indicates data sets applied to your design. 
- Increasing the width of the visual indicators in the list of data sets. 
- Including the data set list's visual indicators in the:
- Design page > Layout tab 
- Settings page > Design Options tab 
- Element Display Condition dialog box, accessible from the Table Options tab when designing timelines or any table element. 
- Row Display Condition dialog box, accessible from the Table Options tab when designing any table element. 
- Highlight Condition dialog box, accessible from the Table Options tab when designing wide tables and transposed tables. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Bolder, wider visual indicators enhance your ability to scan and identify your design's selected data sets and variables. The visual indicators also display in more data set lists throughout Patient Profiles, not just the Data Options tab on the Design page > Elements tab.
## User Impact
 The table below illustrates the visual enhancements made in Patient Profiles 2018.2.0.

## Enhanced Navigation When Saving an Element from Unsaved Changes Dialog Box in Patient Profiles
## Description
 If you edit an element on the Design page > Elements tab and then attempt to leave the Elements tab without saving, then the unsaved changes dialog box displays as expected.
 In previous releases, when you clicked the Save button from the dialog box, you remained on the Elements tab. Now clicking Save directs you to the page or tab you want to navigate to.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Clicking Save in the unsaved changes dialog box directs you to the page or tab that you want to navigate to.

===== PAGE: enhancements_improve_listings_functionality | Enhancements Improve Listings Functionality =====
## Enhancements Improve Listings Functionality
## Description
 You can now search existing listings, edit, and save listings with draft or approved status. The Listings tab indicates the status with a blue or gray marker next to the listing name. You can also search data sets to build conditional expressions while creating listings.
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Data Reviewer access.
## Advantages
 The Draft and Approved listings workflow ensures data management listing reports are peer reviewed by separate individuals before use.
## User Impact
 On the Data Reviewer page > Listings tab: 
- You can search listings in your study using the search field. 
- If you first create a listing, it saves with Draft status. You can then open and edit the draft listing if necessary, preview the listing records, and click Save and Approve to save the listing with Approved status. The Listings tab shows the status next to the listing name. 
- If you click Edit Listing , you can edit approved listings. You can enter the reason for the edit in the Reason for change field. The Edit Listing button does not show if a listing data refresh is in progress. 
- If you click the (clock) icon next to the Listings tab, a new browser window shows the audit history of the listings on the page.  
- If you click the (information) icon next to any listing, a tooltip shows the conditional expression for the listing.
 Tip : Click the image to enlarge.
- If you click Column Filter for an approved listing, the filter list show values for the variables in the listing. If you select values from the list and click Apply , the listing shows records as per the filters you apply. You can click Reset Filter to remove filters. 
 Conditional Expression in Listings 
- Approved listings show listing records whereas draft listings show the conditional expression, which you can edit or review, and save the listing with draft or approved status. 
- The expression builder includes two new comparison operators and the one of operator is available for text fields:
- >= (greater_than_or_equal_to) - compares greater than or equal values. 
- <= ( less_than_or_equal to ) - compares less than or equal values. 
- one of - selects a value from the list to compare variable values. 
- While building conditional expressions for listings, you can: 
- Search data sets using the search field in the Data Sets tab. 
- Search data set variables by dragging a variable or typing in the field. You must type two or more characters to search variables from data sets. You can also select variables without a suffix, for example, date variables with partial dates.  
- 
- Add a text or numeric variable using comparison operators (=, <, >, != ) and a free text field, where you can also drag and drop variable values.
- Select the Exclude Patients with option to exclude certain patients as per the conditional expression you build for the listing.  
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Detect Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support the enhancement: 
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
## Special Considerations
 Only roles with the Manage Data Reviewer building block can build, edit or approve Listings. All users can view, sort, filter and see audit history.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal.

===== PAGE: error_plot_enhancements | Error Plot Enhancements =====
## Error Plot Enhancements
## Description
 The Error Plots page now includes the following  high-level performance-related metrics pertaining to the selected variable: 
- Total # of Outliers  – The total number of distinct data points that are considered outliers for the selected variable. 
- % of Outliers  – The percentage of all the domain set's outliers that are associated with the selected variable. 
- Mean Score Overall  – The selected variable's overall mean discrepancy score for all data points. 
- More Score Outliers  –  The mean discrepancy score for data points that are outliers in the selected variable. 
 In addition, when viewing error plots that apply Text Analysis or Text Versus Text Analysis, the y-axis label now displays as Discrepancy Score.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The high-level performance-related metrics summarize the variable's performance across all the error plot analyses for that variable. These metrics allow you to view and understand the overall variable's performance prior to drilling into the specific error plots. 
 Updating the y-axis label on text analysis plots  ensures a consistent look and feel across text analysis plots. 
## User Impact
 The high-level performance-related metrics on the  Error Plots page display  next to the plot list. 
 Text analysis plots and text versus text analysis plots display a y-axis labeled as Discrepancy Score.
## Special Considerations
 None.

- the error plot visualization filters to highlight only the specific data point you select. 
- the Summary table updates to display information only for the patient associated with the selected data point. The View By field reads Plot Point . 
 You can click the patient ID link in the Summary table to directly access the patient's profile in Medidata Patient Profiles.

For example, in the Summary table you select View By - Country , and Country - Japan , then click a data point and the patient ID link to view the patient data. Now when you click any white space within the error plot, all data points indicating patients in Japan appear highlighted, other data points remain disabled.

===== PAGE: event_analysis_includes_ae_action_taken_-_concomitant_medication_mapping_reference | Event Analysis Includes AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication Mapping Reference =====
## Event Analysis Includes AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication Mapping Reference
## What Is New?
 Detect Mapping's Event Analysis Mapping includes a new AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference. This reference enables you to configure the data sets and variables that Detect consumes to exclude adverse events that have been treated with concomitant medications in AI Data Reconciliation's analysis. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin 
## Workflow Process
 You must configure the AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference's data set and mapped variable for AI Data Reconciliation's analysis to exclude adverse events with concomitant medications. 
## Other Applications
 Configuring the AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference impacts the results produced in AI Data Reconciliation's analysis and reports.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Configuring AI Data Reconciliation to exclude adverse events that have been treated with concomitant medications produces better targeted report results that show only adverse events that were untreated with concomitant medications. Therefore, you can use AI Data Reconciliation's reports to better identify potential medical issues, malpractice, or instances of improper data collection in the study. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Detect Configuration Manager > Detect Mapping > Event Analysis tab > Event Analysis Mapping section, the Reference column now includes the AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference.
 You can select the data set and mapping variable that you want to configure for the AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following link to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
 Map Event Analysis Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
 The AE Action Taken - Concomitant Medication reference's Mapping Variable selection must be a binary variable. Otherwise, you must create and use a derived variable for the Mapped Variable selection.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: event_incidence_plot_improvements | Event Incidence Plot Improvements =====
## Event Incidence Plot Improvements
## Description
 The Event Incidence Plot page includes the following new feature:
- Event Incidence Summary – The Summary table lists all sites and countries with patient-reported events in the Event Incidence Plot visualization. The Summary table also summarizes key event incidence-related metrics with regards to each site and country. 
 The Event Incidence Plot page also includes the following new enhancements:
- View the Event Incidence Plot by Country  –  In previous Medidata Detect releases, you could only view event incidences at the site and study level. You can now additionally use the View By dropdown to filter the Event Incidence plot and Summary table to view patient-reported event terms at the country level. 
- Filter the Event Incidence Plot to Display Specific Reported Event Terms  – The new Select Term(s) dropdown enables you to filter the Event Incidence plot to display data for specific event terms at the site, country, and study level. 
## Affected Roles
- Central monitors 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 The Summary table allows you to:
- View in a tabular format the list of sites or countries with patient-reported events within the selected domain. 
- Sort by column to more easily find and analyze specific data of interest. 
 Filtering the Event Incidence Plot and Summary table by country:
- Helps you focus on and analyze patient-reported event data and trends at the country level. 
 Filtering the Event Incidence Plot and Summary table to display only specific event terms:
- Helps you focus on and analyze specific event terms of interest at the site, country, and study level. 
## User Impact
 The Summary table displays below the Event Incidence plot visualization.  From the Summary   table, you can: 
- View a list of sites or countries that have patient-reported event terms within a domain. 
- Sort by column to view and find data.
 Tip : Click to enlarge.
 The Event Incidence Plot includes the additional View by dropdown, which enables you to filter the Event Incidence plot to display reported event terms at the site or country level.
 The Event Incidence Plot also now includes a More Filters... link. When clicked, the following filters display:
- Select Term(s)  – Use this dropdown to select or enter one or more specific event terms whose data you want the Event Incidence Plot to filter for and display. 
- Study Level Threshold  – Existing functionality from previous releases. 
- Show Outlier Site Only  – Existing functionality from previous releases. 
 When filters are expanded, you can click the Less Filters... link to collapse the filters and return to the default view.
## Special Considerations
- The Event Incidence plot displays reported event terms within the selected domain at the site level by default. 
- The Summary table is filtered by the # Outlier Incidences column in descending order (highest to lower) by default.

- Study Designer

- All Configuration Management users.

## Other Applications
- AI Date Reconciliation   
- Detect CSM, specifically the Event Incidence and Under and Over Reporting features of Reporting Pattern Analysis.

- More detailed AI Data Reconciliation Analysis that further refines interactions between conditions, treatments, and histories 
- Improved reconciliation reports 
- Improved mapping workflow.

===== PAGE: expand_or_collapse_all_elements_when_viewing_a_patient_profile | Expand or Collapse All Elements When Viewing a Patient Profile =====
## Expand or Collapse All Elements When Viewing a Patient Profile
## Description
 In previous Patient Profiles Cloud releases, you could expand and collapse individual elements in a patient profile on the Design page > Profiles tab. Now you can expand or collapse all elements simultaneously.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Expanding or collapsing all elements in the profile viewer enhances your ability to scan data profile data. For example, some profiles may have many elements. Having all or many elements expanded requires more effort and potentially more page scrolling to find a particular element in the profile. Collapsing all elements improves your ability to find the element you need.
## User Impact
 The Design page > Profiles tab displays the Expand All button and Collapse All button below the section header and above the first element.
## Special Considerations
 Exported PDFs do not contain the Expand All and Collapse All functionality.
 In addition, when you export a patient profile to PDF, all elements always display as expanded.

## Feature Release Announcement Informs You of the Latest Release Details
## Description
 RBQM Configuration Manager 2021.2.0 introduces a feature release announcement. 
 The release announcement includes a brief description of the key features and enhancements in the newly released version of RBQM Configuration Manager. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The feature release announcement provides a quick overview of newly released features and enhancements with links to learn more in the product knowledge space. 
## User Impact
 The feature release announcement appears on login when you access RBQM Configuration Manager for the first time after the latest release. The message continues to appear until you click Got it! to dismiss the announcement or Remind Me in One Day to snooze the announcement for 24 hours.
 Note : The release announcement guide is only available for Feature Releases, and does not appear for Standard Software Update (SSU)  or Urgent Software Update (USU) .
## Special Considerations
 The feature release announcement appears automatically the first time you log in after a new feature release is pre-released (if applicable) and generally released (GA). The announcement remains available until dismissed, or for the entire duration of the pre-release cycle. The announcement remains available until dismissed or for a maximum of 4 weeks after the GA date. If you do not log in for 4 weeks after the GA release, you do not see the announcement. The announcement no longer appears if there is a subsequent SSU or USU within 4 weeks of the last feature release GA.

 On the Designs page > Profiles tab, when data is loading from a data set, you can use the   field in the Patient Selector table. 
- The Filter field is available only after all patient data loads into the Patient Selector table. 
- If you enter the first few digits of a Patient ID in the Filter field, the Patient Selector table shows the corresponding patient profiles that include patients with the Patient ID. The first patient with the ID shows at the top of the Patient Selector table. For example,  if you enter 1005, and click Enter or outside of  the Filter field, then the Patient Selector table loads profiles for patient IDs containing "1005", like 100501, 100523, 100528 in an ascending order. 
- If you enter most part of the Patient ID, then click the patient profile from the list in the Filter field, the Patient Selector table shows the corresponding patient profile. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: filter_scheduled_patient_visits_by_visit_name | Filter Scheduled Patient Visits By Visit Name =====
## Filter Scheduled Patient Visits By Visit Name
## Description
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) breaks down at the study, country, or patient-level the number of scheduled patient visits for each weekday throughout the study. You can now filter scheduled patient visits by visit name for any selected weekday. 
## Affected Roles
 Central monitors.
## Advantages
 By filtering scheduled patient visits, you can identify the type of visits easily and investigate specific visits, for example, visits that were recorded on weekends or holidays. Visits recorded as taking place on weekends or holidays may indicate potential fraud, misconduct or simple data entry errors by sites. Based on your findings, you can monitor sites of interest to determine any mitigating actions. 
## User Impact
 On the Medidata Detect > Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) module > Data Veracity > Weekend and Holiday Visits page, when you select a weekday, the list of patient visits and visit details recorded appear in the weekday table.
- If you select multiple sites, countries and a visit date, and one or multiple visit names, and then click Apply, the patient visits list shows visits that match the filter criteria. 
- If you do not select any option from the sites, countries, visit names or visit date fields and click Apply, no visits appear in the weekday table. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The CSM Knowledge Space provides the following updated content to support the enhancement: 
- Investigate Site Visits On Non-Business Days 
## Special Considerations
- You can view visit counts for countries or sites even if you do not have access to the sites or countries. 
- The visit filtering and exporting options become available only after data completely loads into CSM. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: filter_study_risks_by_sites_and_countries_in_the_key_risk_indicators_dashboard | Filter Study Risks By Sites And Countries In The Key Risk Indicators Dashboard =====
## Filter Study Risks By Sites And Countries In The Key Risk Indicators Dashboard
## Description 
 You can filter Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) tracked in your study and their respective KRI values by multiple sites or countries, and reposition KRI value columns in the KRIs Dashboard available on the Detect Landing Page. 
## Affected Roles
- Central Monitors 
- Study Managers 
- Site Monitors 
## Advantages
 You can use filters to:
- Locate, track, compare, and determine how risks evolve at the study for specific sites or countries. 
- CSM possible issues or risks that require mitigating actions. 
## User Impact 
 On the Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) > KRI Dashboard > Key Risk Indicators page, you can apply filters to columns in the Key Risk Indicators table. 
- If you select Country in the View By field and then select one or multiple countries in the Countries field, the Key Risk Indicators table shows KRIs by countries you select. The default view is by Site. Filters also appear under Categories and KRI dashboard fields. 
 Tip : Click image to enlarge. 
- If you select from the list and click Apply , the table shows KRIs value columns based on selected options. 
- If you enter three characters or digits in the field for Sites or Countries, Categories, or KRIs, the list shows data that includes the filter parameter. The filter response differs depending on the selected parameter. For example, if you enter 100 for Site, the list shows 1001, 1002, 1002, in this sequence. If you select sites from the list and then click Apply , the corresponding risk indicator categories and values appear. If you filter by one column and then by another, the first record that matches the filter parameters shows at the top of the Key Risk Indicators table. For example, you can filter by countries, than categories and then specific KRIs. 
- For KRI categories, dragging and dropping column headers allows you to reposition KRI value columns in the Key Risk Indicators table. You can hide all columns except the View By and Enrolled Patient Count columns.  
- If you scroll to the bottom of the Key Risk Indicators table, the updated color-coded risk thresholds text appears as follows: 
- Red* - Risk warrants prompt investigation and site follow up* to determine root cause for site's non-compliance. 
- Orange* - Risk warrants investigation to determine root cause for site's non-compliance. 
- Green - Site is likely operating and reporting data as expected. 
- Gray - Not enough reported data to determine risk level. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Centralized Statistical Monitoring (formerly Medidata Detect) Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support the KRI's Dashboard enhancement: 
- Investigate Data Using the Key Risk Indicators Table (Updated) 
## Special Considerations
- For authorized Issue Management users selecting a KRI value in the Key Risk Indicators table, the button appears to the upper right on the Key Risk Indicators page. 
- Centralized Statistical Monitoring does not perform site-level or country-level KRI analysis for studies with fewer than three sites or three countries. 
- If you do not select all the KRI values from a KRI category, the KRI category header does not appear in the Key Risk Indicators table along with the KRI values columns.

===== PAGE: find_and_add_data_sets_and_variables_faster_when_configuring_custom_qtls_and_percentage_kris | Find and Add Data Sets and Variables Faster When Configuring Custom QTLs and Percentage KRIs =====
## Find and Add Data Sets and Variables Faster When Configuring Custom QTLs and Percentage KRIs
## Description
 When you:
- Add or edit custom percentage KRIs on the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box, or 
- Add or edit custom QTLs on the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box 
 you can now p erform a keyword search in the: 
- Data Set list to filter for the list to show a specific data set. 
- Numerator Query and Denominator Query sections' Variable field to add a variable when building an expression. 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 Performing a keyword search and filtering the Data Set list and Variable field helps you build custom QTLs and percentage KRIs faster and easier.
## User Impact
 On the Custom Percentage KRI dialog box and Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box:
- The Data Sets list now contains a search field at the top of the list. 
- The Variable field in the Numerator Query section and Denominator Query section now provides the keyword search capability. 
- Each search field auto-populates with selectable, predictive search terms in real time as you enter your search text. Selecting a data set name in the Data Set list search field filters the list to show the selected data set. Selecting a data set name in the Numerator or Denominator Query sections' search field filters the search results to show variables existing in that data set. Selecting a variable in the Numerator or Denominator Query section's search field populates the Variable field with the selected variable name. You can also append a period to a data set name in your search text to trigger the search results to search for variables within that data set.

- Add and Edit Custom QTLs 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs

===== PAGE: flag__track__and_audit_reviewed_error_plot_outlier_data_points | Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Error Plot Outlier Data Points =====
## Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Error Plot Outlier Data Points
## Description
 After you review individual outlier data points on error plots, you can flag those data points as reviewed. You can also track which of a variable's outlier data points have or have not been reviewed on error plots. 
## Affected Roles
 Users with CSA Review permissions. 
## Advantages
 Flagging outlier data points as reviewed helps you and other team members identify which data has or has not been reviewed. 
 Knowing the review status of data points in your study prevents inadvertent, repeat review work and helps your team recognize and focus on the data that still requires review. You can also track previous users who reviewed specific data points and when those reviews occurred. 
## User Impact
 You can flag, track, and audit reviewed study data on the Error Plots page. To learn more, see  Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data .
## Special Considerations
 Reviewed data points are marked as unreviewed if those data points change due to an update to the study's source data.
