===== PAGE: flags_functionality_in_headers_restored | Flags Functionality In Headers Restored =====
## Flags Functionality In Headers Restored
## Description
 In Medidata Patient Profiles 2021.1.0, the flags functionality is reinstated for headers. You can now add available%KRIs as flags to headers in your profile design.  For example, when reviewing a patient's report, you can quickly see whether a patient died, had a serious adverse event (SAE) , and so on.  You build flag conditions using variables from any data set to create expressions.  Designs require at least one flag. 
## Affected Roles
- Unblinded Patient Profiles Designer 
- Blinded Patient Profiles Designer 
## Advantages
 Adding %KRIs as flags allow report reviewers to quickly gauge a patient's status and the study's progress. 
## User Impact
 When configuring headers for a profile design, on the Design page > Elements tab > Data: 
- Available %KRIs display as flags. 
- You can add and save available %KRIs as flags to headers. 
- You can remove flags from headers. 
- If KRIs do not exist as flags, a Please configure one or more Flags to use in your Header message displays under Flags. 
 On the Patient Profiles page: 
- If you select to display available %KRIs in the header, the %KRI displays in the header for a patient profile. 
- If you do not select available %KRIs to display in the header, the %KRIs do not display in the header for a patient profile. 
- If you select to display available %KRIs in the Patient Selector, the %KRI displays after the header variables in the Patient Selector for a patient profile. The %KRIs appear with a check mark and in red (default). 
- If you do not select available %KRIs to display in the Patient Selector, %KRIs do not display in the Patient Selector for a patient profile. 
## Special Considerations
 Headers are heavily weighted during the CSA analytics process. Therefore, we encourage you to use headers for information that CSA can analyze. For example, you do not want to add a Study Name variable to a header since the same variable applies across all subjects .

## Flexible Risk Categories and Risk Category Templates

 All.

- Human Subject Protection 
- Protocol Compliance 
- Staff and Facilities 
- Study File 
- Vendor 
- Informed Consent
 Note: The Risk Category Objective field is blank for each of these new categories. Ensure you add an objective when adding a risk category to your template or study.

For example, one category, named Technology may hold this objective: "Determine the technical competency required for a successful study." If you add another category and reuse the name, "Technology," you can enter different objective text.  Authorized users can associate as many questions as they want for reused risk categories.

 All.

## What Is New?
 If a QTL in your study breaches the preidentified data quality threshold or is considered an excursion, then you receive a notification in the Notification Center that at least one QTL has a status of Out of Range or Excursion. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 QTL Dashboards users that opt in to receive notifications through the Notification Center. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 While there is no direct UI impact, the notifications are sent through email, and also made available in the Medidata Notification Center.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can now receive notifications for all Detect Notification-enabled studies in which Detect determines that a QTL has become out of range of the data quality threshold or an excursion.

 You see the refresh notifications through email and also in the Medidata Notification Center.

 None.

===== PAGE: header_flags_display_on_profile_designs_and_profile_design_reports | Header Flags Display on Profile Designs and Profile Design Reports =====
## Header Flags Display on Profile Designs and Profile Design Reports
## Description
 Flags are conditional expressions that highlight important, high-level study information about patients. Profile designs show flags as headers if the study contains patient data corresponding to set flags. If patient data does not meet the set conditions, no flag information appears in the header. Profile design reports show flags in the header section of the patient's report if you set flags for a patient's profile. 
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Profile reviewers can use data matching set flags to quickly assess a patient's status  —  such as, whether a patient died or had a serious adverse event (SAE)  —  to determine the study's progress. 
## User Impact
- On the Design page > Profiles tab, when you select a patient in the Patient Selector, the Patient Profile tab shows flags in red in the header section if patient data matches set flags in the patient's profile design. 
- On the Design page > Elements tab, if you add header flags, then on the Reports page > Profile Design tab, flag information appears under the headers section on the profiles design report. If you do not set flags for a patient's profile, no flag information appears on the corresponding profile design report.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Patient Profiles Knowledge Space provides updated content to support this enhancement: 
- Add and Manage Flags 
- Add and Manage Headers 
 Special Considerations 
 Flags are heavily weighted during the CSA analytics process. Therefore, we encourage you to use flags for information that CSA can analyze. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: identify_and_track_study_risks_using_the_key_risk_indicators_table | Identify and Track Study Risks Using the Key Risk Indicators Table =====
## Identify and Track Study Risks Using the Key Risk Indicators Table
## Description
 You can view the key risk indicators (KRIs) being tracked in your study and their respective KRI values at each site or country from the Key Risk Indicators table. 
 The Key Risk Indicators table allows you to: 
- See all KRIs being tracked in your study and their respective KRI values at each site and country. 
- Determine which site's or country's KRI values are outliers and non-outliers. 
- Determine which   site's or country's   KRIs have surpassed the risk threshold. 
 Based on your observations made from the Key Risk Indicator table, you can determine: 
- The issues or risks that require further investigate or mitigation.  
- The best approach or mitigating actions to take on the issues or risks. 
- The effect the mitigating actions have made on the issues or risks over time. 
## Affected Roles
 Anyone who is assigned to track risks can use the Key Risk Indicators table. For example: 
- Data Quality  (Site, Country, or Data Manager)  – Might  look at abnormal trends in data, adherence to data entry instructions, or proactive discrepancy management.   For example, the manager might examine the number of queries and query response time. 
- Safety  (Medical Monitor)  –   Might be interested in the processing of safety information, non-serious adverse events (AEs), and serious adverse events (SAEs). 
- Subject  (Study, Country Managers)  – Might  refer to outliers in screen failure rate or trends in ratio of subjects. 
## Advantages
 The Key Risk Indicators table: 
- Provides a clear and consistent method of tracking and calculating known and anticipated risks to study data quality. 
- Allows you to track, compare, and determine how risks are evolving at the  study, site, and country levels. 
- Allows for rapid detection of possible issues or risks that may require mitigating actions. 
- Helps you determine any necessary mitigating actions to take on risks. 
- Allows you to see if areas of risk have improved over time after taking mitigating actions. 
- Helps ensure the study conduct operates as planned. 
- Improves decision making, data quality, and good clinical practice (GCP) compliance. 
## User Impact
 You can access the Key Risk Indicators table on the KRIs page. To learn more, see  KRIs .
## Special Considerations
 Medidata Detect does not perform site-level or country-level KRI analysis for studies with fewer than three sites or three countries, respectively.

===== PAGE: identify_potentially_falsified_visit_data_by_viewing_scheduled_patient_visits_that_occurred_on_non-business_days | Identify Potentially Falsified Visit Data By Viewing Scheduled Patient Visits That Occurred on Non-business Days =====
## Identify Potentially Falsified Visit Data By Viewing Scheduled Patient Visits That Occurred on Non-business Days
## Description
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) breaks down at the study or selected country level how many scheduled patient visits occurred on each weekday throughout the study. You can further view the complete list of scheduled patient visits recorded on a specific weekday and investigate visit details such as: 
- Site   – The site where the visit occurred. 
- Country   – The country where the visit occurred 
- Patient   – The patient ID of the patient who attended the visit. 
- Visit Name   – The type of visit, for example, an unscheduled visit. 
- Visit Date   – The date that the visit occurred. 
 Tip : You can filter the list of scheduled patient visits recorded on a weekday to show a specific date; for example, to determine how many visits occurred on a holiday. 
## Affected Roles
 Central monitors. 
## Advantages
 Scheduled patient visits typically do not occur on weekends or holidays. Visits recorded as taking place on weekends or holidays may indicate potential fraud, misconduct, or simple data entry errors by sites. Viewing the scheduled patient visits that occurred on weekends or holidays can help you investigate whether falsified or erroneous patient records exist in your study data. Based on your findings, you can monitor sites of interest to determine any mitigating actions.

===== PAGE: identify_sites_that_potentially_round_or_propagate_vital_sign_records | Identify Sites That Potentially Round or Propagate Vital Sign Records =====
## Identify Sites That Potentially Round or Propagate Vital Sign Records
## Description
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) analyzes a study's vital sign measurements recorded at each site for:
- Rounding – Detect identifies potentially rounded records in two ways:
- When your protocol calls for a vital sign's measurements to be recorded to a specific decimal value, but the records do not capture the decimal values in three or more consecutive visits. For example, if the protocol requires at each site visit that a patient's body temperature be recorded to the hundredth decimal value such as 100.25 degrees Fahrenheit, but the temperatures are recorded as 100, 98, 97. 
- When the last digit of a patient's recorded vital measurement ends in 0 or 5 in three or more consecutive visits. For example, a patient's recorded pulse is 90, 75, 80 in three consecutive visits. 
- Propagation – Detect identifies potentially propagated records when the same vital sign measurement is recorded for a patient in three or more consecutive site visits. For example, if a patient had a recorded blood pressure of 126/83 in three consecutive site visits. 
## Affected Roles
 Central monitors
## Advantages
 Since sites manually enter and collect vital signs, it is critical that sites follow protocol and record data accurately. Poor data could lead to major systemic issues in study conduct and could even compromise patient safely. 
 Rounding and propagation analysis helps you:
- Distinguish between reliable and potentially unreliable data in the vital signs collection case. 
- Identify and investigate sites that:
- May not be following the study protocol correctly. 
- May be falsifying or fabricating data. 
- May be performing misconduct in aspects of the trial outside of data collection. 
## User Impact
 In Medidata Detect > Centralized Statistical Monitoring > Data Veracity, you can click the new left-hand menu tab, Rounding & Propagation , to access the Rounding & Propagation page. The Rounding & Propagation page provides the following tabs:
- Rounding Events 
- Propagation Events 
 Each tab contains a heatmap. Each heatmap cell shows the percentage of a particular vital sign's records at each site that Detect identifies as being rounded or propagated. Deeper and more intense cell coloring indicates a higher percentage of vital records at the site that Detect identifies as being rounded or propagated . You can click any heatmap cell to view a line graph showing the recorded vital sign values for each patient visit at the site over time. Flatter lines indicate a higher likelihood of rounded or propagated data. 
 The Rounding Events tab and Propagation Events tab each contain a Summary table. The table lists per site for each vital sign the total number of rounded or propagated records against the total number of records.
 You can also click the View Side by Side tab for a stacked view of the Rounding Events heatmap on top of the Propagation Events heatmap. This helps you simultaneously compare both the rounding and propagated event analysis at a site.
 Tip : Click images to enlarge.
 Sites with Rounding Events Table 
 Sites with Propagation Events Table 
 | 
 | 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature: 
- Rounding and Propagation Analysis 
- Access and View Sites with Rounding and Propagation Events 
- Identify and Investigate Sites That Potentially Round or Propagate Vital Sign Records 
## Special Considerations
 A CSM Configuration admin user must first configure Rounding and Propagation to enable the Rounding & Propagation feature in CSM.

===== PAGE: impact_factor_scores_and_prioritizes_most_critical_study_data_quality_issues | Impact Factor Scores and Prioritizes Most Critical Study Data Quality Issues =====
## Impact Factor Scores and Prioritizes Most Critical Study Data Quality Issues
## Description
 The impact factor is a numeric score given to the most critical data quality issues affecting your study as identified by Detect. The impact factor quantifies the priority with which Detect's analyses of those data quality issues may require review. Detect calculates the impact factor based on a combination of the following  factors: 
- SDTM Weight –  A weight attributed to the issue based on SDTM domain.  
- Analysis Type –  Type of analysis performed on the issue; that is,error plot,event incidence plot, or KRI. 
- Extent of the Issue – The n umber of affected sites, patients, and data points affected by the issue. 
- Magnitude of the Issue –  Extremeness of the issue's outliers based on a discrepancy score of 0.0-8.0 . 
- Detect Weight – User-defined weight that may be used in the future. Default of 1 for every variable (optional). 
 The higher the impact factor, the greater impact the data quality issue has on your study's discrepancy score. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The impact factor helps you find, prioritize, and focus on reviewing and mitigating study data issues most impacting the quality your overall study.
## User Impact
 The Impact Factor displays on Overview page > Top Contributors sub-page > Contributors list > Impact Factor column.
 Tip : Click to enlarge.
## Special Considerations
 The Contributors list sorts by impact factor in descending order (highest to lowest value) by default.

===== PAGE: improved_percentage_kri_configuration_logic | Improved Percentage KRI Configuration Logic =====
## Improved Percentage KRI Configuration Logic
## Description
 Detect Configuration Manager 2022.1.0 introduces improved logic to configure complex expressions to compare KRIs for patients within a form, between forms and across multiple folders and forms. 
 Previously, a percentage  KRI  used a single expression, the AND operator and parenthesis to configure queries that looked for data in the same Rave folder and study data form. This method of calculation had limitations. You could not build complex sets of expressions and you could only configure KRIs that analyzed patients who matched at least one configured query.  
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Administrators.
## Advantages
 With the improved configuration logic, you can configure complex expressions to differentiate patients within a form, between forms and across multiple folders and forms.  
## User Impact
 You can build an expression using a single condition and the AND operator and parenthesis to configure percentage KRIs. On the Medidata Detect Landing Page > Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) module > KRI Configuration > Key Risk Indicators page: 
- The Preview section shows the complex expression 
- The complex expression passes on to analytics for further processing.

## Improved Support for Risk Reviews
## Description

## Affected Roles

## Advantages
 In the past, when creating a risk, you could not indicate the frequency of risk reviews, and there was a chance that review actions could be missed. With Risk Management 2022.2.0, extra fields for tracking risk reviews have been added to inform the reviewer of necessary actions.

- A Review Status filter appears at the top of the Risk Inventory page. You can filter by Closed, Due Soon, Reviewed, or Overdue. A color-coded pill icon shows the review status for each risk in the Risk Inventory: 
- Yellow - Due Soon . The Current Date is between Last Review Date and Target Review Date indicating the Risk Review is due soon.  
- Red - Overdue . The Current Date > Target Review Date indicating which Risk Review is overdue. 
- Green - Reviewed . The Last Review Date = Current Date indicating which Risks have been reviewed. 
- Gray - Closed . The Risk Status is closed. 
 When you select a Risk ID from the Risk Inventory, the Risk Review page opens where you can view or edit existing Risk Details, QTLs, KRIs, or Risk Mitigations.   
 Note : The Edit Risk page has been renamed Risk Review.
 From the Risk Review page, you can: 
- Add the Target Review Date and Review Status when reviewing or editing a risk associated to Critical Data, Critical Process, or Risk Categorization. 
- View who last reviewed the risk. Two new fields, Last Reviewed By and Mark Reviewed, work together to show review history for risks associated to Critical Data, Critical Processes, or Risk Categorization. The name of the person who last reviewed the risk and the date of the review action automatically populate the Last Reviewed By field when you click Mark Reviewed . 
- Add the Review Frequency while adding a new risk to Critical Data, Critical Process, or Risk Categorization. The system uses the Review Frequency to calculate when the target review date is approaching.  
- Add one or more actions to take when reviewing the risk. 
- View the Closed Date. You cannot manually edit this field. Instead, the date is automatically set to the Current date when the Risk Status value changes to Closed . The Closed Date appears on the Add Risk and Risk Review pages. When the Risk Status is Closed or Transferred, the Target Review Date is set to Not Applicable .
 Note : When a risk is closed or transferred, you can no longer edit fields on the Risk Review page except for Risk Status. If you reopen the risk by changing the Risk Status, you can edit the fields again.
## 
## Calculating the Target Review Date
 For new risks that have not yet been reviewed, the Target Review Date depends on the Entered date and the Review Frequency. Set both the Entered date and Review Frequency on the Risk Details tab when you add a new risk.
 Note : The Review Frequency field replaces the Last Risk Review Date on the Add Risk page. 
- Entered - The date you enter the new risk in Risk Management. 
- Review Frequency - The frequency of the risk review:
- Weekly - The Target Review Date is 7 days after the risk is entered. For example, if the risk is entered on February 1, then the Target Review Date is February 8. 
- Every Other Week - The Target Review Date is 14 days after the risk is entered. 
- Monthly - The Target Review Date is 30 days after the risk is entered. 
 Note: 30 days are added to the Entered date. For example, an Entered date of February 1 (in a non-leap year) shows a Target Review Date of March 2, that is, 30 days after the Entered date.
- Quarterly - The Target Review Date is 90 days after the risk is entered. 
 For existing risks , the Target Review Date is based on the Review Frequency and the Last Risk Review Date.
- Last Risk Review Date - Last date a risk was reviewed.  
 Note : The Last Risk Review Date appears as a column heading in the Risk Inventory. The dates are automatically updated when a risk is reviewed. In previous releases, you could enter a last Risk Review Date in the Add Risk page, but this field has been removed because it is not applicable for new risks. The Review Frequency field replaces the Last Risk Review Date on the Add Risk page in Risk Management 2022.2.0.
- Close Date - Date a risk was closed. For a closed risk, the Target Review Date shows Not Applicable .  
- For example, when the Review Frequency for an existing risk is set to:
- Weekly - The Target Review Date is 7 days after the Last Risk Reviewed Date. 
- Every Other Week - The Target Review Date is 14 days after the Last Risk Reviewed Date. 
- Monthly - The Target Review Date is 30 days after the Last Risk Reviewed Date.   
- Quarterly - The Target Review Date is 90 days after the Last Risk Reviewed Date. 
## Changes to Risk Details 
 When you click in the Add Risk column on the Critical Data, Critical Processes, or Risk Categorization pages, the Add Risk page appears. Here you can create a risk by editing data in these tabs: Risk Details, QTLs, KRIs, or Risk Mitigations. Risk Management 2022.2.0 modifies several fields in the Risk Details form to support a more structured review of risks: 
- Risk Name (Required) 
- Entered 
- Review Frequency (Required) - Options include Weekly, Every Other Week, Monthly, or Quarterly 
- Action Taken - you can add multiple actions for a risk 
- Notification 
- Review Date  
- Color coding to indicate status of risk 
- Marked Reviewed at bottom of page 
- Edit a risk. The Save button remains enabled while navigating from QTLs, KRIs, and Risk Mitigation to Risk Details. 
- The Last Risk Review Date field has been removed from the Risk Details form and is replaced by the Frequency column.

 The  Risk Management Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
- Navigate Risk Management as a Study User 
- Manage Risks from the Risk Inventory

===== PAGE: information_that_you_can_view_and_access_limited_to_data_from_your_site_and_country_assignments | Information That You Can View and Access Limited to Data from Your Site and Country Assignments =====
## Information That You Can View and Access Limited to Data from Your Site and Country Assignments
## Description
 In Detect, you can now only view and access information associated with the sites and countries to which you are assigned in Cloud Administration . Detect de-identifies information for sites and countries not assigned to you. 
 In addition, on the Overview page, you: 
- Cannot select, drill down on, and investigate sites and countries to which you are not assigned. 
- Can use the Assigned button to toggle the Countries perspective and Sites perspective to show: 
- Only countries or sites assigned to you. 
- All study sites and countries, but with unassigned items de-identified. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 In previous Medidata Detect releases, you could view and access all study data. However, depending on your role and responsibilities, not all data may require your attention or investigation. Therefore, when trying to find the data you needed to investigate, you could easily get lost in Detect by accessing and searching through data that did not apply to your needs.
 Now that Detect limits you to only data from your country and site assignments, your Detect workspace  displays only the exact data that you need to investigate. Therefore, you can much more effectively and efficiently focus only on the data you need without the risk and hassle of getting lost or distracted by data that is irrelevant to your role. This results in a streamlined workflow, leading you to produce faster, more accurate, and more effective data analyses. 
 In addition, limiting user access to only assigned country and site data strengthens data security by ensuring users see only the data they are meant to see. 
 Activating the Assigned button on the Overview page allows you to clean up your workspace to help you focus on the sites and countries assigned to you. Deactivating the Assigned button lets you assess how the discrepancy of your assigned sites and countries compares to all sites and countries in the study. 
## User Impact
 The fact that you can now only view and interact with information associated with the sites and countries assigned to you results in changes to the following pages: 
- On the Overview page: 
- You cannot select, drill down on, and investigate sites and countries to which you are not assigned. 
- You can activate the Assigned button above the Countries perspective and Sites perspective to show only countries or sites assigned to you .
- You can deactivate the Assigned button to show all study sites and countries. However, Detect de-identifies unassigned countries.
 Tip : Click to enlarge the images below. The top image shows the Assigned button activated, which displays only countries assigned to you. The bottom image shows the button deactivated, displaying all countries in the study.
- The Risk Categories, Domains, Countries, and Sites perspective labels depicts the number of aspects that Detect has identified as contributing to the perspective. For example, in the images above, Detect identifies a total of 23 countries as contributing to the Countries perspective.
 Note : Depending on your permissions, not all perspectives may display to you on the Overview page. To learn more, see  Role-based Permissions Now Determine the Pespectives You Can View and Access .
- On the Top Contributors page: 
- The Contributors list only displays sites and countries to which you are assigned. 
- On the Error Plots page: 
- Frequency distribution plots using text analysis or text versus text analysis only sum up text for data points associated with the sites or countries to which you are assigned. 
- Box-and-whisker plots  using numeric analysis  or numeric versus numeric analysis show all data points. However, the plot highlights only data points associated with the sites or countries to which you are assigned. All other data points are faded out.
- On the Error Plots page > Summary section:
- When you select View By >  Site , the Site dropdown displays only sites to which you are assigned. 
- When you select View By >  Country , the Country dropdown displays only countries to which you are assigned. However, if you are not assigned to any countries, then Country does not display as an option from the View By menu. 
- When you select View By >  Patient , the Patient  dropdown displays only patients that are in the sites or countries to which you are assigned. 
- When you select View By >  Data: Top 100 Outliers , the Patient  dropdown displays only data points for patients that are in the sites or countries to which you are assigned. 
- On the Event Incidence Plot page:
- All data points in the study display. However, the plot highlights only data points associated with the sites or countries to which you are assigned. All other data points are faded out. 
- You cannot click or hover your cursor to display more information on faded out data points. 
- When you select View By >  Site , the plot  displays only sites to which you are assigned. All other data points are faded out. 
- When you select View By >  Country , the plot  displays only countries to which you are assigned. All other data points are faded out. However, if you are not assigned to any countries, then Country does not display as an option from the View By menu. 
- If you click  ,  , or  , the panel on the right side de-identifies sites and countries to which you are not assigned. 
- The Summary section only displays sites and countries to which you are assigned. 
- On the KRIs page:
- When you select View By >  Site , the Key Risk Indicators table  displays only sites to which you are assigned. 
- When you select View By >  Country ,  the Key Risk Indicators table  displays only countries to which you are assigned.  However, if you are not assigned to any countries, then Country does not display as an option from the View By menu. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: insights__downloaded_open_query_records_report_includes_data_snapshot_timestamp | Insights: Downloaded Open Query Records Report Includes Data Snapshot Timestamp =====
## Insights: Downloaded Open Query Records Report Includes Data Snapshot Timestamp
## What Is New?
 The Open Queries download file now includes a timestamp showing the date and time of the data snapshot represented in the downloaded list of records. The data snapshot timestamp is formatted as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ5, where:
- YYYY – Year 
- MM – Month 
- DD – DD 
- T – Represents the word time. 
- HH – Hour 
- MM – Minute 
- SS – Second 
- Z5 – Eastern Time Zone 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 The data snapshot timestamp:
- Tells you how recent the data is for the records listed in the downloaded file. 
- Enables you to compare records from other Open Queries downloads with different data snapshot timestamps. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 You can find the timestamp when you go to Insights > Open Queries page > Open Query Records table, and then click the Download button and open the Open Queries .CSV file. The timestamp shows in Column B, Row 1. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- Download the Open Query Records List

===== PAGE: insights__outstanding_tasks_bar_graph_no_longer_charts_open_queries | Insights: Outstanding Tasks Bar Graph No Longer Charts Open Queries =====
## Insights: Outstanding Tasks Bar Graph No Longer Charts Open Queries
## What Is New?
 The Clean Patient Tracker > Outstanding Tasks section no longer charts open queries.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 The Outstanding Tasks section previously charted at the study level all:
- Open queries. 
- AI Data Reconciliation reports containing unreviewed records. 
- Data listings containing unreviewed records. 
 However, some studies may have an exceedingly large number of open queries compared to the number of unreviewed records in a given AI Data Reconciliation report or data listing. Therefore, the Outstanding Tasks bar chart > Open Queries bar would skew the graph and make it less readable. Removing open queries from the Outstanding Task bar chart makes the graph more readable.
 Also, the number of open queries shows in the metrics at the top of the Clean Patient Tracker page. Therefore, including the open queries count in the Outstanding Tasks section offered no benefit.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 You can see this enhancement in the Insights > Clean Patient Tracker page > Outstanding Tasks section. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this:
- Track and Clean Patient Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
 The Outstanding Tasks metric at the top of the Clean Patient Tracker also no longer includes the number of open queries in the count.

===== PAGE: integrate_your_designs_with_csa_patient_profiles | Integrate Your Designs With CSA Patient Profiles =====
## Integrate Your Designs With CSA Patient Profiles
## Description
 Patient Profiles integrates with CSA so that you can run CSA's data analytics on the data defined within the profile design to:
- identify issues, trends, and anomalies in your study data; and 
- view advanced report visualizations on your study data. 
 CSA is where the patient profiles with individual subject data is viewed.
 It is important to note that CSA uses your study environment's master design for analytics and to generate profiles. The first design created in your study is the master design by default. However, you can reassign master designs.
 After adding elements to your study design, you can adjust how CSA to analyzes data within specific elements when you run your profile design through CSA's analytics. For example, you can change element settings regarding categories, weights, tags, and so on.  When you add elements to your design, Patient Profiles automatically assigns default CSA settings.  After completing your profile design layout and before viewing the design report, we recommend that you review the CSA settings for your elements and update settings if necessary. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 On the Setting page > CSA tab, you can specify the following CSA settings based on element type:
 Flag 
- Category  –  Defines how CSA will apply weight to the flag during the analytics process. 
 Table 
- Short Name  –  You can apply short names to tables to make CSA reports less text-heavy and easier to read. The short name must be unique and can only be used for one element in your design. Entering a duplicate short name causes a system error. 
- SDTM Type  – Determines which category the CSA findings are tagged with in the CSA OneView table. 
- Stack Name  – Enter a name if you want to combine data from two tables to run through in CSA's analytics the data from two tables to be combined in the analytics, instead of being analyzed as 2 separate elements, the designer will add the same Merge Name to both elements. It does not affect the dislay of the 2 tables, only how it is analyzed. 
- Weight  – Determines which CSA findings display in the CSA OneView table. Typical values are between 0 and 3.5. Give more important tables weights greater than 1. 
- Merge Name  – Enter a name to combine data from two separate tables to run through CSA's analytics the data from two tables to be combined in the analytics. Merging data does not affect the display of the two tables, only CSA analyzes the data. 
- Instrumental  – Defines the element as not important to analytics because it is not reliable data or not valuable to analytics. For example, data collected for patient questionnaires. 
 Timeline 
- Short Name  – You can apply short names to tables to make CSA reports less text-heavy and easier to read. The short name must be unique and can only be used for one element in your design. Entering a duplicate short name causes a system error. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: introducing_clinical_data_studio | Introducing Clinical Data Studio =====
## Introducing Clinical Data Studio
## What Is New?
 Clinical Data Studio is a complete data management tool that provides access to integrated data from Medidata and external sources, using AI to streamline data aggregation, standardization, and management workflows. With Clinical Data Studio, clinical or IT programmers, clinical data management, and clinical operations roles can act on data instantly to reduce user burden, shorten operational timelines, and increase data quality.
 The software capabilities that comprised the former Medidata Detect solution are now part of Clinical Data Studio. Clinical Data Studio includes redesigned and rebranded Detect capabilities available as part of two offerings: Medidata Data Surveillance and Medidata Data Quality Management. 
- Medidata Data Surveillance – Includes the following capability suites:
- Data Surveillance – Provides a drag-and-drop listings builder, automated query generation for Rave EDC-sourced data and issue management for non-Medidata sourced data, AI-powered data reconciliation, patient profiles, and visualizations. Data Surveillance includes the following capabilities:
- Clean Patient Tracker 
- Data Sets 
- EDC Queries  
- Vendor Queries (formerly known as Vendor Issues) 
- Listings 
- AI Reconciliation 
- Patient Profiles 
- Visualizations 
- Oncology 
- Configuration 
- Library 
- Data Connect – Enables self-service data ingestion and no/low-code data transformation capabilities.  
- Medidata Data Quality Management – Includes all the Data Surveillance capabilities above, plus the RBQM capability suite, which provides risk surveillance capabilities supporting a holistic risk-based quality management (RBQM) approach to data quality. RBQM includes the following capabilities: 
- 
- Summary 
- Risk Assessment 
- Risks 
- KRIs 
- QTLs 
- Statistical Monitoring (formerly known as Detect CSM) 
- Configuration 
- Library 
 Tip : For former Medidata Detect users, to learn how Medidata Detect's features and functionalities have been redesigned and reorganized in Data Surveillance and RBQM, see the table describing the differences in the Where Do I See the Change section .
 Note : All your existing permissions in iMedidata and former Detect capabilities remain the same in Clinical Data Studio. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All Clinical Data Studio (CDS) users.
## Workflow Process
 See the Where Do I See the Change? section.
## Other Applications
 Clinical Data Studio also includes an offering, Data Connect , which enables you to import and transform data for use in Data Surveillance and RBQM. 
 Note : Some users may continue to upload study data through Ingestor for use and analysis in Clinical Data Studio. 
 How Do I Benefit? 
 With Clinical Data Studio. you can:
- Ingest any data quickly and easily – CDS provides access to data from Medidata data sources, such as Rave EDC and simplifies importing data from any external source, such as labs or another EDC system. You can configure data transfer agreements into CDS to validate ingested data automatically. 
- Transform Data with Minimal Effort – With Clinical Data Studio, clinical data managers can build complex listings across multiple datasets without the need for programming. Clinical programmers and biostatisticians can use Clinical Data Studio’s no/low-code data transformation capabilities to create custom datasets. Clinical Data Studio maintains complete traceability of all data transformations so you can always see what and how data transformed. 
- Achieve High-Quality Data Faster – Clinical Data Studio delivers accelerated review of data and patient profiles, visualizations, AI-assisted data reconciliation, risk management, site performance monitoring, issue management, anomaly detection, and patient safety overview. 
- The Medidata Advantage – Clinical Data Studio delivers a unified data management and analytics experience for all users, powered by AI and advanced analytics.

===== PAGE: kri_configuration_november_2022_minor_enhancements | KRI Configuration November 2022 Minor Enhancements =====
## KRI Configuration November 2022 Minor Enhancements
## Description
 When adding or editing a custom percentage KRI:
- Detect prevents you from saving the KRI with a name that already exists in your study. 
- Detect prevents you from saving the KRI if one or more fields in the Custom Numeric KRI dialog box or Custom Percentage KRI dialog box are incomplete. 
- The Save button remains disabled until you modify any field in the Custom Numeric KRI dialog box or Custom Percentage KRI dialog box. 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin
## Advantages
 The inability to create multiple custom percentage KRIs with the same name ensures that your KRI data and analysis is cleaner and easier to read and investigate.
 The KRI Dashboard functionality is more logical now that you are unable to s ave an unmodified custom numeric or percentage KRI. 
## User Impact
 When adding or editing a custom percentage KRI:
- If in the Percentage KRI's Name field you enter a KRI name that already exists in your study, and then you attempt to save, then the save attempt fails and you receive the following message: "A KRI with the same name already exists in the study." 
- If you do not enter or select information in one or more fields, Detect prevents you from saving, and a message displays below the incomplete fields instructing you on the required information. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this enhancement: 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs

 None.

===== PAGE: kri_dashboard__modification_rate_system_kri_highlights_sites_with_outlying_data_modification_rates | KRI Dashboard: Modification Rate System KRI Highlights Sites with Outlying Data Modification Rates =====
## KRI Dashboard: Modification Rate System KRI Highlights Sites with Outlying Data Modification Rates
 Important : 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the releases history . 
- For a summary of all features released, the released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | KRI Dashboard
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter :
 The KRI Dashboard now includes an additional system KRI called Modification Rate. The Modification Rate KRI calculates as:
- (The Total  Number of Data Point Modifications Made by Non-system Users Across All Study Data Sets) / (The Total Number of Data Points Across All Study Data Sets). 
 In other words, the Modification Rate KRI calculates the average number of non-system user (manual) modifications per data point. Clinical Data Studio uses a statistical model to calculate site risk based on the Modification Rate, and the KRI Dashboard color-codes each site KRI value to alert you to the KRI risk level: 
- Red** indicates that the KRI value at the site has an average quantile value of less than 5% or greater than 95% for a given KRI value. This means that there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site resulting in its KRI value to be an extreme outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site level. 
- Yellow* indicates that the KRI value at the site has an average quantile value between 5% and 15% or between 85% and 95% for a given KRI value. This means that there is a strong association indicating that there may be an underlying cause at the site resulting in its KRI value to be an outlier. The risk being monitored may warrant investigation at the site level. 
- Green indicates that the KRI value at the site has an average quantile value between 15% and 85% for a given KRI value. This suggests that there is nothing about the study data at the site that would raise alarm about the risk being monitored. The site is likely operating and reporting data as expected. 
- Gray indicates that there are fewer than two patients at the site, which is not enough data to determine risk level. 
 Benefit to Users 
 | The Modification Rate KRI helps you identify sites that disproportionately modify data more or less than other sites, and helps you:
- Gauge site-level data entry quality and transcription error rate 
- Determine sites that may require an adjustment to their source data verification (SDV) strategy. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Anyone who is assigned to track risks can use the Key Risk Indicators table such as CRAs or site users. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 No impact to the workflow process.
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact to other applications.
 Impact on Interface 
 The KRI Dashboard now includes the Modification Rate system KRI listed in the table by default under the Data Collection category.

===== PAGE: kri_dashboard__view_and_analyze_patient-level_impact_on_kri_values | KRI Dashboard: View and Analyze Patient-level Impact on KRI Values =====
## KRI Dashboard: View and Analyze Patient-level Impact on KRI Values
## What Is New?
 On the KRI Dashboard, when you click a KRI value for a site, and then click the Summary button, the Summary panel now includes a KRI Impact section. The KRI Impact section includes a table that lists all patients at the selected site and shows the following for each patient:
- For Percentage KRIs, the KRI Impact section calls out all patients that either do (True) or do (False) not meet the criteria set for that percentage KRI.
- For Numeric KRIs, the KRI Impact section lists the value for each patient ID based on the calculation type configured for that numeric KRI. 
- Calculations types can be: 
- Count 
- Count values 
- Mean 
- Rate 
- Rate values 
- For System KRIs, the KRI Impact section lists the value for each patient ID based on the calculation type configured for that system KRI. 
- The KRI Impact section only provides information about patients meeting the criteria for the following system KRIs by providing numeric values representing the percentages or numbers per month: 
- Number of SAEs per Patient-Month 
- Percent Out of Window Visit 
- Missing Visit Percentage 
- Number of AEs per Patient-Month. 
- The KRI Impact section not provide information about patients meeting the criteria for the following site-level, operational system KRIs: 
- AE Entry Delay 
- Manual Query Rate 
- Non-System Query Delay 
- System Query Delay 
- System Query Rate 
- Visit Entry Delay  
 You can then click patient IDs listed in the KRI Impact table to link to and directly access and review the patient profile for that patient ID.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Anyone who is assigned to track risks can use the Key Risk Indicators table. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 You can click a patient ID in the KRI Impact table to link to and directly access the patient profile for that patient ID.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can better assess the degree of impact a specific patient or group of patients are making on a site's KRI value and investigate root cause at the patient level.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 KRI Dashboard > Summary panel > KRI Impact table.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Investigate Data Using the KRI Dashboard

===== PAGE: listings__data_sets__kris_include_published_audit_datasets | Listings, Data Sets, KRIs Include Published Audit Datasets =====
## Listings, Data Sets, KRIs Include Published Audit Datasets
## What Is New?
 Clinical Data Studio now includes an audit trail review (ATR) capability. The Audit Trail Review (ATR) process examines the recorded history of transactions or activities within a system to ensure compliance with regulations, detect any discrepancies, and verify the integrity of data. This review  allows you to create meaningful datasets that contain all changes made to records, details of who made them, and when, providing a transparent and accountable record of system usage. ATR is crucial in ensuring accuracy in financial reporting, and supporting forensic investigations in cases of fraud or unauthorized access. The Audit Trail Review (ATR) feature in Clinical Data Studio applies Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI to explore complex audit data sets. Once you save and publish audit data sets, you can use them in   listings, data sets, and KRIs in your study. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to workflow process.
## Other Applications
 Audit Trail Review (ATR) pulls in operational metadata from Rave EDC to show edits, updates, and deletions made to data endpoints.   Clinical Data Studio uses Generative AI to automatically build customized queries, and executes them against the operational Rave data to generate meaningful audit data sets that facilitate data quality checks. The published data sets in ATR appear in KRIs, listings, and data sets.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can use audit data sets to build listings, and get audit-related data pertaining to a specific snapshot date into your study. You can use audit data sets in KRIs to track key study risks.
## Where Do I See the Change?
- In Data Surveillance > Data Sets, audit data sets appear in the left accordion with an audit label next to the name.  
- In Data Surveillance > Listings > New Listing, audit data sets appear in the Data sets tab to the left of the expression builder. You can drag and drop audit data sets into the expression builder. Audit data sets include an audit label next to the name. 
- On the RBQM > Configurations > KRIs > KRI Configurations tab, if you click Custom KRI and select either Percentage or Numeric, the KRI builder shows published audit data sets in the Data Sets field. You can then select an audit data set to build a custom KRI. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Data Sets 
- Listings 
- KRI Configuration 
## What Else Should I Know?
- When using audit data sets in Listings, the Submit Query functionality and cross-dataset listing creation remain disabled. 
- Audit data sets in KRIs do not permit cross-data sets. You cannot use audit trail data in a KRI with clinical data. 
- You can use only one audit data set per listing. 
- Audit data sets do not appear in Visualizations. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

 Benefit to Users 
 | On-demand and scheduled refreshes give data managers instant access to the latest study data, streamlining the entire data review and reconciliation process.
 Summary of User Impact

 Impact to Workflow Processes 
- Scheduled data refreshes operate on daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, bimonthly, and quarterly cadences . 
- Listings allow up to four successful refreshes per day per listing . 
- Scheduled or on-demand refreshes limit to a maximum of 15 listings in a single batch. 
- Conflict prevention rules block multiple on-demand refreshes for the same module on the same snapshot, and block on-demand refreshes while scheduled refreshes run .  
- You can export current refresh configurations into a downloadable PDF report through the Notification Center . 
 Impact to Applications 
- Listings included in Unified Scheduler refresh data independently. However, a record is available for selection in either a scheduled or on-demand refresh, not both. 
 Impact on Interface 
 On the Data Surveillance > Listings > Approved Listings tab, you can find the following updates.
 On-demand refreshes 
 Refresh – If you click the Refresh button on the top right corner of the page, you can select a maximum of 15 approved listings for an on-demand refresh. You can refresh any listing up to a maximum of 4 times per day. The On-demand refresh page does not show listings that currently have a refresh in progress, or are part of a scheduled refresh, or have been recently refreshed and have the most updated data snapshot. The Refresh button remains disabled if the listing uses the latest data snapshot.
 Note : Approved listings selected for a scheduled refresh are not available for on-demand refresh.
 Scheduled Refreshes 
 View Schedule – If you click  , More icon, next to the Refresh button on the top right corner of the Listings page > Approved Listings tab, and then click  View Schedule , the Unified Scheduler page shows all the approved listings refresh schedules. For more information, see  Data Surveillance Configuration: Schedule Data Refreshes Using Unified Scheduler . 
 Note : On the Data Surveillance > Listings page, if you select any approved listing, and then click  History , the page shows both on-demand and scheduled refreshes. The refresh table shows the following fields:
- Refresh Date 
- Refresh Type 
- Snapshot Date 
- Record Count 
- Refreshed By 
 Included in Scheduled Refreshes  – The Listings page includes a new Included in Scheduled Refreshes column, which shows a tick mark if an approved listing is part of a scheduled refresh. The Details page displays the current refresh status of any listing. It shows  In Progress while the listing refreshes, Refresh Successful when the refresh completes, and Refresh Failed if the refresh fails. For any approved listing, the last refreshed date and time in the user's local timezone appear under the page title. 
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
- Neither scheduled nor on-demand data refreshes interfere or break existing schedules.  
- For approved listings, records selected for a scheduled data refresh do not appear for selection in on-demand refreshes. The reverse is also true.

If you select a mix of listing records with different statuses using the All filter in the Listing table, you only have the option to mark records as Mark Reviewed. This prevents you from accidentally reversing a finalized record back to open status during a bulk action session. 
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 No existing data changes; no configuration or permission updates required.
 User Impact Assessment 
 | Medium

## Listings: Updated Data Set Variable Types Enable Better Listings and Query Submission Experience
## What Is New?
 Listings and Rave-enabled queries now maintain the correct integer, boolean, and float type data set variables in all operations, including listing previews, approved listings, query submissions, and listing results display. Listings also now include date time data set variables. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 With accurate data set variable classification and date time variables, data managers can build listings with greater flexibility ensuring study data integrity and accuracy.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the Data Surveillance > Listings page > if you click Create Listings , and select a dataset in the expression builder, for example, an audit dataset, datetime variables appear for selection. For date time variable formats supported in Data Surveillance and RBQM see Date Time Variable Formats . Date time variables include operations such as:
- Not Equals (`!=`) 
- Less than (<) 
- Greater than (>) 
- Less than equals to (<=) 
- Greater than equals to (<=) 
- Is Missing. 
- Is Not Missing. 
- Comparison between two date time variables. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Listings 
## What Else Should I Know?
 In the Listings expression builder:
- The Equal to ( =) operation is not available for date time variables. 
- The Enable Query option remains disabled if you select a queries dataset.

## Activate Your Medidata Account
 Access to iMedidata is by invitation only. As a new user, you cannot log in until you receive an email and click the link to accept the invitation to join iMedidata. You are then redirected to an activation web page where you create your username and password and register as an iMedidata user. 
 You can register, create a username and password, and accept the Terms of Use for up to 45 days after you receive an invitation.
 To learn more, see  How to Activate Your iMedidata Account .
## Log In to Medidata
 You can access iMedidata after you receive your email invitation and activate your iMedidata account .
- Enter  www.imedidata.com  in your browser address field.  
- Enter your username and password on the iMedidata login page.
Your Medidata homepage  appears. This  includes any assigned studies, study groups, app access, and eLearnings. 
 If you cannot log in to iMedidata, see Trouble Logging into iMedidata for help with resolving potential login issues.

===== PAGE: manage_data_set_variable_types_patient_profiles | Manage Data Set Variable Types Patient Profiles =====
## Manage Data Set Variable Types Patient Profiles
## Description
 Medidata Patient Profiles automatically defines the subject ID/patient ID variable for all data sets through the MEDS data standardization. We recommend that data managers parse through the data set to ensure all variables are coordinated with the appropriate data types. For example, if Patient Profiles defines a variable housing a date as a "Text" variable, then you can change the variable's data type to "Date."  
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Vetting variable data types optimizes:
- the efficiency in which CSA's analytics scan your study data; and 
- how the data displays in your profiles. 
## User Impact
 On the right side of the Settings page > Date Options tab, or any element work space, you can access variables by way of the data set accordion. From there, you can select a variable to change its data type.
## Special Considerations
 We recommend that you complete any data type changes prior to building elements.

===== PAGE: manage_date_settings_patient_profiles | Manage Date Settings Patient Profiles =====
## Manage Date Settings Patient Profiles
## Description
 Patient Profiles requires a reference point for a patient’s study participation, which is represented by the Day 0 Date. The Day 0 Date is when the patient officially meets the study eligibility criteria and gets enrolled into the study. In addition, you can provide additional details such as:
- Setting the lower time limit and upper time limit  that Patient Profiles pulls data for timelines or graphs relative to the Day 0 Date ;
- Setting the study start date to occur one day after the Day 0 Date; and
- Defining a variable in which CSA's analytics will use to cluster patients.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 See the Description section.
## User Impact
 On the right side of the Settings page > Date Options tab, you can:
- Define your study's Day 0 Date;
- Define the lower time limit and upper time limit from the Day 0 Date in which Patient Profiles pulls data for timelines or graphs; 
- Set the study start date to occur one day after the Day 0 Date; and
- Define a variable in which CSA's analytics will use to cluster patients.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: manually_refresh_data_in_individual_patient_profile_designs | Data Surveillance: Manually Refresh Data in Individual Patient Profile Designs =====
## Data Surveillance: Manually Refresh Data in Individual Patient Profile Designs
## What Is New?
 Prior to the Clinical Data Studio September 2024 release, all published patient profile designs would automatically refresh daily to show and reflect data based on the latest study data ingested by Data Surveillance. Now you can manually refresh individual patient profile designs to show and reflect data based on the latest study data ingested by Data Surveillance. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All.
## Workflow Process
 Important : Patient Profiles no longer performs automatic data refreshes. You must manually perform a data refresh on individual patient profile designs to show and reflect data based on the latest study data for that design. 
 Data Surveillance will produce the first data snapshot for all published designs as of the September 2024 release. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 In previous Patient Profiles releases, automatic daily data refreshes made it difficult to track and ascertain which patient profile design data was: 
- Never reviewed. 
- Reviewed and up to date. 
- Previously reviewed but now out of date due to post-review data changes. 
 Therefore, your team ran the risk of potentially reviewing the same data multiple times or overlooking data that required review.  
 Now, performing manual data refreshes on individual patient profile designs enables you to: 
- Control the data that you want to show for your patient profile designs. 
- Control the pace of your patient profile review cycles. 
- Gain clearer visibility and understanding of the data that: 
- Requires initial review. 
- Is reviewed and up to date. 
- Was previously reviewed but now requires rereview due to post-review data changes. 
 Therefore, conducting patient profile design reviews is now clearer, simpler, and more efficient. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles: when working on published designs, the Profiles tab now contains a  Refresh button above the Patient Selector section.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Refresh Designs to Reflect the Latest Available Study Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
 Patient profile designs may take several minutes or more to refresh depending on the design complexity and patient volume. 
 Tip : We recommend refreshing data for patient profile designs only when you need to see new data. For example, you might want to refresh a patient profile design to review data after a specific study milestone date. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: map_patient_milestone_data_points_for_third-party__fully_ingested_studies | Map Patient Milestone Data Points for Third-party, Fully Ingested Studies =====
## Map Patient Milestone Data Points for Third-party, Fully Ingested Studies
## What Is New?
 In Data Surveillance and RBQM, the Configuration > Data Mapping capability now includes the Patient Milestones tab > Patient Master Mapping table. The Patient Master Mapping table enables you to map data points from third-party studies whose study data is fully ingested through the Data Connect > Imports capability, so that Clinical Data Studio can identify the following milestone dates: 
- Patient Enrolled Date – Mapping Patient Enrolled Date data points enables Clinical Data Studio to analyze study data from third-party, fully ingested studies in the following capabilities: 
- KRI Dashboard 
- QTL Dashboard 
- Data Anomaly Detection 
- Event Incidence 
- Under-over Reporting 
- Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding and Propagation 
- Duplicate Patients 
- AI Data Reconciliation (specifically the Treatment Without Conditions report) 
- Clean Patient Tracker 
- Patient Informed Consent Date – Mapping Patient Informed Consent Date data points is not required for any Clinical Data Studio capability to analyze study data from third-party, fully ingested studies.  
- Patient Randomized Date – Mapping Patient Randomized Date data points enables Clinical Data Studio to analyze study data from third-party, fully ingested studies in the following capabilities:
- KRI Dashboard 
- QTL Dashboard 
- Data Anomaly Detection 
- Event Incidence 
- Under-over Reporting 
- Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding and Propagation 
- Duplicate Patients 
- AI Data Reconciliation (specifically the Treatment Without Conditions report) 
- Clean Patient Tracker 
- Patient Screening Date – Mapping Patient Screening Date data points is required to save the patient milestone mappings. However, mapping Patient Screening data points is not required for any Clinical Data Studio capability to analyze study data from third-party, fully ingested studies.  
 Note : For third-party, fully ingested studies, the following capabilities require Patient Enrolled Date or Patient Randomized Date to be mapped :
- KRI Dashboard 
- QTL Dashboard 
- Event Incidence 
- Under-over Reporting 
- Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding and Propagation 
- Duplicate Patients 
- Statistical Monitoring 
- AI Data Reconciliation (specifically the Treatment Without Conditions report) 
- Clean Patient Tracker 
 Clinical Data Studio factors in the mapped  Patient Enrolled Date or Patient Randomized Date —whichever is mapped— as the start date. The start date start date is taken as an indication for enrolled patients  on the study. The capabilities listed above require the defined start date in order to process the study data and properly generate and visualize their analyses. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Clinical Data Studio configuration administrators
## Workflow Process
 The current process of tagging data for Rave studies does not change. However, the ability to map patient milestone data in Clinical Data Studio now enables Clinical Data Studio's capabilities to process and run analysis on study data from third-party studies that are fully ingested from the Data Connect > Imports capability. 
## Other Applications
 If you map patient milestone data in the Patient Milestones tab > Patient Master Mapping table and your study contains data that is tagged in Rave, then the Clinical Data Studio patient milestone data mappings override the Rave taggings to identify Day 0 in Patient Profiles and Over-under Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 In previous Clinical Data Studio releases, Clinical Data Studio's capabilities could not perform study data analysis on third-party studies with fully ingested study data. Clinical Data Studio could only perform analysis on study data that had been tagged in Rave. Now, the ability to map patient milestones data in Clinical Data Studio enables you to run Clinical Data Studio's analysis on third-party study data that is fully ingested and incorporated into Clinical Data Studio outside of Rave by way of the Data Connect > Imports capability. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Data Surveillance and in RBQM, the Configuration capability > Data Mapping page includes the new Patient Milestones tab. The Patient Milestones tab includes the Patient Master Mapping table, which enables you to map the Data Set, Folder, and Mapped Variable for the following patient milestone dates: 
- Patient Enrolled Date 
- Patient Informed Consent Date 
- Patient Randomized Date 
- Patient Screening Date 
 Tip : Click image to enlarge.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Map Patient Milestone Data for Third-party, Fully Ingested Studies 
- Import External Data with Imports 
## What Else Should I Know?
- Mapping patient milestone data in the Patient Milestones tab > Patient Master Mapping table is not required for Rave studies whose study data is already tagged in Rave. 
- Mapping patient milestone data is required for third-party studies whose data is fully ingested through Data Connect > Imports in order for Clinical Data Studio to identify key milestone data points required to process and analyze the study data. 
- The calculation of system KRIs requires tagging study data in Rave. Clinical Data Studio cannot perform system KRI analysis on third-party, fully ingested study data. Patient Milestone Configuration does not enable for the mapping of data points required for system KRI analysis. 
- You cannot map patient milestone data in Clinical Data Studio until after the first time Clinical Data Studio successfully processes the study data. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: medidata_knowledge_hub_provides_a_centralized__transformative_product_content_experience | Medidata Knowledge Hub Provides a Centralized, Transformative Product Content Experience =====
## Medidata Knowledge Hub Provides a Centralized, Transformative Product Content Experience
## Description
 The Medidata Knowledge Hub is a new content experience that replaces the current Knowledge Spaces Help in Medidata Detect. The Knowledge Hub intends to unify all customer-facing product knowledge into a single self-service site to give you a streamlined, connected, and personalized interface. The Knowledge Hub allows you to fine-tune your search on certain parameters such as your role or what you are looking for related to your product. 
 The Knowledge Hub puts you, the Medidata user, front and center, and empowers you to self-serve through an innovative, best-in-class knowledge experience integrated with all Medidata products. You do not have to sift through multiple sources of information, but rather enjoy a unified experience, seamlessly integrated with your  product.  
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Knowledge Hub benefits include: 
- A user-friendly design that provides content from all sources in one site. 
- A faceted search that uses product features to refine your results using machine learning and a built-in taxonomy, which is global and consistent. 
- A personalized user experience that lets you define and save your own subset of the content. 
- A fully integrated on-screen user assistance, which gives you quicker time to resolution in a self-service support model.  
- A cross-platform workflow that helps you understand and go through the entire Knowledge Hub. 
## User Impact
 You access the new Knowledge Hub for Medidata Detect when you click:
- Help > Knowledge Space Home 
- Help > Page-level Help 
 When you enter the Knowledge Hub for the first time, you see a series of short tutorials to introduce this new, streamlined experience. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Knowledge Space contains no new updates. See the new Knowledge Hub at learn.medidata.com . It currently provides the same content as the Knowledge Spaces site and will be expanded with more content over time.
## Special Considerations
 As of 03 Apr 2023 , the Knowledge Hub will be the single source for product knowledge, and the Knowledge Spaces site will be shut down. Any saved links or bookmarks to pages on the Knowledge Spaces may no longer work. You can either: 
- Update your bookmarks, or 
- Use the new “My Collections” feature in the Knowledge Hub to create your own in-hub bookmarks, which you can organize into collections and share with colleagues.

===== PAGE: missing_data_in_elements_indicated_with_yellow_markers | Missing Data in Elements Indicated with Yellow Markers =====
## Missing Data in Elements Indicated with Yellow Markers
## Description
 When you copy a design to another study, Patient Profiles appends a yellow marker to elements with missing data variables, configurations, or settings. A warning message provides more information about the missing data.  
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Patient profile reviewers can: 
- Identify missing data from a copied design in the destination study. 
- Replace or remove missing variables, configurations, or settings. 
## User Impact
 For All Elements 
- On the Design page > Elements tab, a yellow marker appears for elements with missing variables, configurations, or settings. You can hover your cursor on the marker to read a message detailing the missing information.
- On the Design page > Elements tab > when working in Elements > TABLE OPTIONS > Conditional Options, a yellow marker appears for elements with missing variables, configurations, or settings. You can hover your cursor on the marker to read a message detailing the missing information.
 In Reports 
 On the Reports page > Profile Design tab: 
- Shows all the missing variables in Element Type, Element Name, Section Name, and Missing Variables columns at the top of the report. 
- A yellow marker   appears next to elements with missing variables, configurations, or settings. 
- Clicking Print will print a report with missing data. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Patient Profiles Knowledge Space provides the following updated content to support this feature: 
- Data Sets 
- Copy Designs To Different Studies 
- Add and Manage Elements 
- View Design Reports 
 Special Considerations 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: modifications_made_to_improve_data_integration_with_medidata_detect | Modifications Made To Improve Data Integration With Medidata Detect =====
## Modifications Made To Improve Data Integration With Medidata Detect
## Description
 Some functionalities have changed in Patient Profiles 2021.1.0 to improve data integration with Medidata Detect.  
## Affected Roles
 Medidata Detect users. 
## Advantages
 Authorized users can seamlessly access Patient Profiles from the Medidata Detect user interface to identify outliers or percentage key risk indicators in individual patient data. 
## User Impact
 Improved data integration allows authorized Medidata Detect users to access the following functionality in Medidata Patient Profiles from the Medidata Detect user interface. 
- On clicking a single patient ID, the Patient Selector and the corresponding patient's profile displays. 
- Selecting another patient ID from the Patient Selector displays the patient's profile. 
- You can export a single patient's profile or bulk export all patient profiles in a study. 
 Published master designs and unpublished draft designs display in Published Designs and Draft Designs tables respectively. The current master design appears at the top of the Published Designs table and can be copied, updated, and published as a new master. Master designs cannot be edited, but can be renamed or duplicated. 
 On the Patient Profile Designs page: 
- Two new tabs exist : Published Designs and Draft Designs . 
- The Published Designs table displays current and previous master designs. 
- Any new design that is not a master displays in the Draft Designs table. 
- By default, the Published Designs table lists the current master design at the top of the table. This table is sorted in the reverse chronological order. You can change this sorting order. 
- By default, the Draft Designs table lists draft designs with the latest draft design displayed at the top of the table. This table is sorted in the reverse chronological order. You can change this sorting order. 
- Both Published Designs and Draft Designs tables display data in Name , Privacy , Published Date , and Updated By columns. 
- The Draft Designs table displays a Create Design button that lets you create new designs.  
- If a master design is not yet set, the Published Designs table displays "A master design has not yet been setup" message. 
- If a master design has been set, the Published Designs table displays the current master design at the top, with a  (key) icon next to it indicating that it the master design. 
- If a new design is set as master, it displays at the top of the Published Designs table, with a  icon next to it. 
- To duplicate current and previous master designs, click   in the far right of the page, and then click Duplicate . You can rename a master design after duplicating. 
- If you set a new design as master, a warning message displays "Once a design is set as the master design, it can no longer be edited. Master designs can still be duplicated. Do you wish to continue?." You can click Set as Master Design to continue or click Cancel . Once a design is set as master, it becomes read-only. The Save button is disabled. 
- If you set an existing design in the Draft Designs table as master by clicking  in the far right of the page, and then clicking  Make Master , a warning message displays "Once a design is set as the master design, it can no longer be edited. Master designs can still be duplicated. Do you wish to continue?". Click Make Master to mark the design a master. Once a design is set as master, it becomes a read-only design. 
 Data you view in Patient Profiles by way of Detect aligns with the last snapshot date in Detect. Patient Profiles does not show any patient data added or modified after the last snapshot date. 
## Special Considerations
 None.
