## Modifications Made to Improve Integration with Other Medidata Products
## Description
 Some functionalities are no longer available in Patient Profiles 2020.1.0 to improve integration with other Medidata products. For more details on which areas of Patient Profiles are affected, see the User Impact section below.
## Affected Roles
 Patient Profiles Designer.
## Advantages
 Updating the Patient Profiles functionality ensures that you do not encounter patient profile design configurations that are now obsolete or will be re-implented in future releases. 
## User Impact
 The following functionality changes are made in Patient Profiles 2020.1.0:
- The Studies page is no longer available.
- On the Settings page:
- The CSA Settings tab no longer displays. 
- On the Settings page > Design Options tab:
- The data set accordion on the right side of the page no longer displays. 
- The Primary Day Zero Date section no longer displays. 
- The Secondary Day Zero Date section no longer displays. 
- The Add 1 to study days check box no longer displays. 
- The CSA Cluster Variable section no longer displays. 
- Only the Lower time limit field and Upper time limit field remain on the page. 
- On the Design page > Elements tab:
- The Add Element > Flag button no longer displays. 
- The Add Element > Table button no longer displays the Transposed Table option when clicked. 
- When working in any element type:
- The Settings option,  , no longer displays when you hover your cursor on a data set in the DATA OPTIONS tab. 
- When working in Headers: 
- The Flags data set accordion no longer displays in the list of data sets. 
- When working in Wide Tables:
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > General Options > Visit Name Column field no longer displays. 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Timeline Options > End Line for Ongoing Events at Last Date Available check box no longer displays. 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Timeline Options > Color options for functionality is always disabled. 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Graph Options > Red Border if Value Outside Shaded Range check box no longer displays. 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options section no longer displays. 
- When working in Patient Information Tables: 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab no longer displays. 
- When working in Timelines: 
- The Visit Variable section no longer displays. 
- The Drug Variable section no longer displays. 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab no longer displays. 
- On the Design page > Profiles tab: 
- The Day 0 reference no longer displays in the patient profile. 
- On the Report page > Profile Design tab, the Profile Design Report no longer displays the following information:
- CSA Settings formatting on any element 
- Primary Day 0 
- Secondary Day 0 
- Add 1 to study days 
- Cluster 
- Visit Column 
- End line 
- Red Border Outside Shaded Range 
- Drug Variables 
## Special Considerations
- Initially accessing Patient Profiles lands you on the Patient Profiles Design page instead of the Studies page. 
- You no longer must configure Day 0/1 for each study. The configuration is automatically identified by the system. 
- The CSA Settings page is no longer required as Medidata Detect (formerly known as CSA) has been decoupled from the Patient Profiles configuration.  
- Flags functionality no longer exists in Patient Profiles. Flag configuration will occur in a separate app in the future. 
- Transposed table functionality no longer exists in Patient Profiles.

===== PAGE: multiple_key_risk_indicators_for_a_risk | Multiple Key Risk Indicators for a Risk =====
## Multiple Key Risk Indicators for a Risk
## Description
 You can now associate Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) to a risk on a new KRIs tab   in the risk form. 
 A KRI is a  qualitative or quantitative metric that is used to monitor identified risk exposures over time.  KRIs are often associated with the operation and control of the clinical trial.  You can use KRIs to: 
- Identify and track known or anticipated risks to data quality. 
- Evaluate country and site performance in a study. 
- Ensure that study conduct operates as planned. 
## Affected Roles
 Study User.
## Advantages
 You can track one or multiple   KRIs when:
- Using Risk Management by itself. 
- Your deployment includes Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) Platform applications such as RBQM Configuration Manager and Medidata Detect. Configuration occurs in RBQM Configuration Manager. Metrics analysis occurs in Medidata Detect. 
## User Impact
 A KRIs tab appears on the risk form in Risk Management. Use this tab to add or edit KRIs associated to a risk.  You can track a KRI by creating a new KRI and manually entering a KRI Value from a third-party tool or vendor.  
 When configuring risks for a study, a list of system KRIs appears in the dropdown menu. 
 Note : System KRIs appear in the KRI dropdown menu whether Risk Management is deployed by itself or integrated with Medidata Detect. You cannot edit any system KRI fields in Risk Management. When Medidata Detect is integrated with Risk Management, Detect analyzes the data and populates the KRI Value field. Otherwise, the KRI Value field is blank
 The system KRIs include:   
- AE Entry Delay 
- Non-System Query Delay 
- Number of AEs per Subject-Year 
- Number of SAEs per Subject-Year 
- Percent Missing Visit 
- Percent Non-System Query 
- Percent Out of Window Visit 
- Percent System Query 
- Screen Failure Percentage 
- System Query Delay 
- Visit Entry Delay 
 For integrated deployments, both system and custom KRIs from Medidata Detect are available for selection in a dropdown menu on the KRIs tab of the risk form. The data analysis for the KRI occurs in Medidata Detect, so you cannot edit KRI Values directly in Risk Management . 
## Special Considerations
- Manual entry of data in the KRIs tab is available only when a user creates a new KRI in Risk Management. 
- The Medidata RBQM Metric Status shows either   Integrated or Not Available .  Integrated   appears when the KRI Value is populated by Medidata Detect.   Not Available   can appear when: 
- Your deployment does not include Medidata Detect. 
- The KRI Value analysis from Medidata Detect is unavailable. 
- For deployments that use RBQM Platform applications, check with your Medidata Detect data administrator to determine why KRI analysis data is not being pulled into Risk Management. The refresh of KRI analysis data in Risk Management occurs simultaneously with the refresh of Medidata Detect data. 
 Note : KRIs created within Risk Management are available for tracking only . KRIs created within Risk Management are not available for integration with RBQM Configuration Manager .

===== PAGE: multiple_quality_tolerance_limits_for_a_risk | Multiple Quality Tolerance Limits for a Risk =====
## Multiple Quality Tolerance Limits for a Risk
## Description
 You can now associate Quality Tolerance Limits (QTLs) to a risk on a new QTLs tab in the risk form. 
 A QTL is a study-level metric that indicates if a study parameter's reported data has breached a preidentified data quality threshold. QTLs target and monitor the greatest risks to study safety, conduct, performance, compliance, and data quality. QTLs that reach or exceed a threshold indicate that the QTL's target study parameter may warrant investigation and mitigation. 
## Affected Roles
 Study User.
## Advantages
 You can track one or multiple QTLs when:
- Using Risk Management by itself. 
- Your deployment includes Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) Platform applications such as Detect Configuration Manager and Medidata Detect. Configuration occurs in Detect Configuration Manager. Metrics analysis occurs in Medidata Detect. 
 When using RBQM Platform applications, you can associate QTLs that were configured using Detect Configuration Manager with a risk in Risk Management. Data analysis from Medidata Detect is then pulled into Risk Management for those QTLs.
## User Impact
 A QTLs tab appears on the risk form.  You can associate one or more QTLs with the risk. 
 For integrated deployments: 
- Create a QTL either in Risk Management or in Detect Configuration Manager. 
- Share a QTL created in Risk Management with Detect Configuration Manager.  
- Share a QTL created in Detect Configuration Manager with Risk Management. 
- Associate any of these QTLs with a risk on the risk form in Risk Management. 
 When the data administrator activates a QTL in the Detect Configuration Manager, Medidata Detect can perform calculations for the QTL. 
 The Actual Occurrence graphic shows the Observed value as an animated calculation for the QTL.  
## Special Considerations
- The Share QTL toggle is Off  by default when you create a new QTL in Risk Management.  Ensure that the Share QTL toggle is  On  if you want to share the QTL with Detect Configuration Manager. You can click the information icon  to confirm whether integration for a QTL is turned on. 
- When the Share QTL toggle is  On , it is on for every risk using that QTL. Switching the toggle to  Off  turns sharing off for every risk using that QTL.  
- A QTL created in Detect Configuration Manager must be activated in Detect Configuration Manager before it can appear in the dropdown menu in the Risk Management QTL tab. When activated, you can select the QTL to associate with a risk in Risk Management. After the QTL is activated, you can no longer edit certain fields in the Risk Management QTL tab. These fields are grayed out because data is pulled in from Detect Configuration Manager and Medidata Detect: Unit , Expectation , Actual Occurrence , Sides , Lower Tolerance Limit , Upper Tolerance Limit . 
- Medidata Detect provides analysis data to Risk Management after a QTL is activated in the Detect Configuration Manager. Check with your Medidata Detect data administrator to determine the frequency of the refresh cycle for analysis data sent to Risk Management. The refresh of QTL analysis data in Risk Management occurs simultaneously with the refresh of Medidata Detect data .

===== PAGE: new_operators_available_for_expression_builder | New Operators Available for Expression Builder =====
## New Operators Available for Expression Builder
## Description
 You can use the following new operators while building data set variables with the Expression Builder workflow: 
- one of  – Checks if the compared value matches with any of the values of the selected data set variable.  
- contains  – Checks if the compared value contains a substring from a selected data set variable values. 
 The new operators appear in the Derived Variables page's Operator tab.  In addition, the Operator tab now remains  available until you save the derived variable. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables building block. 
## Advantages
 With new operators available, you can configure derived variables to see the data you need and take appropriate action. 
## User Impact
 To create derived variables, you must select a combination of data set variables from the Derived Variables > Data Sets tab and operators from the Derived Variables > Operators tab.  
 You can only use the  one of  and the  contains  operators for IF-THEN-ELSE blocks. In addition, you can only apply the  contains operator to text-based data set variables.  When you add one of , then add Select in the following field, then Select automatically populates with a list of values of the respective data variable. You can select values by either typing ahead or selecting from the list and build a comparison expression. 
 When you add contains , you must add at least three characters from the values of the respective data variable in the following text field to complete the expression. The substring you enter is used for comparison. When you enter fewer than three characters, a "Comparison value you enter must have at least three characters ." appears.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The following article has been updated in the MEDS Data Viewer Knowledge Space to support this feature: 
- Create Derived Variable from Expression 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: new_qtl_configuration_requirements_and_validation_checks | New QTL Configuration Requirements and Validation Checks =====
## New QTL Configuration Requirements and Validation Checks
## Description
 When you add or edit custom QTLs on   the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box: 
- If you enter an existing QTL name in the Parameter field and then try to create the QTL, a prompt appears informing you that the name already exists in the study and you are unable to create. 
- The Save button is always enabled. 
- If you click Save before you address all required fields, a prompt appears below the corresponding incomplete fields. 
- When you modify QTLs, you must enter text in the Reason for Change field before saving. 
## Affected Roles

===== PAGE: patient_profiles__edit__delete__and_view_audit_history_of_patient_profile_comments | Patient Profiles: Edit, Delete, and View Audit History of Patient Profile Comments =====
## Patient Profiles: Edit, Delete, and View Audit History of Patient Profile Comments
## What Is New?
 When working in published patient profile designs, the patient-level review comment functionality now enables you to:
- Edit and delete existing comments. 
- View the audit trail history of each comment. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Patient profile designers.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Previously, you could only add comments to patient profiles. So if you submitted a comment, you had to create an altogether new comment to address typos, inaccuracies, or missing details or include more details. Now you can edit or delete existing comments as needed without creating a separate, new comment.
 The comment audit trail enables you to view the full detailed history of all comments and comment-related actions made within a patient profile design.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles, when working with published designs, the Profiles tab > Patient Selector table > Comments column shows a blue Comment Bubble   icon in the row of profiles with comments. When you click the Comment Bubble icon to view the Comments pane, you can:
- Click the More icon associated with one of your comments, and then click  Edit or Delete to edit or delete the comment. 
- Click the Clock   icon to view the comment's full audit trail history. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- Review and Export Patient Profiles 
## What Else Should I Know?
- Deleting a comment completely removes the comment from the design in the user interface. However, you can still find the comment's full historical details and updates in the audit trail history. 
- Comment actions take about 10 mins to reflect in the audit trail history. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: patient_profiles__get_newest_published_designs_data_using_on-demand_and_scheduled_refreshes | Patient Profiles: Get Newest Published Designs Data Using On-Demand And Scheduled Refreshes =====
## Patient Profiles: Get Newest Published Designs Data Using On-Demand And Scheduled Refreshes
 Important :
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the   released features index .
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Patient Profiles 
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 The Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles includes a refresh option where you can trigger on-demand or scheduled data refreshes You can further manage scheduled refreshes on the Unified Scheduler page.
 Benefit to Users 
 | Data managers can obtain the latest study data using on-demand and scheduled refreshes, and conduct study data review and reconciliation using the most recent data. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Data managers and study team members must possess both building blocks; capability-specific, and Unified Scheduler related, to view and manage data refresh schedules . 
 Data Surveillance Capability 
 Building Block Required 
 User Action pertaining to refresh schedules 
 | Unified Scheduler 
 | View Data Refresh Scheduler 
 | View  
 | Manage Data Refresh Scheduler 
 | Create or Edit 
 | Patient Profiles 
 | View Data Refresh Scheduler AND
View Patient Profiles 
 | View 
 | Manage Data Refresh Scheduler AND  
 Patient Profile Refreshes AND All site access 
 | Create or Edit 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
- Scheduled refreshes operate on daily, weekly, biweekly, monthly, bimonthly, and quarterly cadences . 
- Patient Profiles allow up to two successful refreshes per day . 
- Conflict prevention rules block multiple on-demand refreshes for the same module on the same snapshot, and block on-demand refreshes while scheduled refreshes run . That is, a record selected for a scheduled refresh is not available for on-demand refresh selection. 
- You can export current refresh configurations into a downloadable PDF report through the Notification Center . 
 Impact to Applications 
- Profile designs included in Unified Scheduler refresh data independently, however a record is available in either a scheduled or on-demand refresh, not both. 
 Impact on Interface 
 On the Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles > Published Designs tab, you can find the following updates.
 On-demand refreshes 
 Refresh – If you click the Refresh button on the top right corner of the page, you can select a published profile design for an on-demand refresh. You can refresh any patient profile design up to a maximum of 2 times per day. The Refresh button remains disabled if the patient profile design uses the latest data snapshot.
 Note : The On-demand refresh page does not show profile designs that currently have a refresh in progress, or are part of a scheduled refresh, or have been recently refreshed and have the most updated data snapshot.
 Scheduled Refreshes 
 View Refresh Schedule  – On the Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles page, if you click the  View Refresh Schedule button, the Unified Scheduler page appears, showing all Patient Profiles refresh schedules for published designs. For more information, see Data Surveillance Configuration: Schedule Data Refreshes Using Unified Scheduler .  
 Note : On the Data Surveillance > Patient Profiles page, you can select any published profile design. If you  click , More icon, and then History , the page shows both on-demand and scheduled refreshes. The refresh table shows the following fields: 
- Refresh Date 
- Refresh Type 
- Snapshot Date 
- Refreshed By 
 If you click Download, you can download the refresh history for the profile design.
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
- Neither scheduled nor on-demand data refreshes interfere or break existing schedules.  
- For patient profile designs, records selected for a scheduled data refresh do not appear for selection in on-demand refreshes. The reverse is also true.  
 User Impact Assessment 
 | High 
 Learning Resource Updates 
 | The following lists any new or added resources that support this change: 
- New Article: Unified Scheduler . 
- Updated Article: Refresh Patient Profile Designs .

 |

===== PAGE: patient_profiles_cloud_can_ingest_new_external_date_formats | Patient Profiles Cloud Can Ingest New External Date Formats =====
## Patient Profiles Cloud Can Ingest New External Date Formats
## Description
 Patient Profiles Cloud can properly ingest external data (data not entered from Rave) in the following formats:
- YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss 
- YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm 
- YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss 
- YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 If a patient profile designer creates an element with dates in any of the following formats:
- YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss 
- YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm 
- YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss 
- YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm 
 then Patient Profiles Cloud can handle and properly display the dates in the given format.
## User Impact
 None.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: patient_profiles_cloud_introduces_unblinded_and_blinded_user_role_permissions | Patient Profiles Cloud Introduces Unblinded and Blinded User Role Permissions =====
## Patient Profiles Cloud Introduces Unblinded and Blinded User Role Permissions
## Description
 In previous releases, Patient Profiles Cloud did not have a way of identifying which data was considered clinically unblinding. And as such, any patient profile designer who had access to Patient Profiles Cloud also had access to all data sets, including the unblinding data. In this scenario, depending on a designer's role in a sponsor's organization, there was the risk of an accidental unblinding incident, which could potentially nullify the results of the entire trial. Therefore, it was not always safe to run certain studies in Patient Profiles Cloud. And ideally, an organization should be able to safely run all studies on the same platform.
 To alleviate this issue and allow organizations to run all studies in Patient Profiles Cloud, Patient Profiles now provides four total users roles:
- Unblinded Patient Profile Designer 
- Blinded Patient Profile Designer 
- Unblinded Patient Profile Viewer 
- Blinded Patient Profile Viewer 
 Implementing unblinded and blinded users role permissions controls the types of actions users can and cannot perform in Patient Profiles Cloud, and which designs users can and cannot view.
 Note : Patient Profiles 2019.1.0 also includes a feature in which you can designate designs as unblinded or blinded .
 The table below illustrates the each user role's level of access and edit privileges:
 User Role 
 Can View Blinded Designs 
 Can View Unblinded Designs 
 Can Create Designs 
 Can Edit Designs 
 Can Mark Designs as Blinded or Unblinded 
 Additional Notes 
 | Unblinded Patient Profile Designer 
 | Yes 
 | Yes 
 | Yes 
 | Yes 
 | Yes 
 | Patient profile designers have unblinded permissions by default. 
 | Blinded Patient Profile Designer 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | Patient profile designers with blinded permissions cannot create or access designs in Patient Profiles Cloud.
 | Unblinded Patient Profile Viewer 
 | Yes 
 | Yes 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | -- 
 | Blinded Patient Profile Viewer 
 | Yes 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | No 
 | -- 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Implementing unblinded and blinded user roles ultimately protects blinded data within Patient Profiles Cloud. This enables organizations to confidently and safely run any study in Patient Profiles Cloud without running the risk of voiding the study.
## User Impact
 We now refer to the Patient Profile Designer role as the Unblinded Patient Profile Designer role. The available set of functionalities available to designers remains the same other than the ability to designate designs as unblinded or blinded .
 The Patient Profile Viewer role is now divided between the Unblinded Patient Profile Viewer role and the Blinded Patient Profile Viewer role. The set of available functionalities and the tasks that each role can perform remains the same. The only difference is that the Unblinded Patient Profile Viewer role can view all designs. And the Blinded Patient Profile Viewer role can only view blinded designs.
## Special Considerations
- Ensure that the appropriate unblinded or blinded permissions are assigned to you in Cloud Admin. If necessary, contact your Medidata representative. 
- If you are a patient profile designer and you cannot create or access designs in Patient Profiles Cloud, contact your Medidata representative. 
- If you are a blinded user and you try to access an unblinded design using a saved link, then you land on the Design List page and cannot access the design. This may occur if the study was previously designated as a blinded design and changed to unblinded.

===== PAGE: patient_profiles_clouds_adds_a_leading_zero_to_single-digit_dates | Patient Profiles Clouds Adds a Leading Zero to Single-Digit Dates =====
## Patient Profiles Clouds Adds a Leading Zero to Single-Digit Dates
## Description
 If someone enters the day or month portion of a date into Rave X with a single digit rather than two digits (for example, 2 May 2018 instead of 02 May 2018), then when Patient Profiles Cloud consumes that data, it automatically inserts a leading zero to begin the number. For example, Patient Profiles Cloud automatically turns 2 May 2018 into 02 May 2018.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Before Patient Profiles 2018.3.0, if someone entered the day or month portion of a date into Rave X with a single digit rather than two digits (for example, 2 May 2018 instead of 02 May 2018), then Patient Profiles Cloud did not recognize the patient's Day 0 Date. Therefore, that patient's profile would display empty graphs and timelines even though data was present for that patient in Patient Profiles Cloud.
 Now if someone enters the day or month portion of a date into Rave X with a single digit rather than two digits, Patient Profiles Cloud automatically inserts a leading zero in the digit. As a result, Patient Profiles can better handle data from Rave X to render graphs and timelines in profiles.
 In addition, the Design Page > Profiles tab > Patient Selector table always displays the day and month portion of a date with two digits.
## User Impact
 None.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: patient_profiles_displays_queries_in_study_data | Patient Profiles Displays Queries In Study Data =====
## Patient Profiles Displays Queries In Study Data
## Description
 On the Design page > Profiles tab, a new Patient Query tab shows the Rave queries raised for a selected patient in the study.  
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 By tracking queries in Patient Profiles, profile reviewers: 
- Need not follow up queries in Rave 
- Can review site responses within Patient Profiles, and 
- Monitor data accuracy by reviewing the query information for a patient. 
## User Impact
 When viewing the profile design for a selected patient from the Design page > Profiles tab > Patient Selector table: 
- On the Patient Profile tab 
- Clicking the   tab below the Patient Selector section shows the patient's profile. 
- Selecting another Patient ID in the Patient Selector table loads the profile information for the new patient. 
- On the Patient Query tab 
- If you click the   tab below the Patient Selector section, Rave queries raised for the patient show.  The list of queries appears as per the order in the Form  column. 
- If a query is opened in Rave, the  Action column reads Open , and the Answered Date , Answered Data , Answered Text , Answered User , Resolved User , Resolved Date columns are blank. 
- If a query is answered in Rave, the  Action column reads Answered , and the  Resolved User , Resolved Date columns are blank. 
- If a query is closed in Rave, the  Action column reads Closed , and the  Answered Date , Answered Data , Answered Text , Answered User , Resolved User , Resolved Date columns have relevant information.
- Clicking the  Patient Profile tab or the  Patient Query tab  allows you to switch between a patient's profile and query data, respectively. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The following articles have been created or updated in the Medidata Patient Profiles Knowledge Space to support this feature: 
- View Patient Query Data 
- Review and Export Patient Profiles 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: patient_profiles_provides_clearer_missing_variables_messaging | Patient Profiles Provides Clearer Missing Variables Messaging =====
## Patient Profiles Provides Clearer Missing Variables Messaging
## Description
 Patient Profiles 2022.2.0 provides clearer messaging for missing variables in copied elements in a study. 
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
The updated messages show the status of the data and prompt you to take appropriate action.
## User Impact
 When you copy an element to another study in the Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) module > Patient Profiles > Design page > Elements tab, Patient Profiles appends a yellow marker for elements with missing variables, configurations, or settings.  Tip: Click image to enlarge. 
 When you copy an element to another study in the Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) module > Patient Profiles > Design page > Elements tab > Table Options > General Options, Patient Profiles appends a yellow marker for missing variables used in the First Sort Column, Second Sort Column, or Third Sort Column. When you hover your cursor on the marker, a message alerts you that the variable does not exist in the table.

 None.

## Patient Profiles Releases History
 The following lists all Patient Profiles releases (starting with the initial release to up to the 2022.3.3 release) and the features and enhancements introduced in each. All Patient Profiles features and enhancements released after Medidata Patient Profiles 2022.3.3 are listed in the Clinical Data Studio Releases History .
 Code Continuity Across Releases
 Note : All Patient Profiles releases are cumulative. That is, each release or software update is built on the prior releases as noted in the release notes. For example, Software Update 2016.2.1 includes all of the release 2016.2.0 code, which in turn is based on the release 2016.1.0 code and so on. Any updates between releases or software updates (urgent or otherwise) are described in the release notes.

===== PAGE: patient_selector_table_includes_more_data_points_to_investigate_in_patient_profiles | Patient Selector Table Includes More Data Points to Investigate in Patient Profiles =====
## Patient Selector Table Includes More Data Points to Investigate in Patient Profiles
## Description
 In previous releases, the Patient Selector table on the Profiles tab only included the Patient ID column and Site ID column. Now the Patient Selector table includes individual sortable columns for each flag, header variable, and data set included in your profile design layout.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 You can search the Patient Selector table for specific flags, header variables, or data sets to identify patient profiles with specific data elements. Doing so allows you to quickly and easily validate if the design for those data elements is correct and displaying the desired results. You can then, if necessary, iteratively go back into the design to make adjustments and then view the profile again with the modified design against the subject data.
## User Impact
 See the Description section above.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: pds__add_and_manage_internal_review_comments_on_ai_data_reconciliation_report_records | PDS: Add and Manage Internal Review Comments on AI Data Reconciliation Report Records =====
## PDS: Add and Manage Internal Review Comments on AI Data Reconciliation Report Records
## What Is New?
 You can add comments directly on individual records that appear in any AI Data Reconciliation report. You can also: 
- View a record's comment history. 
- Edit and delete your own comments. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data Managers. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Comments enable you to share review notations with your study team. For example, you can comment on your rationale for marking a record as reviewed. Or you can communicate with others your intention to review a record once its query is closed.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) > AI Data Reconciliation: when viewing any report, you can c lick the More button, , in the row corresponding to a finding you want to comment on, and then click Comment . A Comments panel appears where you can enter and submit your comment. Afterwards, i n the row containing the finding, the Status column shows a Comment icon, . You can click a Comment icon to: 
- View the comment history and associated metadata. 
- Edit or delete your own comments. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- Review AI Data Reconciliation Report Findings 
## What Else Should I Know?
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: pds__add_columns_to_listings_without_defining_in_the_listing_expression | PDS: Add Columns to Listings Without Defining in the Listing Expression =====
## PDS: Add Columns to Listings Without Defining in the Listing Expression
## What Is New?
 When creating data listings, you configure conditional expressions to capture patient records within a specified variable or variable grouping that match a set of criteria. Data listings then produce a list of patients that have data records that meet the criteria set in the listing's conditional expression. The list of patients contains a data column for each variable defined in the expression and the corresponding data recorded for each patient in that variable. 
 Sometimes you may want a data listing's results to include a data column showing patient records for simple variables such as age or demographics. In previous Data Reviewer releases, you had to tediously define additional conditions in the listing's expression to configure the data listing results to include such data columns. 
 Now you can configure data listings to add data columns directly to the data listing results without having to build the columns in through the conditional expression. You can add multiple columns and delete columns as well. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All Data Reviewer users.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Adding data columns directly into data listings:
- Helps keep data listing conditional expressions simpler and cleaner. 
- Enables you to more easily add simple data columns—for example, age or demographics—to data listing results without building tedious arguments in the listing's conditional expression. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In the Data Reviewer > Data Listings page > New Listing window or Edit Listing window > Define Listing section, the Add Column toggle button shows on the right side. When you activate the Add Column button, the Add Column section shows beneath the Definite Listing column. In the Add column section, you select a data set and corresponding variable to add as a data column to the listing. You can click the Plus (+) icon to add more columns, or click the x icon to delete columns.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- View and Edit Approved Listings 
## What Else Should I Know?
- To ensure the data listings do not capture an overly large number of records, we recommend when adding columns that you use:
- Data sets that are already defined in the core data listing expression. 
- Single record per patient data sets, such as demographics. 
- You can use a maximum of ten different data sets in the Add Column section. 
- The data listing results show the added variable columns to the right of the variable columns included as part of data listing's conditional expression. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: pds__build_custom_study_data_visualizations_on_demand | PDS: Build Custom Study Data Visualizations On Demand =====
## PDS: Build Custom Study Data Visualizations On Demand
## What Is New?
 Visualizations is a Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) capability that enables you to chart the relationship between any combination of datasets on a single visual using real-time study data on demand. 
 You can plot study data in a bar chart, stacked bar chart, line chart, multiline chart, donut chart, or segmented donut chart. 
 You can create, view, edit, and delete study data visualizations. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All study team members.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Visualizations enables you to flexibly plot any study data you want to visualize, catering to your specific needs or area of interest depending on your study role. For example: 
- Medical monitors can view the number of adverse events per site.
- Site monitors can track patient enrollment rate.   
- Data managers can view missed visits or data entry delay. 
- CRAs can view, track, and compare patients records for pulse against blood pressure.  
- Study managers can see the number of nonrandomized patients in the study or track the number of study dropouts per month. 
 You can also conveniently view the data in whichever graphical rendering works best for that data—whether in a bar graph, stacked bar graph, line graph, or donut graph. 
 Graphically visualize study data relationships enables you to more effectively: 
- Gain a clearer understanding or perspective of the study data. 
- Identify study trends and patterns. 
- Track study performance. 
- Build and share reports or present on study data metrics using clear, visually appealing graphical renderings. 
 And you can create visualizations on your own anytime you want. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) module now includes a Visualizations tab in the left-hand navigation, which you can click to access the Visualizations page and its functionalities.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Visualizations 
## What Else Should I Know?
- For visualizations with a large amount of data, we recommend that you add chart filters to narrow your results. If the visualization you want to build experiences slow performance, we recommend that you refresh the page, use additional filters, and then regenerate the preview.
 Tip : For visualizations with many data points on the x-axis, we recommend using a bar graph.
- When selecting a date or text variable for a line chart's x- or y-axis, we highly recommend selecting an aggregation.
- If you do not select an aggregation for a text variable on the y-axis, then the line chart does not render. 
- If you do not select an aggregation for a date variable on the x-axis, then the line chart plots the data for every single day in the database.
 Note : Ideally, we recommend that you use date variables on the x-axis to create a timeline or visualize trends.
- When selecting any variable other than a date variable for the x-axis, if you select an aggregation, then you must select a color series. Otherwise, the chart does not render. 
- When building donut charts, we recommend selecting Percentage as the aggregation for optimal chart readability.
- The donut chart may not chart all patients in a data set if there are missing or incomplete patient records. 
- Saved visualizations update daily based on the latest study data snapshot processed by Data Reviewer. 
- The color palette in the Color Series is read-only. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: pds__build_data_listing_configurations_using_time_variables | PDS: Build Data Listing Configurations Using Time Variables =====
## PDS: Build Data Listing Configurations Using Time Variables
## What Is New?
 You can now build data listing configurations to include time variables.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All.
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 The time variable's comparator value format is based on how the variable is formatted in Rave EDC. For example, HH.NN. You must enter the comparator value based on the defined format in Rave EDC.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can build data listing configurations to monitor for assessments that your protocol specifies to occur in a set chronological order. For example, if a protocol calls for patients to get their blood taken after the first medication dosage, you can build a listing to monitor for patients who report getting their blood taken first. Therefore, you can better assess whether the site follows the study protocol correctly.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the Data Reviewer > Data Listings page, on the New Listing window or Edit Listing window > Define Listing section, you can enter or select time variables along with the associated comparator and comparator value.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement.
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- View and Edit Approved Listings 
## What Else Should I Know?
 To preview data listings containing time variables, you must enter time variables in the data listing's conditional expression using the following 12- or 24-hour format: 
- 12-hour Format – HH:nn am/PM 
- 24-hour Format – HH:nn. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: pds__build_data_listings_to_identify_records_present_in_rave_edc_but_missing_from_external_lab_data | PDS: Build Data Listings to Identify Records Present in Rave EDC But Missing from External Lab Data =====
## PDS: Build Data Listings to Identify Records Present in Rave EDC But Missing from External Lab Data
## What Is New?
 You can build data listings to identify and report patient records that exist in Rave EDC but are missing from external lab data. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can very quickly and easily reconcile Rave EDC data and external lab data to accurately identify missing lab data. You can then create vendor issues directly from the data listing results to communicate data issues and queries with vendors. This helps ensure that you account for and acquire the lab data you need for your study.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 In the Data Reviewer > Data Listings page > New Listing window or Edit Listing window > Define Listing section, the   Missing Records   toggle button shows on the right side. When you activate the Missing Records button, the   Missing Records   section shows beneath the Definite Listing column. In the Missing Records section, you can build conditional expressions defining the source target datasets and the external datasets you want the data listing to search, compare, and report on. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this enhancement:
- View, Create, and Edit Draft Listings 
- View and Edit Approved Listings 
## What Else Should I Know?
 In the Missing Records section:
- The data set on the left side of the conditional expression must be the source data set; typically the data from Rave EDC. The data set on the right side of the expression must be the target data set; typically external data from the lab. 
- The source data set and the target data set must be the same data type. 
- The list of available source datasets that you can select only include data sets currently used in the core data listing expression. 
- You can only select "=" as the comparator. 
- You can only select AND when building multiconditional missing records expressions. 
- When building multiconditional missing records expressions, the list of target data sets that you can select only includes the data set currently used in the original missing records expression. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: pds__conditions_without_treatments_report_indicates_actions_taken | PDS: Conditions Without Treatments Report Indicates Actions Taken =====
## PDS: Conditions Without Treatments Report Indicates Actions Taken
## What Is New?
 In AI Data Reconciliation, the Conditions without Treatments report now includes the following columns:
- ACTION TAKEN CM – A check mark indicates that the patient took a concomitant medication.  
- ACTION TAKEN CP – A check mark indicates that the patient underwent a concomitant procedure. 
## What Is the Impact?

===== PAGE: pds__download_listings_table_from_the_listings_manager | PDS: Download Listings Table from the Listings Manager =====
## PDS: Download Listings Table from the Listings Manager
## What Is New?
 You can download the Listing Manager page > Listings table locally as a CSV file. The Listings Manager CSV file contains the following details: 
- Name – The listing's object identifier (OID). 
- Expression – The data listing's user-defined conditional expression, which Data Reviewer runs against your study data to capture the patient records within a specified variable that match the expression's defined specifications. In general, expressions are built to identify and report high-risk data points that your study team can review and investigate as necessary. 
- Created By – The user who created the listing. 
- Created – The listing's creation date is formatted as: DD MON YYYY 
- Updated by – The user who most recently updated the listing. 
- Last Updated – The data listing's creation date or when the last saved edit occurred. The date is formatted as: DD MON YYYY 
- Rave Enabled – Shows either True or False. True  indicates that the listing is configured so that users can directly within Data Reviewer view and submit Rave queries on the patient records captured by the data listing . 
- Status – Shows either Draft or Approved. The status indicates whether the listing is in approved or draft status. 
- Activated – Shows either Yes or No. Yes indicates that the listing currently shows in its Approved Listings table or Draft Listings table. No indicates that the listing is currently hidden from the Approved Listings table or Draft Listings table.  
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers
## Workflow Process
 No impact to the workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
   Downloading the Listings table enables you to: 
- Review the listings and associated listing details in your study outside the Data Reviewer application. 
- Easily exchange the Listings table externally with stakeholders to facilitate communication. 
- Locally save and archive the Listings table. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Data Reviewer > Listings Manager page now includes a Download button above the Listings table. You can click the Download button to download the Listings table as a CSV file to your browser. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Download the Listings Table 
## What Else Should I Know?
 The downloaded CSV file always includes all listings included in your study, regardless of the table filters set on the Listings Manager page at the time of download.

## PDS: Report External Data Issues and Track with Vendor Issue Sets
## What Is New?
 Patient Data Surveillance includes a new Vendor Issues capability that tracks, flags, and monitors external vendor data issues from within Detect. You can use Vendor Issues to:
- Communicate discrepancies identified during data reconciliation with third-party vendors. 
- Build vendor issue sets to relay queries and issues. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Study Managers and Data Managers.
 All Detect users with Submit Vendor Issues and Manage Issue Sets access. 
## Workflow Process
 On the Data Listings page, when reviewing the list of records identified in a data listing, you can report issues with specific records directly to vendors. Vendor issues created in the Data Listings page then populate in the Vendor Issues page. You can then submit, track and manage vendor issues on the Vendor Issues page. Once the vendor addresses the issue, you can mark the record as reviewed on the Data Listings page. 
## Other Applications

## How Do I Benefit?

- Acts as a bridge to relay queries and issues between vendors and Detect users. 
- Provides seamless communication of discrepancies and inconsistencies with vendors. 
- Builds an easily downloadable and shareable vendor issue set, ready for vendor consumption and action. 
- Facilitates faster reconciliation of RAVE EDC and external vendor data. 
- Saves time and effort by integrating into your data review process within Detect.

- You can mark records as reviewed or unreviewed, based on vendor responses received.

===== PAGE: pds__track_patient_tumor_burden_data_with_the_recist_1_1__dashboard | PDS: Track Patient Tumor Burden Data with The RECIST 1.1 Dashboard =====
## PDS: Track Patient Tumor Burden Data with The RECIST 1.1 Dashboard
## What Is New?
 Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) v1.1 is the standard criteria used to evaluate treatment outcomes of solid tumors in oncology studies. For more details on RECIST 1.1, see  RECIST 1.1 . Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) includes an interactive   RECIST 1.1 dashboard that visualizes, classifies, and lists the tumor burden change for patients in Oncology studies. You can use the RECIST 1.1 dashboard to: 
- Track tumor burden change for all patients for a specific scan visit.
- Track tumor burden for individual patients in a study. 
- Compare tumor response measurements with site entered response details. 
- View visualizations of tumor burden, tumor burden response, and scan visit information. 
- Identify discrepancies in tumor measurements.  
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Study Managers, Medical Monitors, and Data Managers.
 All Detect users with View Oncology Analytics and Detect Oncology Reviewer access.
## Workflow Process
 RECIST 1.1 consumes study data from Rave EDC, visualizes and lists: 
- Tumor burden percentage change at specific visits, and over time. 
- A summary count of total patients, and patients in Complete Response (CR), Stable Disease (SD), Partial Response (PR), Progressive Disease (PD), and Not Evaluable /Not Applicable (NE/NA|) stages in a study. 
- Tumor burden response by patient per scan visit type. 
## Other Applications
 The RECIST 1.1 dashboard works only if you configure data sets and variables in Medidata Detect > Configuration and Reporting > Detect Mapping > Oncology Mapping > RECIST. Source and target variables you configure in Oncology Mapping populate the RECIST 1.1 dashboard and the tumor burden response by patient table. For more information, see  Configuration and Reporting: Map Data Set and Variables for the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard .
## How Do I Benefit?
 RECIST 1.1:
- Quantifies tumor burden and outcome calculations for patients. 
- Summarizes the total count of patients, and those in various stages of treatment response at the selected scan visit type and site. 
- Tracks tumor burden over a period of time and identifies discrepant records. 
- Assists data managers in assessing the accuracy of RECIST 1.1 calculations and safety monitoring. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 Patient Data Surveillance (PDS) in Medidata Detect includes a new Oncology Analytics tab in the left-hand navigation, which you can click to view the RECIST 1.1 Dashboard.

===== PAGE: pds__view_and_use_stacked_datasets_in_data_reviewer | PDS: View and Use Stacked Datasets in Data Reviewer =====
## PDS: View and Use Stacked Datasets in Data Reviewer
## What Is New?
 Your study team can now merge datasets with common variables into one dataset called a stacked dataset . You can view and use stacked datasets on the: 
- Data Reviewer > Data Sets page 
- Data Reviewer > Data Listings page 
- Data Reviewer > Visualizations page 
- Patient Profiles > Design page 
- Configuration and Reporting > Detect Mapping 
- Configuration and Reporting > QTL Configuration 
- Configuration and Reporting > KRI Configuration 
- Configuration and Reporting > Derived Variables 
- Configuration and Reporting > Oncology Mapping 
 Note, though, that on the: 
- Data Reviewer > Data Sets page 
- Data Reviewer > Data Listings page 
- Data Reviewer > Visualizations page 
- Configuration and Reporting > Derived Variables page 
 the list of available data sets that you can sort through and select from append stacked data set names with the green DERIVED icon. No other pages use the green DERIVED icon. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers
## Workflow Process
 No impact to other applications.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Stacked datasets:
- Simplifies the organization of your study data. 
- Enables you to review your study data, create data listings, and create derived variables faster and easier by streamlining the datasets you must access, review, and work with. 
- Optimizes the statistical analysis and visual outputs that  Visualizations and AI Data Reconciliation report produce on your study data to be as clean and accurate as possible. 
 The green Derived icon helps you scan your study data and recognize which datasets are stacked to help you better determine which datasets you want to access, review, and work with.

===== PAGE: percentage_kri_configuration_risk_threshold_edit_checks | Percentage KRI Configuration Risk Threshold Edit Checks =====
## Percentage KRI Configuration Risk Threshold Edit Checks
## Description
 When creating or modifying a percentage KRI, KRI Configuration prompts an error message if you try to enter an integer between 1-100 or a noninteger for Moderate Risk Threshold and High Risk Threshold.
## Affected Roles
 Users with Manage KRI Configuration permissions. 
## Advantages
 Entering only integers between 1-100 for Moderate Risk Threshold and High Risk Threshold maintains consistency between the functionality for QTL Configuration and improves system stability.
## User Impact
 In the Detect Configuration Manager > KRI Configuration > Custom Percentage KRI dialog, if you select User Defined from the Threshold Type field, then the Moderate Risk Threshold and High Risk Threshold fields appear. The Moderate Risk Threshold and High Risk Threshold fields include two enhancements:
- Each field contains the following instructional text: "Enter integer value from 1-100" 
- If you enter a value outside of the range of 1-100 or if you enter a noninteger value, then Detect prompts an error message.  
## Knowledge Hub Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Hub provides new and updated content to support this enhancement: 
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: profile_designs_marked_as_master_become_read-only | Profile Designs Marked As Master Become Read-only =====
## Profile Designs Marked As Master Become Read-only
## Description
 The first design created in a study is no longer the master design by default. A study can have multiple master designs. The master design with the most recent time stamp is the current (active) master. The patient profiles data are based on the active master design. Patient profile designs marked as a master design for a specific date become read-only. 
## Affected Roles
 Patient Profile Designers. 
## Advantages
 Marking patient profiles designs as master for a specific date allows Medidata Detect users to keep a historic record of current and previous master designs with active dates. Therefore, Medidata Detect users can view data in a master profile design corresponding to a specific date. 
## User Impact
 On the Patient Profiles Designs page: 
 A new patient profile design: 
- Does not save as a master design by default. 
- Appears in the  Draft Designs  table. 
 An existing profile design displays the Published Date column header in replace of Last Updated. 
 A new or existing patient profile design marked as master: 
- Displays the date when the profile design was marked as master in the  Published Date  column. 
- Becomes read-only. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: protocol_integrity_report__protocol_integrity_report_now_available | Protocol Integrity Report: Protocol Integrity Report Now Available =====
## Protocol Integrity Report: Protocol Integrity Report Now Available
 Important :
- To learn more about changes done to these release notes, see the revision history . 
- To learn more about features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the releases history . 
- To learn more about all features in this release, see the released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.3.0
 Change Type 
 | Feature (New Functionality) 
 Functionality or Module 
 | RBQM > Protocol Integrity Report
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter :
 The Protocol Integrity Report (PIR) centralizes and automates the tracking of protocol deviations . It aggregates deviations from Rave EDC queries, clinical data listings, and manual entries into a single dashboard . PIR uses the Protocol Deviation Assessment Plan (PDAP) to categorize deviations . 
 Benefit to Users 
 | PIR replaces manual tracking and categorization . It aligns deviations with the PDAP to ensure consistent data and regulatory compliance . It provides a review and approval workflow with an audit trail and detects duplicate deviations. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 The change impacts users assigned the View Protocol Deviation or Manage Protocol Deviation roles. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 The protocol deviation workflow moves from manual tracking to an automated process . Users review deviations in the Proposed, In Review, and Confirmed statuses, and finalize them as Approved or Dismissed. 
 Impact to Applications 
 PIR integrates with Rave EDC to import Answered or Closed queries prefixed with terms like PD or Potential PD . PIR also integrates with Listings to import flagged records. 
 Impact on Interface 
 A new Protocol Integrity Report dashboard is available in RBQM . A new Protocol Deviation Assessment Plan configuration is available in Plan Documents. 
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 You must configure and publish a PDAP to map protocol deviations . You must configure Rave EDC queries with specific prefixes to enable automatic identification . 
 User Impact Assessment 
 | High 
 Learning Resource Updates 
 | 
 The following lists any new or added resources that support this change:
- Updated Article:  About RBQM 
- Updated Article:  RBQM Building Blocks and Permissions 
- Updated Article: Access, View, and Create Plan Documents 
- New Article: Protocol Integrity Report 
 Special Considerations 
 | For Plan Documents :
- You can only edit the plan under the Draft version. 
- Only the most recent plan will be retained as the active plan document whether it is in Draft status or Published status. Any older versions of it will be archived. However, all other older plans will be removed from the interface. 
- Users can only have one draft and one published plan at a time, and the one they have most recently worked on is treated as the final plan document. 
 For Protocol Integrity Report (PIR) :
- PIR automatically populates the Category, Impact on Data, and Classification fields based on the PDAP . 
- You cannot edit these fields in PIR . 
- PIR automatically marks records submitted from listings as reviewed in the listing. 
- PIR excludes queries against blinded data. 
- PIR fetches the PDAP details from the latest published plan document

## Publish Profile Designs as View Only or Master for Detect
## Description
 You can set profile designs that have no missing data as view-only and publish them as read-only designs. A new Type column on the Published Designs page marks designs as View Only for Detect, indicating if the design was published as view-only or for use in Medidata Detect.  
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Data managers can identify discrepancies and anomalies from patient data using view-only designs, and use designs published as Master for Detect to obtain the latest data from Detect. 
 User Impact 
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page > Draft Designs tab > for a selected design, if you click the on the right of the page, and then select View Only and on the Confirm window, click View Only , the design is published as View Only and appears on the Published Designs page. The Type column on the Published Designs page marks the design as View Only. You cannot edit a view only design. 
- The Make Master option for draft designs is renamed to  Master for Detect .  
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page > Published Designs tab > for a View Only design, click the on the right, select Copy to another study   to copy the published design to another study or Duplicate within study to create a copy within the study.  
- The copied design appears under Draft Designs in the destination study. 
- The duplicate design appears under Draft Designs page in the current study. 
- On the Patient Profiles Designs page > Draft Designs tab > for a selected design, if you click the on the right of the page, the View Only option appears disabled if the design has missing data .

## Quality Tolerance Limit Summary Report
## Description
 Use the Quality Tolerance Limit (QTL) Summary Report to review the QTLs associated with your study.  View the report online or download it as a PDF file.   
## Affected Roles
 Study Users.
## Advantages
 Use the QTL Summary Report to view all of the QTLs associated with risks in the study. This information is useful when creating or updating Clinical Study Reports (CSRs) for your clinical trial.

- The Risk Plan Reports label in the left pane is renamed to Reports . 
- From the Reports tab, you can generate a PDF version of either the Risk Plan Report or QTL Summary Report. 
- Changes to QTL Summary Report details automatically save as soon as you enter new or updated information. You do not have to manually save changes when you edit the report details.  
- Adding or deleting Participant records for one report automatically updates the Participant lists available for use in all Risk Management reports. 
- You can indicate which participants need to review the report by selecting Yes or No in the Review Required column. 
- You can issue a bulk selection request for all participants by clicking the check box in the header of the Participants list. Click once to select all check boxes. Click again to deselect all check boxes. 
## Special Considerations
 Ensure that your role includes the  Generate Reports  building block permission. This allows a study user to generate the QTL Summary report.
 Note : You can acknowledge your review of the report manually by signing in the Signature box at the top of a printed copy of the report. Or use a signature feature if included in your PDF viewer software.

===== PAGE: rbqm__associated_mitigations_with_functional_plans | RBQM: Associate Mitigations with Functional Plans =====
## RBQM: Associate Mitigations with Functional Plans
## What Is New?
 When adding risk mitigations to risk assessments, you can associate the mitigations with functional plans. Then when creating data quality plans in the RBQM > Plan Documents capability,  if you add a risk assessment table to a plan document, the risks table includes the Functional Plans Affected column, which autopopulates based on the entries made in the Mitigations and Plans > Functional Plans Affected field for each mitigation added to risks in the Add Risk and Risk Review subpages. You can filter the tables in plan documents to show only mitigations that apply to the plan. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Risk managers
## Workflow Process
 The Add Risk subpage and Risk Review subpage no longer include the Risk Mitigations tab. The functionality that enables you to add and manage risk mitigations now exists in the Details tab > Mitigations and Actions section. 
## Other Applications
 When writing integrated data quality plans in the RBQM > Plan Documents capability, if you add a risk assessment table to a plan document, the risks table includes the Functional Plans Affected column, which autopopulates based on the entries made in the Mitigations and Plans > Functional Plans Affected field for each mitigation added to risks in the Add Risk and Risk Review subpages. You can filter the tables in plan documents to show only mitigations that apply to the plan. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 When creating risks mitigations in RBQM, associating mitigations with functional plans: 
- Streamlines the connection between the mitigations you add to the risk assessment and the mitigations you add to functional plans as part of the data quality plan. 
- Enables you to filter data quality plans in the RBQM > Plan Documents capability to focus solely on mitigations and action plans that affect you or that you are responsible for. 
- Makes creating data quality plans faster and easier. 
- Improves compliance by linking actions and mitigations to plans, providing full visibility for better alignment. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 When you: 
- Create a new risk in the Risk Assessment > Add Risk subpage,  
- View or edit a risk in the Risk Assessment > Risk Review subpage , or 
- View or edit a risk in the Risk Inventory > Risk Review subpage 
 the Add Risk subpage and Risk subpage no longer include the Risk Mitigations tab. Instead, the functionality that enables you to add and manage risk mitigations now exists in the: 
- Risk Assessment > Add Risk subpage > Details tab > Mitigations and Actions section, 
- Risk Assessment > Risk Review subpage  > Details tab > Mitigations and Actions section, and 
- Risk Inventory > Risk Review subpage  > Details tab > Mitigations and Actions section. 
 In the Mitigations and Actions section, you can click the Add Mitigation button, which when clicked, opens the Mitigations and Plans side panel. 
 Tip : Click images to enlarge.
 When adding or editing a mitigation, you can click the Functional Plans Affected field and select one or more functional plans that you want to associate the mitigation with.

===== PAGE: rbqm__enhance_study_data_compliance_and_accuracy_with_audit_trail_review | RBQM: Enhance Study Data Compliance And Accuracy With Audit Trail Review =====
## RBQM: Enhance Study Data Compliance And Accuracy With Audit Trail Review
## What Is New?
 Audit trails are computer-generated records that capture all the activity in the system, and are valuable tools to maintain a high-level of data integrity, and are extremely useful to study teams. An Audit Trail Review (ATR) involves examining the recorded history of transactions or activities within a system to ensure compliance with regulations, detect any discrepancies, and verify the integrity of data. This review tracks all changes made to records, who made them, and when, providing a transparent and accountable record of system usage. It is important in ensuring accuracy in financial reporting, and supporting forensic investigations in cases of fraud or unauthorized access. The Audit Trail Review feature in Clinical Data Studio applies Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI to explore complex audit trail data sets.   
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All study team members.
## Workflow Process
 Audit Trail Review (ATR) pulls in operational metadata from Rave EDC to show edits, updates, and deletions made to data endpoints. Clinical Data Studio uses Generative AI to automatically build customized queries, and executes them against the operational Rave data to generate meaningful audit data sets that facilitate data quality checks.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Audit Trail Review: 
- Provides an intuitive, user-friendly interface that makes data exploration simple and accessible. 
- Enables you to effortlessly extract insights from vast and complex audit trail datasets using Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI technology. 
- Seamlessly filters massive datasets, where you can type a question into the interactive field to generate a meaningful dataset from your audit trail data. 
- Delivers actionable insights that allow you to make smarter data decisions. 
- Provides an Intuitive and user-friendly interface where AI-driven capabilities make finding the insights you need quicker and easier. 
- Accelerates decision making by allowing you to create, explore, and analyze audit trail data in ways that were previously time-consuming or complex. 
- Enables you to configure published audit data sets in KRIs and listings for use in your study. 
 For ATR Manager users (with the Manage Audit Trail Review access), ATR offers additional flexibility to publish data sets directly within Clinical Data Studio capabilities. This integration allows audit trail insights to be used for analysis, collaboration, and reporting across projects and teams. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The RBQM tab in Clinical Data Studio includes a new Audit Trail Review tab.

- Edit – Adds the query prompt to the chat dialog box where you can engage with the interface to modify the query as necessary. 
 Audit Review – You can click Audit Review from the top right corner of the Audit Trail Review page to start a new audit review session, or to choose to stay in the current session. 
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the feature:
- Audit Trail Review 
## What Else Should I Know?
 Permissions 
- You must have the  View Audit Trail Review t o ask questions and save prompts, whereas to publish audit data sets you need the Manage Audit Trail Review building block added respectively to your role in Cloud Administration.  
 ATR Behavior 
- No blinded data sets are shown as part of audit trail review data. 
- You can only publish a maximum of 10 audit data sets in any study.  
- You can publish only ten audit data sets per study environment. 
- The audit workflow runs weekly, every weekend. The published data set is available in the study only after the audit workflow runs. 
- You cannot publish and download a data set if the Data Preview shows no records. 
 ATR Limitations 
- Audit trail review does not support: 
- Any aggregations. For example, a question like Give audits for AE form where a data point was modified more than 10 times, may produce a data set that was modified just once. 
- Complex computations, or calculating differences in timestamps. For example, a question like Give audits where a datapoint was modified 10 days after it was entered. may not produce a result. 
- Results at any level other than data points. For example, a question like Give me all sites in the data, does not produce a result. 
- Filtering on data point values. 
- Question prompts asking for all audits in the study. 
- Filtering in the published audit data set is limited to the following fields:  
- audit user, audit date/date range, form oid, field oid, audit subcategories, patient ID, country, and site. 
- Published audit data listings do not support the following functionality: 
- Submit queries. 
- Submit vendor queries. 
- Cross-dataset listing creation 
- Missing records 
- The ATR functionality times out if the learning model takes longer than five minutes to process a request.

## RBQM: Ensure Study Data Accuracy Using Data Quality Plans
## What Is New?
 A Data Quality Plan (DQP) in a study is a comprehensive document that outlines the strategies, procedures, and measures to ensure the accuracy, completeness, reliability, and integrity of the data collected during the trial. The plan is essential for verifying that the data supports robust conclusions and complies with regulatory standards. Clinical Data Studio now includes a capability where you can build integrated data quality plans for your study. The RBQM tab in Clinical Data Studio includes a Plan Document capability where you can build data quality plans that include risk mitigations for your study.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers with the Manage Data Quality Plans building block can publish, whereas data managers with View Data Quality Plans permissions can only view existing plans.
## Workflow Process
 Data managers add mitigations and associate functional plans in the Risk Review section in Risk Management to track risks for better study data accuracy. Data managers then use various components available under the Plan Documents section to build integrated data quality plans which act as a guide for risk mitigation in the study. 
## Other Applications
 When adding and managing mitigations, you can associate mitigations with functional plans. When writing integrated data quality plans in the RBQM > Plan Documents capability, if you add a risk assessment table to a plan document, the risks table includes the Functional Plans Affected column, which auto-populates based on the entries made in the Mitigations and Plans > Functional Plans Affected field for each mitigation added to risks in the Add Risk and Risk Review subpages.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data Quality Plans:
- Streamlines operational planning by enabling the quick creation and management of comprehensive plans, allowing for faster execution. 
- Transforms risk data into actionable, dynamic plans that actively guide team member actions. 
- Provides enhanced transparency into actions and mitigations linked to each plan, ensuring alignment, accountability, and improved compliance across teams. This turns data quality management into a proactive, integrated process.

===== PAGE: rbqm__identify_potential_study_data_issues_using_signals | RBQM: Identify Potential Study Data Issues Using Signals =====
## RBQM: Identify Potential Study Data Issues Using Signals
## What Is New?
 In the centralized monitoring process, a signal is an  alert or indication of a potential problem, risk, or deviation in a clinical study.   Signals get  detected remotely  by analyzing study data centrally, and allow proactively identifying potential risks in the study data.  Signals help sponsors  focus resources  on sites or issues needing immediate attention, improving data integrity and patient safety.
In short,  
- A  signal is a potential issue identified through data analysis. 
- An issue is a confirmed finding, the result of a signal validated through central monitor review, site discussion, or site visit.  
 RBQM includes a new Signals feature that you can use to build automated and manual signals. Each signal is an observation that meets a set threshold, and derives data from a module you configure for signal generation. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates, and users with View Signals and Manage Signals building blocks.
## Workflow Process
 Study data automatically refreshes daily at approximately 6:00 AM (EST). When you click Refresh on the Signals page, signals generate for configured modules, based on the source module's last successful data update, and the set threshold for each module. On the Signals page, each configured module shows the last snapshot date and time from its source module. This means you can determine the exact version of the signals data in each module based on its snapshot date. 
 While configuring signals for individual modules, you can set up thresholds based on which automated signals get created. You must also choose the modules you want the signals to report on. For example, if you do not enable KRIs in the Signals Configuration, and add custom configurations, no signals get created for any KRI in your study when the signals data refreshes. Once you configure a signal, observations appear as signals based on custom configurations and the latest data snapshot for individual modules when you next refresh data. Custom configuration changes made after 6:00 AM EST do not show in the automated signals report until the next day.  
## Other Applications
 Signals read data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- KRIs. 
- QTLs. 
- Rounding. 
- Propagation. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients. 
- Under/over Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 With automated signals, Central Monitors can aggregate and track signals, create and assign actions for signals, and investigate signals of interest. You can monitor values that appear outside the set threshold and investigate observations.  Consolidating signals from various analyses into a single, centralized report: 
- Streamlines the identification, tracking, and management of data quality issues across study data. 
- Allows for continuous monitoring and ensures that potential risks get mitigated before they escalate as issues. 
- Enhances efficiency, reduces manual effort, and improves decision-making for users involved in central monitoring and central statistical monitoring. 
- Provides clear, actionable insights, ensuring that critical data quality issues are identified and addressed promptly. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The RBQM tab includes a new signals page that appears as follows:

## What Else Should I Know?
- You can perform the following signals report actions only if you have the View Signals building block added to your role in Cloud administration:
- View the Signals Report. 
- Add, update, assign actions.  
- Resolve Signals. 
- View Signals Audit Report. 
- With the Manage Signals building block, in addition to performing all the above actions, you can create, assign, dismiss, watch, and close signals. 
- You can refresh data only once for the automated signals. If an  observation falls below the configured threshold, it does not update when you refresh data. The last value which met the threshold was met is shown as the signal observation. 
- You cannot generate or configure signals for Rounding and Propagation, if pivot is turned on under RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping > Rounding and Propagation for the data set. 
- Custom configuration changes made after 6:00 AM EST do not show in the automated signals report until the next day.  
- For Statistical Monitoring modules such as Rounding, Propagation, Duplicate Patients, and Under/over Reporting, if the Signals workflow encounters an error with any one module, the automated signals report for that module shows observations misaligned with those shown on the module's dashboard. On the signals report, the Module Snapshot still reflects the latest snapshot data from that module. For example, if Rounding has an error, then the signals for Rounding may not align with the data shown on the RBQM > Statistical Monitoring > Rounding and Propagation > Rounding tab.

 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
