 Functionality or Module 
 | RBQM Configuration > KRI Configuration
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter :
 When configuring custom numeric KRIs, you can build an expression to filter for the specific subset of data that you want the KRI to perform statistical analysis on.
 Benefit to Users 
 | In previous releases, you could only create custom numeric KRIs that performed statistical analysis on the full set of data in a selected data set. Now, you can specify data subset populations within a dataset that are meaningful to your study that you want to perform statistical analysis on. For example, you may want to run analysis on SAEs that are grade 3, 4, or 5, and exclude SAEs of grade 1 or 2 from your analysis.
 Therefore, you now have more control over specific study data that you want to track, monitor, and review.

 KRI Dashboard

Selecting the check box reveals and expression builder, which you can use to filter the data population subset that the KRI runs analytics on within the selected data set.

## RBQM Configuration: Set Observation Thresholds For Weekend and Holiday Visits Using Signal Configurations
 Important: 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the  revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the  releases history.   
- For a summary of all features released, the  released features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Enhancement (Updated Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | RBQM Configuration
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter :  
 Configure weekend and holiday visits for signal generation to improve monitoring of site activity patterns. 
 Signals now include weekend and holiday visit observations. However, to produce automated signals for weekend and holiday visits, you must first  configure signals in RBQM > Configuration > Signals. 
 Benefit to Users 
 | With automated signals, Central Monitors can aggregate and track signals, create and assign actions for signals, and investigate signals of interest. You can monitor values that appear outside the set threshold and investigate observations, if necessary. 
 Consolidating signals from various analyses into a single, centralized report: 
- Streamlines the identification, tracking, and management of data quality issues across study data. 
- Allows for continuous monitoring and ensures that potential risks get mitigated before they escalate as issues. 
- Enhances efficiency, reduces manual effort, and improves decision-making for users involved in central monitoring and central statistical monitoring. 
- Provides clear, actionable insights, ensuring that critical data quality issues are identified and addressed promptly. 
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles 
 Central Monitors, Clinical Research Associates (CRAs), users with View Detect CSM Configuration and Manage Detect CSM Configuration building blocks added to their Cloud Administration profile. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 Signal configuration includes two aspects. First, the modules included in the signals report. Second, the specific thresholds within the modules at which signals get generated. 
 While configuring signals for Weekend and Holiday Visits, you can set up thresholds based on which automated signals get created. You must also choose Weekend and Holiday Visits if you want the signals to report on, otherwise no signals get created for weekend and holiday visits in your study when the signals data refreshes. Once you configure a signal, observations appear as signals based on custom configurations and the latest data snapshot for individual modules. Weekend and Holiday Visits shows the time at which data refreshed in the users local time zone. 
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact on other applications. However, automated signals get generated based on values you set up as thresholds for Weekend and Holiday Visits. 
 Impact on Interface 
 The RBQM > Configuration > Signals page now includes Weekend and Holiday Visits on the left-hand menu.  
 You must click the toggle button , next to Weekend and Holiday visits to include signals from the module in the automated signal report. Automated signals appear only if you enable the module, and then add configuration details. However, if you toggle off the module with previously saved configurations, they remain saved. If you refresh data in the automated signal report, signals from the deactivated module do not appear in the report. They appear once the module is toggled on. 
 If you click Weekend and Holiday Visits , the right-hand side shows the following: 
- Day of the week  
- Exclude visits 
- Default Description  
 You can click Save to save the signal configuration.
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 No existing data changes; no configuration or permission updates required.
 User Impact Assessment 
 | High 
 Learning Resource Updates 
 | The following lists any new or added resources that support this change: 
- Updated Article: Signal Configuration . 
 Special Considerations 
 | 
- Only users with View Detect CSM Configuration building blocks added to their Cloud Administration profiles can view and download custom configurations. Users with Manage CSM Detect Configuration can add, edit, or delete custom configurations. 
- You can refresh data only once for the automated signals report.  
- Custom configuration changes made after 6:00 AM EST do not show in the automated signals report until the next day.  
- For Statistical Monitoring modules such as Rounding, Propagation, Duplicate Patients, and Under/over Reporting, if the Signals workflow encounters an error with any one module, the automated signals report for that module shows observations misaligned with those shown on the module's dashboard. On the signals report, the Module Snapshot still reflects the latest snapshot data from that module. For example, if Rounding has an error, then the signals for Rounding may not align with the data shown on the RBQM > Statistical Monitoring > Rounding and Propagation > Rounding tab.

===== PAGE: rbqm_configuration__signals_integration_with_rave_ctms_issue_management | RBQM Configuration: Signals Integration With Rave CTMS Issue Management =====
## RBQM Configuration: Signals Integration With Rave CTMS Issue Management
## What Is New?
 In the Centralized Monitoring process , a signal is an   alert or indication of a potential problem, risk, or deviation in a clinical study . An issue is a confirmed finding, the result of a signal validated through central monitor review, site discussions, or site visits. You can now raise issues and resolve them both internally within the Signals capability, or use an external clinical trial management system (CTMS) like Rave CTMS for issue resolution. 
 You can configure Rave CTMS for signal issue resolution using Integrations. On the RBQM > Configurations > Integrations page, in the CTMS application section, if you select  Rave CTMS from the list, your study is integrated with Rave CTMS for signal issue tracking and resolution. You can configure only one external CTMS per study. You can remove the integration if you click  , the Delete icon next to a configured CTMS. 
 Important : You must configure the study and set up integration with the Rave CTMS issue management system before integrating with Signals for issue resolution.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates. 
- U sers with View Detect CSM Configuration and Manage Detect CSM Configuration. 
## Workflow Process
 Once a CTMS application is configured with your study, you can raise issues for signals and send to the external CTMS for progress tracking and issue resolution. Metadata about tasks assigned as part of issue tracking, or the change in issue status transmits back into Signals. You can view issue-related information on the Signal Details page.
## Other Applications
 Rave CTMS must be available and set up for the study before integration.
## How Do I Benefit?
 You can raise and track progress for issues in signals using an established, external issue management system, like Rave CTMS without the need to copy and duplicate work, saving time and improving efficiency. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 See What's New?.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the feature:
- Signal Configuration 
- Integrate With External Issue Management System. 
## What Else Should I Know?
 You must have the View Detect CSM Configuration and Manage Detect CSM Configuration building blocks assigned to your role in Cloud Administration to set up integrations with Rave CTMS.
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: rbqm_configuration_manager_integrates_with_medidata_detect | RBQM Configuration Manager Integrates with Medidata Detect =====
## RBQM Configuration Manager Integrates with Medidata Detect
## Description
 RBQM Configuration Manager allows you to create custom KRIs using the data sets and variables available in your study environment . You can then activate the custom KRIs to get consumed, analyzed, and calculated by Medidata Detect's data science microservice algorithms.  
 Based on the analytics, Medidata Detect automatically generates the KRI data analysis and renders the visualization output in the Key Risk Indicator table . From the Key Risk Indicators table, you can view, analyze, track, and write issues against the custom KRIs. 
 You can then use RBQM Configuration Manager to deactivate KRIs from getting consumed, analyzed, calculated, and displayed in Medidata Detect when that KRI no longer requires analysis. 
## Affected Roles
- RBQM Configuration Manager Admin 
- RBQM Configuration Manager Viewer 
- Medidata Detect users 
## Advantages
 RBQM Configuration Manager provides a single, centralized location for KRI configuration, storage, management, and activation. This promotes platform-wide standardization and consistency among the KRIs you are tracking in your studies. 
## User Impact
 You can use RBQM Configuration Manager's Key Risk Indicators page to:
- Add and Edit Custom Numeric and Percentage KRIs , and 
- Activate and Deactivate KRIs in RBQM Configuration Manager . 
 You can view KRI data analysis and visualization in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table. From the Key Risk Indicators table, you can view, analyze, track custom KRIs as well as log issues against custom KRIs.
 Activated KRIs get consumed, analyzed, calculated, and visually rendered by Medidata Detect. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: receive_warning_message_when_deleting_certain_elements | Receive Warning Message When Deleting Certain Elements =====
## Receive Warning Message When Deleting Certain Elements
## Description
 If you attempt to:
- delete an event table that is currently used in a timeline, or 
- delete a flag that is currently used in a header 
 outside of the respective timeline or header itself, then you receive a warning message.
 The message states that the event table or flag you want to delete will be removed from all timelines or headers in which they currently exist.
## Affected Roles
 Unblinded patient profile designers.
## Advantages
 The warning message acts as safeguard to inform you of the repercussions of deleting events or flags outside of their respective timeline or header. Thus, potentially preventing you from unknowingly and unintentionally deleting elements.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: reconcile_data_accurately_using_data_reviewer_algorithms | Reconcile Data Accurately Using Data Reviewer Algorithms =====
## Reconcile Data Accurately Using Data Reviewer Algorithms
## Description
 Data Managers and Central Monitors must reconcile study data collected at sites to ensure data accuracy. However, lack of clinical experience in personnel conducting reconciliation or errors encountered while manually entering data can hamper the reconciliation process or even threaten study integrity. Medidata Detect 2023.1.0 introduces six new AI Data Reconciliation reports that use built-in algorithms to automatically reconcile study data.
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Data Reviewer building block. 
## Advantages
 As Data Managers and Central Monitors, you can:
- Produce error-free data by avoiding a manual  reconciliation process. 
- Use built-in algorithms to create reconciliation reports, and save time spent on reviewing study data and finding matches for each report. 
- Overcome lack of clinical experience to reconcile study data. 
## User Impact
 The update includes various changes to the user interface including creation of a new page - AI Data Reconciliation in Data Reviewer. The screenshot and table below indicate the changes.

Each child record includes a Link button which you can click to link the child record to the parent record in the report and mark the parent record as reviewed. The Confidence column for the parent record shows a icon. 
- 
 | 6 
 | You can click Refresh Data to refresh all the data in the AI Data Reconciliation reports. The button disables while data refreshes. The page shows the date and time when the refresh completes. The button enables if there is new data in the reconciliation reports.

===== PAGE: remove_blank_rows_at_the_bottom_of_tables | Remove Blank Rows at the Bottom of Tables =====
## Remove Blank Rows at the Bottom of Tables
## Description
 Based on how forms are structured in Rave Architect, wide tables, event tables, and patient information tables may sometimes display an empty row at the bottom of a patient profile. Not only is the row distracting, but the empty row can also impact how CSA calculates analytics for a patient profile.
 Therefore, Patient Profiles Cloud introduces the Item Group Repeat Key variable in the list of available data sets. You can eliminate the blank row in your tables by adding a row display condition so that rows only display if they have an Item Group Repeat Key variable with a value greater than 0.
## Affected Roles
- Patient Profile Designers 
## Advantages
 You can remove blank rows from displaying at the bottom of wide tables, event tables, and patient information tables in a patient profile. Doing so also yields more accurate CSA analytics results.
## User Impact
 Patient Profiles Cloud now includes the Item Group Repeat Key variable in its list of data sets. On the Design page > Elements tab, you can select to add or edit an element and go to the Table Options tab > Conditional Options section for that element. You can then click the Add button that corresponds with the Row label to display that Row Display Condition dialog. From there, you can click and drag the Item Group Repeat Key variable from the data set accordion to the table on the left, select the greater than symbol (>) in the Operator column, and then enter 0 in the Value column. Going forward, wide tables, event tables, and patient information tables no longer display blank rows at the bottom.
## Special Considerations
 None.

- Review metadata information for a given data set.

===== PAGE: risk_categorization_and_risk_scoring | Risk Categorization and Risk Scoring =====
## Risk Categorization and Risk Scoring
## Description
 The risk assessment team can categorize risks to make them easier to review and develop mitigation strategies.  Yo u can use predefined templates or create new risk categorization templates to apply to all studies in the client division. You can also create new risk categories at the study level.   
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Yo u can list the risk categories in a template for use in many studies or define a unique set of risk categories for a single study. The risk categories make it easier for the risk assessment team to review and develop mitigation strategies for a group of similar risks.  
## User Impact
## Client Division Level
 A list of predefined templates displays when you click   Risk Categorization Templates   in the left pane. These templates provide a starting point for you to categorize the risks for your study. You may add or delete risks in these predefined templates or create your own unique template. 
- Decentralized Clinical Trials (DCT) Risk Assessment Considerations   - The DCT Risk Assessment Considerations template provides categories of risk, questions for discussion, and considerations specific to risk categories associated to the implementation of decentralized trials. This template supports risk identification that could affect patient safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance because of the impact of decentralized trials on clinical trial operations. The source of information for this template is the Association of Clinical Research Organizations (ACRO). 
- Medidata COVID-19   - The COVID-19 template provides categories of risk, questions for discussion, and considerations specific to risk categories associated to the COVID-19 pandemic. This template supports risk identification that could affect patient safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance because of the impact of COVID-19 to clinical trial operations. The source of information for this template is Medidata, a Dassault Systèmes Company. 
- TransCelerate BioPharma Inc. RACT   -   This TransCelerate   template provides categories of risk, questions for discussion, and considerations specific to risk categories. This template supports risk identification that could affect patient safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance. The source of information for this template is TransCelerate   BioPharma   Inc. 
## Study Level
- You can use a predefined risk categorization template to group the risks associated with the study. Or you can create new risk categories and add risks unique to your study.  
- When you add a risk category, you can configure a list of questions that the team uses when discussing the risk or mitigation strategies. You can associate a risk score with a question, with a risk, or with a risk category. 
- The risk score is based on the Scoring by Product methodology and uses a three-point scale: High, Medium, and Low. 
- A Total Risk Categorization Score shows at the top of the Risk Categorization page. The Total Risk Categorization Score is calculated as the sum of the individual Risk Category Scores. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: risk_inventory | Risk Inventory =====
## Risk Inventory
## Description
 When a study user selects a study in Risk Management, the Risk Inventory page  displays all risks associated with the study environment. Data for the h ighest study environment level displays by default.  
 Note : The study environment order from highest to lowest is: Production, Development, Functional Testing, Interactive Verification, User Acceptance Testing, Training, and Other, which includes custom study environments ordered alphabetically.
  To view high-scoring risks that may require mitigation, sort risks by risk score. The highest risk scores then display at the top of the list. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The Risk Inventory is the one place where you can view all risks applicable to the study .
## User Impact
 You can search or sort the risks in the inventory to identify problems flagged by indicators that are out of range. You can view the origin of the risk, such as Critical Data, Critical Process, or Risk Category. You can also drill down to view or edit the risk details.
## Special Considerations
 None.

## Risk Plan Reporting
## Description
 You can create a risk plan report that provides risk assessment details for your study. View the report online or download it as a PDF file. 
## Affected Roles
 Study User.
## Advantages
 View the critical data, critical processes, risk categories, and risk inventory in a single consolidated report or in a selection of reports.
## User Impact
 Use this feature to:
- Update risk plan report details and participants. 
- Indicate which participants are required to acknowledge the report. 
- Configure the report to print all or specific components such as critical data, critical processes, risk categories, or the risk inventory. 
- Generate the risk plan report for online review or to download in PDF format. 
## Special Considerations
 Ensure that your role includes the  Generate Risk Plan Report  building block permission. This allows a study user to generate the risk plan report.
 Note : The Study Approval / Acknowledge permission associated with an eSignature is not yet active for Risk Management. Instead, you may acknowledge the report manually by signing in the Signature box at the top of a printed copy or by using a signature feature if included in your PDF viewer software.

===== PAGE: role-based_permissions_now_determine_the_pespectives_you_can_view_and_access | Role-based Permissions Now Determine the Pespectives You Can View and Access =====
## Role-based Permissions Now Determine the Pespectives You Can View and Access
## Description
 Medidata Detect users are now assigned roles defined by your Detect administrator in Cloud Administration . The roles assigned to you determine the perspectives you can view and interact with in Detect, as well as the actions you can perform.
 The table below lists examples of suggested roles, perspectives available to each role, and permissible actions:
 Role 
 Available Perspectives 
 Permissible Actions 
 | Detect Site Monitor 
 | 
- Sites 
 | 
- View and Assess Site-level Study Performance 
- Access and View the Top Contributors 
- Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot 
- Investigate Data Using the Key Risk Indicators Table 1 
- Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data 
 | Detect Country Manager 
 | 
- Countries 
- Sites 
 | 
- View and Assess Country-level and Site-level Study Performance 
- Access and View the Top Contributors 
- Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot 
- Investigate Data Using the Key Risk Indicators Table 1 
- Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data 
 | Detect Data Manager 
 | 
- Domains 
- Countries 
- Sites 
 | 
- View and Assess Overall Study Performance (excluding the risk categories perspective) 
- Access and View the Top Contributors 
- Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot 
- Investigate Data Using the Key Risk Indicators Table 1 
- Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data 
 | Detect Super User 
 | 
- Risk Categories 
- Domains 
- Countries 
- Sites 
 | 
- View and Assess Overall Study Performance 
- Access and View the Top Contributors 
- Investigate Data Using Data Anomaly Detection Plots 
- Investigate Data Using the Event Incidence Plot 
- Investigate Data Using the Key Risk Indicators Table 1 
- Flag, Track, and Audit Reviewed Study Data 
- Schedule or Trigger When CSM Refreshes and Outputs the Latest Study Data Analysis 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 In previous Medidata Detect releases, you could view and access all perspectives and data analyses provided for the overall study data. However, depending on your role and responsibilities, not all of the perspectives and data analyses may require your attention or investigation. Therefore, when trying to find the data you needed to investigate, you could easily get lost in Detect by accessing and searching through data that did not apply to your needs.
 Now that Detect users are assigned role-based permissions, your Detect workspace  displays only the exact perspectives and data analyses that you need to investigate. Therefore, you can much more effectively and efficiently focus only on the data you need without the risk and hassle of getting lost or distracted by data that is irrelevant to your role. This results in a streamlined workflow, leading you to produce faster, more accurate, and more effective data analyses. 
## User Impact
 The Overview page displays only the perspectives and data analyses permissible to you based on your assigned role. For example, if you are assigned only the Detect Site Monitor role, then you can only view and access the Sites perspective on the Overview page as defined by your organization.
## Special Considerations
 Detect administrators must update existing roles or create new roles with the appropriate permissions to ensure users can view and access perspectives.
 If you do not have permissions to view any perspectives, you cannot view data in Detect and the Overview page displays the following message: " You do not have permissions to view perspective data. Contact your admin to update your Detect permissions."

===== PAGE: schedule_or_trigger_when_kri_dashboard_refreshes_with_the_latest_study_data_analysis | Schedule or Trigger When KRI Dashboard Refreshes with the Latest Study Data Analysis =====
## Schedule or Trigger When KRI Dashboard Refreshes with the Latest Study Data Analysis
## Description
 KRI Dashboard now has a KRI Scheduler page, which allows you to schedule or trigger when KRI Dashboard refreshes and renders the most recent study data analysis.
## Affected Roles
 Users with:
- View KRI Dashboard permissions can view the KRI scheduler. 
- Manage KRI Scheduler permissions can schedule and run refreshes. 
## Advantages
 In previous KRI Dashboard releases, you had to schedule and trigger data refreshes from the Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) History page. Now you can schedule and trigger data refreshes from directly within KRI Dashboard and independent of the data refresh schedule set up for other Detect modules such as CSM.
## User Impact
 You can now access the KRI Scheduler page from the Detect Landing Page or from KRI Dashboard's left-hand menu. On the KRI Scheduler page, you can: 
- Select the Snapshot Schedule to determine the data refresh frequency:
- Weekly 
- Bi-Weekly 
- Monthly 
- Bi-Monthly 
- Quarterly 
- Select the specific day of the week or month you want the data refresh to trigger. 
 Also, for users with proper permissions, the KRI Scheduler page includes the   Refresh button. When you click  Refresh , the KRI Dashboard refreshes to show visual renderings of the most recent study data analysis. The Last Updated field updates to show the time stamp of the currently rendered study data's most recent completed run through Medidata Detect's analytics.  
## Knowledge Hub Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Hub provides new and updated content to support this feature: 
- Schedule or Trigger When KRI Dashboard Refreshes and Outputs the Latest Study Data Analysis 
## Special Considerations
 Depending on study data volume, there may be lag time between when the data refresh triggers and when the updated data renders in the KRI Dashboard. So newly rendered data analyses that you view in the KRI Dashboard may reflect the data snapshot from a day or two prior.
 Detect now includes a new user role building block, Manage KRI Scheduler. To learn more, see Detect User Roles and Capabilities .
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: search_patient_data_by_column_filter | Search Patient Data By Column Filter =====
## Search Patient Data By Column Filter
## Description
 On the Design page > Profiles tab, you can search patient data by applying filters to columns in the Patient Selector section. Query data associated with the patient you select in the Patient Selector section shows in the Patient Query tab. 
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 With updated filtering options, profile reviewers can efficiently locate patient data of interest from a study. 
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Profiles tab, you can apply filters to the columns in the Patient Selector table.  
- If you click   from the top of the Profiles page, filter fields appear under all column headers. 
- For any column, if you enter three characters or digits in the   field, the list shows patient data that includes the filter parameter. The filter response differs slightly depending on the selected parameter. For example, for the Patient ID  column if you enter 100 and click Enter, the list shows 11371001, 10031023 and so on, in an ascending order. You can apply column filters to all columns. If you filter by one column and then by another, the first record that matches the filter parameters shows at the top of the Patient Selector section. The first query that matches the filter parameter in the Patient Selector section, shows at the top of the Patient Query table. 
- If you click   from the top of the Profiles page, filter fields no longer appear under each column.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Medidata Patient Profiles Knowledge Space provides updated content to support this feature: 
- View Patient Query Data 
- Review and Export Patient Profiles 
## Special Considerations
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: set_observation_thresholds_for_modules_using_signal_configurations | RBQM: Set Observation Thresholds For Modules Using Signal Configurations =====
## RBQM: Set Observation Thresholds For Modules Using Signal Configurations
## What Is New?
 In the Centralized Monitoring process , a signal is an alert or indication of a potential problem, risk, or deviation in a clinical study. Signals get detected remotely by analyzing study data centrally, and allow proactively identifying potential risks in the study data. Signals help sponsors focus resources on sites or issues needing immediate attention, improving data integrity and patient safety.
In short,  
- A signal is a potential issue identified through data analysis. 
- An issue is a confirmed finding, the result of a signal validated through central monitor review, site discussion, or site visit.  
 RBQM includes a new Signals feature that you can use to build automated signals. However, to produce automated signals, you must first configure the modules you want the signal to report on. You can configure signals in RBQM > Configuration > Signals. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Central Monitors, Clinical Research Associates (CRAs), users with View Detect CSM Configuration and Manage Detect CSM Configuration building blocks added to their Cloud Administration profile.
## Workflow Process
 Signal configuration includes two aspects. First, the modules included in the signals report. Second, the specific thresholds within the modules at which signals get generated. 
 While configuring signals for individual modules, you can set up thresholds based on which automated signals get created. You must also choose the modules you want the signals to report on. For example, if you do not enable KRIs in the Signals Configuration, and add custom configurations, no signals get created for any KRI in your study when the signals data refreshes. Once you configure a signal, observations appear as signals based on custom configurations and the latest data snapshot for individual modules.
## Other Applications
 No impact on other applications. However, automated signals get generated based on values you set up as thresholds for the following:
- Patient Profiles 
- KRIs 
- QTLs 
- Duplicate Patients 
- Rounding 
- Propagation 
- Under/over Reporting 
## How Do I Benefit?
 With automated signals, Central Monitors can aggregate and track signals, create and assign actions for signals, and investigate signals of interest. You can monitor values that appear outside the set threshold and investigate observations, if necessary. Consolidating signals from various analyses into a single, centralized report: 
- Streamlines the identification, tracking, and management of data quality issues across study data. 
- Allows for continuous monitoring and ensures that potential risks get mitigated before they escalate as issues. 
- Enhances efficiency, reduces manual effort, and improves decision-making for users involved in central monitoring and central statistical monitoring. 
- Provides clear, actionable insights, ensuring that critical data quality issues are identified and addressed promptly.

 You can configure Signals reports in RBQM > Configuration > Signals.

## What Else Should I Know?
- Only users with View Detect CSM Configuration building blocks added to their Cloud Administration profiles can view and download custom configurations. Users with Manage CSM Detect Configuration can add, edit, or delete custom configurations. 
- You can refresh data only once for the automated signals report.  
- You cannot generate or configure signals for Rounding and Propagation, if pivot is turned on under RBQM > Configuration > Data Mapping > Rounding and Propagation. 
- Custom configuration changes made after 6:00 AM EST do not show in the automated signals report until the next day.  
- For Statistical Monitoring modules such as Rounding, Propagation, Duplicate Patients, and Under/over Reporting, if the Signals workflow encounters an error with any one module, the automated signals report for that module shows observations misaligned with those shown on the module's dashboard. On the signals report, the Module Snapshot still reflects the latest snapshot data from that module. For example, if Rounding has an error, then the signals for Rounding may not align with the data shown on the RBQM > Statistical Monitoring > Rounding and Propagation > Rounding tab.

## Signals: Raise Protocol Deviation And Non-Protocol Deviation Issues Using Signals
## What Is New?
 You can now specify the type of issues you can raise for signals generated for study data. You can specify the following:
- A Protocol Deviation (PD) issue or,  
- A Non-Protocol Deviation (Non-PD)  
 You can further resolve these issues internally, that is, within Signals, or send them to an external issue management system like Rave CTMS for resolution. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates 
-  Users with View Signals and Manage Signals building blocks. 
## Workflow Process
 For any signal with status Open, you can raise either a Protocol Deviation (PD), or a N on-Protocol Deviation (Non-PD) issue. If you send the issue to an external issue management system like Rave CTMS.  
## Other Applications
 To raise issues to an external issue management system, Rave CTMS, you must ensure that Signals is integrated with Rave CTMS. 
 Signals read data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- KRIs. 
- QTLs. 
- Rounding. 
- Propagation. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients. 
- Under/over Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Central Monitors can create actionable issues for autocomplete generated and user-generated signals, track, and resolve them. This ensures potential issues get checked in time and do not threaten study data integrity. This further:
- Ensures protocol deviations, safety issues, and high-risk findings are formally tracked and resolved in alignment with sponsor expectations. 
- Provides a clear audit trail for all issues raised, reducing inspection risks. 
- Streamlines the workflow by allowing you to raise issues directly from Signals rather than duplicating work in multiple systems. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the Signals page, for any signal with an Open or Reopened status, you can create an issue.

===== PAGE: signals__resolve_issues_within_signals_or_using_external_issue_management_system_rave_ctms | Signals: Resolve Issues Within Signals Or Using External Issue Management System Rave CTMS =====
## Signals: Resolve Issues Within Signals Or Using External Issue Management System Rave CTMS
## What Is New?
 In the Centralized Monitoring process , a signal is an   alert or indication of a potential problem, risk, or deviation in a clinical study . An issue is a confirmed finding, the result of a signal validated through central monitor review, site discussions, or site visits. You can now raise site and study level issues and resolve them both internally within the Signals capability, or use an external clinical trial management system (CTMS) like Rave CTMS. You can no longer send issues from Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) and Statistical Monitoring dashboards to Rave CTMS. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates 
- Users with View Signals, Manage Signals, Create Issues , and View Issues and Actions building blocks. 
## Workflow Process
 Once your study is integrated with an external issue management like Rave CTMS, you can send issues for resolution. You can also receive issue progress information like issue status from Rave CTMS. Any issue-related actions you perform in Rave CTMS affect the issue outcome in Signals. However, if you close a signal with an open issue in Rave CTMS, the issue does not automatically close. 
 For issues raised internally and tracked for resolution, the entire issue progress occurs within Signals.
## Other Applications
- You must have access to Rave CTMS to progress and resolve issues. 
- Signals read data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- KRIs. 
- QTLs. 
- Rounding. 
- Propagation. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients. 
- Under/over Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Depending on the sponsor set up, for signals that move into a formal issue management system like Rave CTMS, 
- Tracking issues ensures that you can resolve protocol deviations, safety issues, minor, major, and high-risk findings in accordance with regulations, and in alignment with sponsor expectations. 
- Resolving issues provides a clear audit trail of all actions and personnel involved, reducing inspection risks.  
- Raising issues directly from within Signals avoids duplication of work in multiple systems and reduces human errors.  
 For issues raised internally within Signals, tracking, reviewing progress, and resolution occurs in one place, allowing all study personnel involved a clear view into each step of the resolution process.
## Where Do I See the Change?
## For issues sent to Rave CTMS 
 On the RBQM > Signals page, for any signal with Open or Reopened status, if you click , the More icon, and then click Raise an issue , the Create Issue window appears. If you  click the Send to CTMS option on the Create Issue window and select one of the issue types, you can send either a protocol deviation (PD), or a non-protocol deviation (Non-PD) issue to Rave CTMS for tracking and resolution. You cannot send an issue to Rave CTMS if actions are assigned for the signal. You can raise multiple issues of each type for a signal. Once you send an issue to Rave CTMS, the issue is tracked and resolved entirely within Rave CTMS. Only the issue status transmits back to Signals. Issues raised to Rave CTMS are at site and study level. 
## For issues set for resolution internally within Signals  
 On the RBQM > Signals page, for any signal with Open or Reopened status, if you click , the More icon, and then click Raise an issue , the Created Issue window appears. If you click either a protocol deviation (PD), or a non-protocol deviation (Non-PD) issue on the Create Issue window, then you can raise an issue within Signals. You can raise only one issue for resolution within Signals. The Raise an issue button becomes disabled if a signal has an issue set for resolution internally within Signals. You can resolve an issue by clicking the Clear Issue option.

## Signals:Track Signal Action Progress Using the Actions Tab
## What Is New?
 Actions are steps central monitors take in investigating signals in the study. You can now receive a notification when you are assigned actions and signals. The Signals page includes an Actions tab where you can track the progress for all actions assigned to team members for signals in your study.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates. 
- Users with View Signals and Manage Signals building blocks. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to workflow process.
## Other Applications
 Signals read data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- KRIs. 
- QTLs. 
- Rounding. 
- Propagation. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients. 
- Under/over Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Clinical research associates no longer need to individually review each signal to find assigned actions. The Actions tab groups all the actions into a single list, providing a complete set of actions assigned in a study. This enables faster accessibility, reducing time taken to complete oversight, making reconciliation and progress tracking smother, provides a clear view of the workload across study team members. It also enables better management at high-incidence sites and prevents duplication of effort if actions already exist for signals.

## Signals: Updated Signals Include Preset Filters, Comments, And Downloads
## What Is New?
 Signals now include preset filtering cards that show dismissed, watched, or signals with issues. You can also add comments, apply additional filters, and download signals as .xlsx files.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- Central Monitors and Central Statistical Monitors, Clinical Research Associates 
-  Users with the View Signals and Manage Signals building blocks associated with their roles in Cloud Administration. 
## Workflow Process

 Signals read data from the following capabilities:
- Patient Profiles. 
- KRIs. 
- QTLs. 
- Rounding. 
- Propagation. 
- Potential Duplicate Patients. 
- Under/over Reporting. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Study team members can search and find signals of interest with the readily available preset filters at the top of the Signals page. With more filter options, you can locate high incidence sites based on signal observations, download signals for easy circulation and action. With comments, you can add more notes or make specific observations on signals, providing a fuller context to the indicative potential risks at a site or within study data. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the RBQM > Signals page, the following preset filter cards appear at the top of the signals table:
- Dismissed –   If you click Dismissed, the table filters to show dismissed signals. 
- Watching – If you click Watching, the table shows signals with watched status. 
- Issues – If you click Issues, the table shows signals with issues. 
 If you click the , Filter option next to the Search field at the top right corner of the page, and then click More filters, additional filters appear which you can select. 
 Signals Additional Filters 
 On the RBQM > Signals page > Signals tab, if you click  , the More icon, in the row corresponding to a signal, and then click open signal details, a slide-out panel shows the Signal Details page. If you click the Comments tab on the Signal Details slide-out panel, and then click Add Comments, you can add notes or comments for the signal. 
 On the RBQM > Signals page > Signals tab, if you click , the Download icon, from the top right corner of the page, you can download all the signals in the study in an .xlsx file. When you download, all the comments, actions, issues, and resolution associated with the signals download too. 
 On the RBQM > Signals page > Signals tab, if you click , the Module icon, you can see the data refresh time for configured modules in your local time. If you hover over the icon, a tooltip that reads Module Status appears.

## Signals: Updated Signals User Interface Shows Changed Data
 Important: 
- For a summary of changes done to these release notes, if any, see the revision history . 
- For features and enhancements covered in previous releases, see the release history .   
- For a summary of all features released, the released  features index . 
## Change Details
 Product 
 | Clinical Data Studio
 Version 
 | 2026.1.0
 Change Type 
 | Enhancement (Updated Functionality)
 Functionality or Module 
 | Signals
 Summary of Changes 
 | 
 As highlighted in the Release Newsletter : 
 You can now easily identify changes in observation values between workflows, helping detect updates to previously acted-upon signals. Signals highlights scenarios where observations fall below the configured threshold while the configuration remains active in modules like Rounding and Propagation, QTLs, Under/Over Reporting, and KRIs. Signals includes a Changed Data column which shows changes in observation between data refreshes. 
 Benefit to Users 
 | Central monitors, CRAs, and study managers can identify significant updates, and trends of a signal, and prioritize review without the need to manually compare new data versus previous data. Preset filters allow you to quickly identify signals of interest.
 Summary of User Impact 
 | 
 Impact to Users and Roles

- Users with View Signals and Manage Signals building blocks. 
 Impact to Workflow Processes 
 No impact to workflow processes.
 Impact to Applications 
 No impact to other applications.
 Impact on Interface 
 The Signals table shows three new columns. if there is a change in signal observation. You can hover over icon to view the previous observation value. In the example below, for an issue, the Issue Type and Target Issue columns reads Protocol Deviation and Internal respectively. 
 The Signals table includes a new Changed Data column. Between refreshes, signal data may change due to observation values going above or below set thresholds for respective modules. The updated Signals page includes a Changed Data column with a  icon that shows if an open or reopened signal's underlying data changed. If you hover over the changed data icon, a tooltip shows the changed value, for example, over 16.7% . It also includes preset filters. A changed card also appears at the top of the Signals page showing the total count of observations. 
- If no signals get generated as observations fall below configured thresholds, the change is shown as follows: 
- For Potential Duplicate Patients analysis, the observation value updates to “No longer duplicate” for acted-upon signals. 
- For Patient Profiles analysis, the observation value sets to 0 patients when signals get no longer identified. 
- For Weekend and Holiday Visits analysis, the observation value updates to 0 when no visits get detected. 
- If a signal configuration for any module is no longer active, then the analysis hyperlink reads the inactive configuration when you hover over it. 
 Impact to Existing Data or Settings 
 No existing data changes; no configuration or permission updates required.
 User Impact Assessment 
 | Medium

===== PAGE: standardized_data_type_terminology | Standardized Data Type Terminology =====
## Standardized Data Type Terminology
## Description
 Previously, when you added an event table to a timeline which included a text variable, then the text variable's data type displayed as "String" in the Reports page > Type column. 
 However, if that same text variable was added to an event table, then the text variable's data type instead displayed as "Text"  in the Reports page > Type column. 
 Patient Profiles Cloud now consistently displays "Text" as the data type in the Reports page > Type column for timelines and event tables. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Standardizing the terminology used for data types across element types promotes consistency across the app and improved usability.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 None.

- Unblinded Patient Profile Viewers 
- Blinded Patient Profile Viewers 
- Unblinded Patient Profile Designers 
- Blinded Patient Profile Designers 
## Advantages

===== PAGE: track_and_clean_unclean_patient_data_with_clean_patient_tracker | Track and Clean Unclean Patient Data with Clean Patient Tracker =====
## Track and Clean Unclean Patient Data with Clean Patient Tracker
## What Is New?
 Clean Patient Tracker is an interactive dashboard that visualizes, lists, and prioritizes in one centralized location the outstanding patient data cleaning tasks   across Detect that require vetting and review. You can use Clean Patient Tracker to: 
- Track unvetted and unreviewed patient data. 
- Drilldown and directly access and complete outstanding data cleaning tasks. 
- View historical details of actions taken on Clean Patient Tracker in your study environment. 
- Manually trigger Clean Patient Tracker to recount the number of outstanding patient data cleaning tasks that require vetting and review. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data managers.
## Workflow Process
 Clean Patient Tracker pulls in the following study data: 
- The number of unreviewed data listing records for up to ten listings that you select to track in Data Reviewer > Data Listings. 
- The number of unreviewed and report records from Data Reviewer > AI Data Reconciliation. 
- The number of open queries from Rave EDC. 
 Clean Patient Tracker then visualizes, lists, and prioritizes: 
- Outstanding study-level data cleaning task metrics. 
- The sites in your study with the highest unclean patient counts. 
- The specific data cleaning tasks with the highest count of unclean or unreviewed records. 
- The most unclean patients in your study. 
 You can then track unvetted and unreviewed patient data , and further drill down directly to complete the outstanding data cleaning tasks listed in Clean Patient Tracker. 
## Other Applications
 Detect users with the proper permissions can m anually trigger Clean Patient Tracker to recount the number of outstanding patient data cleaning tasks that require vetting and review. For the most up-to-date counts, you can first refresh individual listings on the Data Listings page and refresh the AI Data Reconciliation page, and then recalculate   in Clean Patient Tracker. 
## How Do I Benefit?
 Clean Patient Tracker:
- Consolidates in one centralized location the metrics regarding outstanding data cleaning tasks across your RBQM portfolio in Detect. 
- Visualizes, lists, and prioritizes outstanding data cleaning tasks so you can focus on the most unclean data or areas of most importance in your study. 
- Facilitates faster cleaning of data. 
- Refreshes for an up-to-date view of data cleanliness. 
- Increases study team-level coordination and visibility of data cleanliness and outstanding data cleaning tasks. 
- Promotes cleaner, more fully vetted study data. 
## Where Do I See the Change?
 The Detect Landing Page now includes the Insights card, from which you can access the new Clean Patient Tracker page and its functionalities.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of this feature:
- Clean Patient Tracker 
- Access and View Clean Patient Tracker 
- Track and Clean Patient Data 
- View and Export Clean Patient Tracker Audit Reports 
- Trigger Clean Patient Tracker to Recalculate Outstanding Records Based on the Latest Study Data 
## What Else Should I Know?
 An admin must associate the View Clean Patient Tracker building block to a role in your Cloud Administration study group so that you can access Clean Patient Tracker .
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: track_study-level_threats_using_quality_tolerance_limits__qtls_ | Track Study-level Threats Using Quality Tolerance Limits (QTLs) =====
## Track Study-level Threats Using Quality Tolerance Limits (QTLs)
## Description
 Authorized users can now view and track quality tolerance limits (QTLs) on the Quality Tolerance Limits page. QTLs  are study-level metrics that indicate whether  a study parameter's reported data has breached a pre-identified data quality threshold.   QTLs target and monitor the greatest risks to  a study's: 
- Safety 
- Conduct 
- Performance 
- Compliance 
- Data quality 
 Each QTL has a value that is computed based on Medidata Detect's statistical analysis of your study data. QTLs are calculated at the study level. The QTL value calculations are reflected as one of the following: 
- Number  – Provides a total count of the number of subjects that meet the QTL's defined criteria. 
- Percentage  – Provides a percentage of the number of subjects that meet the QTL's defined criteria. 
 QTLs that reach or exceed a threshold indicate that the QTL's target study parameter may warrant investigation and mitigation. 
## Affected Roles
- Study managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 Tracking QTLs helps: 
- Ensure the study conduct operates as planned. 
- Identify as well as prevent or mitigate systematic issues early on in the study that may: 
- Threaten subject safety or study efficacy. 
- Invalidate the reliability of the study findings. 
## User Impact
 You can click QTLs on the left-hand menu to navigate to the Quality Tolerance Limits page. The Quality Tolerance Limits page allows you to: 
- Track the QTLs in your study and their respective values. 
- Determine which QTLs exceed the upper or lower tolerance limit of what is considered acceptable for that study metric. 
 Each QTL has a graphical output that displays:
- Observed  – The observed number or percentage of patients that meet the study parameter's criteria. For example, the observed percentage of patients in the study who experienced a serious adverse event. 
- Expectation    – The QTL's expected median value based on historical data. 
- Upper Limit   – The study parameter's upper statistical threshold value that, if breached, would require investigation or mitigation of the parameter's target study risk. 
- Lower Limit   – The study parameter's lower statistical threshold value that, if breached, would require investigation or mitigation of the parameter's target study risk. 
 Tip : QTLs can be configured to have only an upper limit, only a lower limit, or both.
 As shown below, QTLs whose values are within the acceptable range display in green. QTLs whose values are not within the acceptable range display in red. 
## Special Considerations
 You can hover your cursor on QTL names to display its full-text description.

===== PAGE: transpose_table_highlight_values_outside_a_range | Transpose Table Highlight Values Outside a Range =====
## Transpose Table Highlight Values Outside a Range
## Description
 Transposed tables highlight high and low variable values that lie outside a specified normal range. You can set these limits without choosing graphs for the transposed tables.  A ( ) displays next to variable values exceeding the upper limit. A ( ) displays next to variable values below the lower limit.
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 With high and low values shown with red and blue markers respectively, Patient Profile design reviewers can easily identify outliers in a study. 
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab:  
- When working in Transposed Tables: 
- The Normal Range section always displays at the bottom of the page. 
- The DATA OPTIONS tab allows you to drag-and-drop upper and lower limit variables into the Variable column in the Normal Range section. The Display column shows the upper limit in red and the lower limit in blue. These colors are set by default and cannot be changed. 
 On the Design page > Profiles tab: 
- If you specify both upper and lower limit variables, high and low variables outside the specified normal range display with a  or icon respectively, for a patient. A legend appears at the bottom of the table. The legend and markers do not display if no upper or lower limit is set. 
- If you specify only upper limit variables, high variables outside the specified normal range display with a  icon for a patient. A legend  appears at the bottom of the table. The legend and markers not display if no upper limit is set. 
- If you specify only lower limit variables, low variables outside the specified normal range display with a icon for a patient. A legend  appears at the bottom of the table. The legend and markers do not display if no lower limit is set. 
- When you export patient profile designs in a study to PDF, h igh and low variables that lie outside the specified normal range display with a or icon respectively.  A legend  appears at the top of the page. The legend and markers not display if no upper or lower limit is set. 
## Special Considerations
 Transposed tables indicate high and low values outside a range only if upper and lower limit variables have been defined for the selected test. If a variable is exactly equal to either the set upper or lower limit, a visual marker does not appear next to the variable as this it is within the specified range.

===== PAGE: transposed_tables_allow_positioning_of_graph_and_table | Transposed Tables Allow Positioning Of Graph And Table =====
## Transposed Tables Allow Positioning Of Graph And Table
## Description
 You can configure transposed tables to display tables, graphs, or both for data elements. You can configure transposed tables to position graphs and tables above or below the data element. You can also configure specific data variables in transposed tables to display in tables, graphs, or in both.  
## Affected Roles
 Patient Profile Designers. 
## Advantages
 Showing data elements in graph and table format, provides the flexibility of gaining better insight into specific data points in profile designs. 
## User Impact
 For transposed tables, on the Design page > Elements tab > Table Options> Graph Options, you can select  Show Both ,  Table Only  or  Graph Only . Depending on the selection, transposed tables will show either graph or table or both for data elements.  
- If you do not select Show Both ,  Table Only  or  Graph Only , then Table Only is the default option. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only tables display for the element. 
- If you select Table Only , graph options become disabled. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only tables display for the element. 
- If you select Graph Only , graph options become enabled. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only graphs display for the element. 
- If you select Show Both , graph options become enabled. If you then switch to Table Only , graph options become disabled and become enabled when you switch to Graph Only . 
- If you select Show Both ,  
- and then set  Table Position to Above Graph , the table appears above the graph while viewing profiles on the Profiles page. 
- and then set  Table Position to Below Graph , the table appears below the graph while viewing profiles on the Profiles page. 
- If you select Show Both , and then click the vertical ellipsis in a data variable's name,  Show only in Table ,  Show only in Graph , or Show in Both options display . 
- If you select  Show only in Table ,  displays indicating that the variable does not display in graphs. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the specific variable only displays in the table and the graph displays to the left to account for the hidden column. 
- If you select  Show only in Graph ,   displays indicating that the variable does not display in tables. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the specific variable only displays in the graph and the columns in the table display to the left to account for the hidden column. 
- If you select  Show in Both or select neither  Show only in Table , nor  Show only in Graph , no additional icon displays near the data variable's name. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable displays both in graphs and tables for the patient. 
- Data variables is in the "Tests" and Visit Variables section in a table, cannot be set to display in tables, graphs or both, as this is not applicable to such data variables. 
- If you do not select   Show Both ,  Table Only , or  Graph Only , then   Table Only   is the default option. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable displays in tables for the patient. 
- If you select Show Both  and also select General Options > Hide "No Data" Elements , then on viewing patient profiles: 
- The table and graph do not display if the patient does not meet the criteria to have this data element displayed. 
- Both table and graph display if the patient meets the criteria to have the data element displayed. 
- If you select Graph Only , and also select General Options >  Hide "No Data" Elements , then on viewing patient profiles : 
- The graph does not display if the patient does not meet the criteria to have this data element displayed. 
- The graph displays if the patient meets the criteria to have the data element displayed. 
- If you select Table Only , and also select General Options > Hide "No Data" Elements , then on viewing patient profiles: 
- The table does not display if the patient does not meet the criteria to have this data element displayed. 
- The table displays if the patient meets the criteria to have the data element displayed 
- The Visit Date Column  option now displays under Graph Options. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: trends_plots_improve_your_ability_to_monitor_variable_data_across_sites | Trends Plots Improve Your Ability to Monitor Variable Data Across Sites =====
## Trends Plots Improve Your Ability to Monitor Variable Data Across Sites
## Description
 Trends plots graphically display a variable's data at each site from a side-by-side perspective.
 Trends plots for a single numeric variable are output using a box plot.  Trends plots for a single text variable are output using a stacked bar chart. 
 Detect also computes a strength of association for each variable. The strength of association indicates the likelihood that patients at an individual site will have reported the same or similar numeric or text values for a particular variable. The higher a variable's strength of association, the more likely it will be that all or most reported values at a site will be the same or similar. Medidata Detect calculates strength of association on a range from 0.00 to 1.00. 
## Affected Roles
- Site Monitors 
- Data Managers 
- Medical Monitors 
## Advantages
 Trends plots allow you to easily compare a variable's patient-reported data across sites to help you pinpoint sites with abnormal or incorrect data that may warrant investigation.
 Trends plots greatly increase your ability to focus on and monitor variables that are important to your study.
 By knowing a variable's strength of association, you gain clearer expectations for how each individual site should report patient data. For example, if a variable has a very high strength of association, but one particular site contains a high level of variance in reported data points for that variable, then you might want to investigate that site.
## User Impact
 On the Error Plots page, you can click the Trends List tab to display a list of variables in the Trends List. You can click a variable in the Trends List to display the variable's graphical output for each site and accompanying Summary data in the Trends Plot tab.
 Tip : Click to enlarge the Trends Plot stacked bar chart image and box plot image below, respectively.
 To learn more, see  Trends Plots .
 The Error Plots page also provides  additional high-level performance-related plot variable metrics next to the plot list for:
- Strength of Association 
## Special Considerations
- Trends plots only output for single text variables and single numeric variables. 
- You can only view trends plots for sites that you have access to view in Detect.

===== PAGE: uncover_potential_duplicate_patients | Uncover Potential Duplicate Patients =====
## Uncover Potential Duplicate Patients
## Description 
 Duplicate patients are patients who enroll in clinical trials for financial gain or for extra dosages of medication. This problem is more prevalent in certain types of trials such as pain, dependencies, or trials where monetary compensation and low impact of multiple dosings prompts some patients to enroll more than once. Duplicate patients threaten both participant safety and the integrity of research findings. 
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) uncovers potential duplicate patients by analyzing six demographics: date of birth, gender, height, weight, race, and ethnicity. Additionally, CSM also analyzes the physical distance within 100 miles of the site location of each patient to find patients that look very similar. Patients with too many similarities may indicate that those patients are indeed the same person. 
## Affected Roles
 Central monitors
## Advantages
 Identifying and removing potential duplicate patients from the study: 
- Prevents financial loss 
- Yields cleaner data 
- Improves the chances of study success 
## User Impact
 Tip: Click image to enlarge.

- You must configure the study in Detect Landing Page > Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) > CSM Configuration to identify potential duplicate patients in CSM. The interactive heat map will not show if you fail to configure the study. A message will alert that the study has no configuration. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: update_derived_variable_workflow | Update Derived Variable Workflow =====
## Update Derived Variable Workflow
## Description
 You can update your derived variables' name and label with the derived variables update workflow.
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables permission.
## Advantages
 If you created a derived variable with an incorrect name or label, you can update the variable instead of creating another variable.
## User Impact
 You can rename derived variables by selecting   Derived Variable in the application's left menu, then  n avigating to a data set > derived  variable  within Data Sets list and clicking derived . 
## Special Considerations
 You cannot update derived variables that are in use by other applications.

===== PAGE: updates_to_date_format_display_and_behavior_in_patient_profiles | Updates to Date Format Display and Behavior in Patient Profiles =====
## Updates to Date Format Display and Behavior in Patient Profiles
## Description
 Patient Profiles 2018.2.0 updates the date format display and behavior:
- Non-conformant dates display as entered in tables and do not display on timelines or graphs.
- UN or UNK values display as entered in table elements, and change to Jan for UN or UNK month or 01 for day to display on timelines or graphs.
- Date formats display in elements to align with the CSA date display.
- PRF_DAT displays in tables in full formatting including the timestamp; for example, 2016-04-01 00:00:00.0.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Updating the data format display and behavior provides:
- consistency of date handling between CSA and Patient Profiles, and  
- visibility to non-conformant date data. 
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: updates_to_detect_user_permissions | Updates to Detect User Permissions =====
## Updates to Detect User Permissions
## Description
 Centralized Statistical Monitoring, Key Risk Indicators, Quality Tolerance Limits, Data Reviewer, and Detect Configuration Manager include updates to permissions in your customer-defined platform role. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 The Centralized Statistical Monitoring, Key Risk Indicators, Quality Tolerance Limits, and Detect Configuration Manager permission update support the new Detect style.
 The updated Data Reviewer permissions allow you to access Data Reviewer as per your roles.
## User Impact

- The following permission labels are updated:
- Manage Detect CSM From Manage Detect

- View Detect Risk Categories Perspective

- View Detect Domains Perspective

 For Quality Tolerance Limits:
- The following permission labels are updated:
- View QTL Dashboard From View QTL 
 For Data Reviewer:
- To access Medidata Detect > Patient Data Surveillance > Data Reviewer, you must have the following   permissions to your customer-defined platform role in Data Reviewer.
- View Data Reviewer - to view listings. 
- Manage Data Reviewer - to create, edit, and approve listings. 
- Submit Queries - additional permission to submit Rave queries for a listing record. You must have either the View Data Viewer or the Manage Data Viewer permission to view listings. 
 For Detect Configuration Manager:

- Manage Detect Configuration 
- Manage KRI Configuration 
- View KRI Configuration 
- View QTL Configuration 
- Manage QTL Configuration 
- View Detect Configuration

===== PAGE: updates_to_qtl_details_when_defining_custom_qtls | Updates to QTL Details When Defining Custom QTLs =====
## Updates to QTL Details When Defining Custom QTLs
## Description
 When you add or edit custom QTLs , the Quality Tolerance Limit dialog box includes the following new fields: 
- Final Population (# of Patients) – Total number of patients expected to enroll in the study.
 Tip : A djust the expected number of patients to correspond with protocol revisions or if the study is over- or under-enrolled. 
- Trigger Point – The minimum required number of patients that meet the QTL's conditions for Detect to analyze and output the QTL's results in Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM).
 Tip : We recommend entering 25 or higher in Trigger Point.
 The dialog box no longer includes the following fields: 
- Analysis Type 
- Number 
- Percentage 
- Sides 
## Affected Roles
 Detect Configuration Manager Admin 
## Advantages
 Final population and trigger point details help Detect better calculate the QTL's lower and upper threshold limit confidence levels. Therefore, Detect provides more accurate, reliable QTL results for clearer data analysis and better informed study decisions.
 Detect Configuration Manager no longer allows you to create QTLs measured by total subject count. Therefore, the Analysis Type field and its associated subfields, Number and Percentage, are removed since these details are no longer required.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Detect Configuration Manager Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
- Add and Edit Custom QTLs 
## Special Considerations
 The number entered in Trigger Point must be less than the number entered in Final Population (# of patients).
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: upgraded_one_of_operator_available_for_derived_variables | Upgraded One Of Operator Available For Derived Variables =====
## Upgraded One Of Operator Available For Derived Variables
## Description
 When using the Expression Builder or Conditional Concatenate workflow to build derived variables, when you add the  One of operator for a selected data set, the corresponding data variable values populate the expression's next field as a list. You can then select or remove values from the list, then click Apply to confirm selection, and then complete the expression. The  field indicates the number of selected values. When you hover your cursor over the field, then a tooltip shows the selected values. 
 Tip : Click the image to enlarge. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the Manage Derived Variables building block. 
## Advantages
 With upgraded One of operators available, you can configure derived variables to see the data you need and take appropriate action. 
## User Impact
 To create derived variables, you must select a combination of data set variables from the Derived Variables > Data Sets tab and operators from the Derived Variables > Operators tab. For more information, see Description. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None. 
## Special Considerations
- You can use the one of operators only for IF-THEN-ELSE blocks in the Expression Builder and Conditional Concatenate workflows. 
- For simple expressions, the Conditional Concatenate workflow also includes the contains, is missing, isnot missing operators. 
- The operators list for Derived Variables also includes the which you can use to obtain the absolute value of numeric variables. 
- You cannot edit the configuration for an existing derived variable. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the   Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: use_the_event_table_check_box_to_turn_wide_tables_into_event_tables | Use the Event Table Check Box to Turn Wide Tables into Event Tables =====
## Use the Event Table Check Box to Turn Wide Tables into Event Tables
## Description
 When working with wide tables on the Design page > Elements tab, the Table Options tab > Timeline Options section replaces the 'Show in Timeline' check box label with 'Event Table.'
## Affected Roles
- Patient Profile Designers 
## Advantages
 The previous label, 'Show in Timeline,' was often unclear to patient profile designers. The new label, 'Event Table,' more clearly indicates that selecting its check box turns the wide table into an event table.
## User Impact
 See the Description section.
## Special Considerations
 The Event Table check box only applies to wide tables.

===== PAGE: user_interface_changes_to_risk_table_column_headers | User Interface Changes to Risk Table Column Headers =====
## User Interface Changes to Risk Table Column Headers
## Description
 There are changes to the risk form fields in the Risk Management 2021.2.0 release. Some fields have been moved or renamed, and the order of columns on the Risk Inventory and Risk Category pages has changed. These changes affect the risk context view on the Critical Data, Critical Processes, Risk Categorization, and Risk Inventory pages. 
## Affected Roles
 Study User.
## Advantages
 Improved navigation and labeling on the Risk Management pages provide a more consistent user experience with the software. 
## User Impact
 These fields, which held self-defined indicators in past releases, have been repurposed and enhanced:  
- Indicator Type 
- Indicator Description 
- Indicator Value 
 Instead of entering indicator type, description, or value, you can, optionally, enter these components on separate tabs in the risk form:
- Quality Tolerance Limits (QTLs) 
- Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) 
- Risk Mitigations 
 Additional filters for   QTLs and KRIs have been added to the top of the Risk Inventory page.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: user_interface_changes_to_the_risk_plan_report | User Interface Changes to the Risk Plan Report =====
## User Interface Changes to the Risk Plan Report
## Description
 The Risk Plan Report labels have changed to align with other Risk Management Reports.
## Affected Roles
 Study User.
## Advantages
 Improved labeling on the Risk Management report pages provides a more consistent user experience when generating reports. 
## User Impact
- The Risk Plan Reports label in the left pane is renamed to Reports . 
- From the Reports tab, you can generate a PDF version of either the Risk Plan Report or Quality Tolerance Limit QTL Summary Report. 
- Changes to Risk Plan Report details automatically save as soon as you enter new or updated information. You do not have to manually save changes when you edit the report details. 
- The pane titled Risk Plan Participants has been renamed to Participants . Adding or deleting Participant records for one report automatically updates the Participant lists available for use in all Risk Management reports. 
- You can issue a bulk selection request for all participants by clicking the check box in the header of the Participants list. Click once to select all check boxes. Click again to cancel the selection of all check boxes. 
## Special Considerations
 The Generate Risk Plan Reports building block name has changed to Generate Reports .

===== PAGE: using_space_and_operators_in_derived_variable_name_validation | Using Space And Operators In Derived Variable Name Validation =====
## Using Space And Operators In Derived Variable Name Validation
## Description
 The derived variable creation workflow now expands Name field validation to disallow blank space and AND/OR operators. 
## Affected Roles
 All roles with the View Data building block.
## Advantages
 The expanded validation ensures that you do not accidentally name derived variables with names such as derived variable and derived AND OR variable .  
## User Impact
 A warning message appears when you attempt to save a derived variable that has a blank space or uses AND/Operators without an underscore in the Name field.
## Special Considerations
 Within a given data set, you can use an  underscore  to add blank space or AND/OR operators to derived variable names. For example,  Sample_dv_and_or_name  is permitted but not Sample dv and or name.

===== PAGE: vendor_queries__vendor_query_shows_vendor_personnel_name_after_vendor_provides_response | Vendor Queries: Vendor Query Shows Vendor Personnel Name After Vendor Provides Response =====
## Vendor Queries: Vendor Query Shows Vendor Personnel Name After Vendor Provides Response
## What Is New?
 In Data Surveillance > Vendor Queries, if you click any vendor query set, and then click a query, the Vendor Response section in the Vendor Query slide out panel shows the vendor contact who responded to the query. 
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
- All vendors with the Submit Vendor Feedback role. 
- Data managers. 
## Workflow Process
 Data managers review listings to identify issues with vendor data and submit the query set to the vendor. Vendors receive an email with a hyperlink to access the notification centre. Vendors then add comments, update query status, provide clarification for the queries in the notification centre. The query set gets updated with the vendors' response for further data manager review and the vendor response section shows the name of the vendor personnel who responded to the query. 
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data managers can track vendor query responses and follow up with the right vendor personnel to resolve vendor queries in the study.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 See What is New?.
## Where Do I Learn More?
 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Create, view. delete, and submit vendor query sets 
## What Else Should I Know?
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .
