===== PAGE: view_a_patient_s_profile_from_detect_to_analyze_patient-level_details | View a Patient's Profile from Detect to Analyze Patient-Level Details =====
## View a Patient's Profile from Detect to Analyze Patient-Level Details
## Description
 Detect users with authorized Medidata Patient Profiles access can launch and view individual patient profiles from Detect's Error Plots page and Event Incidence Plot page. You can also save and print the patient profiles as a PDF. 
## Affected Roles
- Data managers 
- Medical Monitors 
## Advantages
 Within Detect, authorized users can quickly navigate to a patient's data within Patients Profiles. This enables you to: 
- Quickly drill into Patient Profiles directly from Detect's error plot  and event incidence plot to help you better understand the patient's data in context. 
- Seamlessly perform data point analysis on specific patients to determine why the patient is an outlier . 
- Conveniently view data in a per-patient format to understand the patients’ journey throughout the trial. 
## User Impact
 You can navigate to a patient's data within Patient Profiles from the Error Plots page or Event Incidence Plot page.
 On the Error Plots page, you can access a patient's profile using the following methods:
- When viewing a Text Analysis plot  or Text Versus Text Analysis plot: click an individual data point to view additional details , and then click any blue, hyperlinked patient ID in the Patient column. Clicking a patient ID launches that individual patient's profile in a new tab. 
- When viewing any error plot visualization type: navigate to the Summary table > select Patient or Data: Top 100 Outliers from the View By dropdown > click any blue, hyperlinked patient ID in the Patient column.  Clicking a patient ID launches that individual patient's profile in a new tab. 
 On the Event Incidence Plot page, you can access a patient's profile using the following method: 
- Click an individual data point to view additional details , and then click any blue, hyperlinked patient ID in the Patient column. Clicking a patient ID launches that individual patient's profile in a new tab. 
 Within the patient profile window, you can click the View PDF button to view and save the patient profile as a PDF. 
## Special Considerations
 You can only view patient profiles for patients that have a master patient profile design configured in Medidata Patient Profiles . 
 Only users with 'View Profile' Cloud Administration  permission granted can view patient IDs as hyperlinks and access individual patient profiles from Detect.

## View All Patient Queries in One Location

## Where Do I See the Change?

## Where Do I Learn More?

- View Open and Answered Query Records 
## What Else Should I Know?
 The list of open queries automatically refresh every 12 hours. 
 An admin must associate the View Clean Patient Tracker building block to a role in your Cloud Administration study group so that you can access the Open Queries page. 
 Otherwise, the links on the Detect Landing Page > Insights card show as inactive.

===== PAGE: view_and_create_issues_on_the_weekend_and_holiday_visits_page | View and Create Issues on the Weekend and Holiday Visits Page =====
## View and Create Issues on the Weekend and Holiday Visits Page
## Description
 Medidata Detect-Issue Management integration now allows authorized users working in Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) to: 
- View site- and country-level weekend and holiday visits that are flagged with one or more issues.
- View a list of issues and associated issue details observed for specific weekend and holiday visits, such as issue description, issue creation date, and issue status.
- Launch Issue Management's New Issue page to create issues for site- and county-level weekend and holiday visits.
- Launch Issue Management directly to a specific issue's page to view or edit that issue's details and statuses. 
## Affected Roles
 Central Monitors. 
## Advantages
 CSM provides a centralized, singular workspace to log, track, and manage issues while jointly reviewing your study data analysis. This yields the following benefits: 
- Streamlined issue logging. 
- Reduced recurrence of duplicate issues. 
- Clear line of sight of site or country  issues and issue status. 
- Reduced time and cost required to create and manage issues. 
- Enhanced work experience and productivity in a centralized location. 
- Improved ability to identify and mitigate risks to protocol compliance, patient safety, data integrity, and overall study quality. 
## User Impact
 From the  Weekend and Holiday Visits page > Issues tab, authorized users can: 
- View site- and county-level weekend and holiday visits that are flagged as having one or more closed and open issues. 
- View a list of issues and associated issue details observed for specific data points, such as issue description, issue creation date, and issue status. 
- Create issues for  site- and county-level weekend and holiday visits. 
 Important : When creating an issue, Issue Management opens up directly from the CSM user interface. Upon saving the issue, you automatically navigate back to CSM and the Weekend and Holiday Visits page automatically reloads to include the new issue.
- Drill down to an individual issue and open that issue in Issue Management  to update the issue details and status . 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Centralized Statistical Monitoring Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature: 
- Investigate Site Visits On Non-Business Days 
## Special Considerations
 To view issue flags and issue details, you must have the following Cloud Administration  permissions granted: 
- View Issues, Create Issues, or Edit Issues 
- Read Issue Management Settings 
 To edit issues, you must have the following Cloud Administration permissions granted: 
- Create Issues or Edit Issues 
- Read Issue Management Settings 
 To create issues, you must have the following Cloud Administration permissions granted: 
- Create Issues 
- Read Issue Management Settings 
 You can create protocol deviation  issues and non-protocol deviation issues at the site level. However, you can only create non-protocol deviation issues at the country level. 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

## Description

 Viewing and printing a patient profile in PDF format allows you to  send the patient profile to design reviewers who do not have access to Medidata Patient Profiles. Therefore, reviewers without Medidata Patient Profiles can still evaluate the patient profile design and provide feedback to the designer regarding design layout adjustments.

===== PAGE: view_and_track_user-defined_custom_kris | View and Track User-Defined Custom KRIs =====
## View and Track User-Defined Custom KRIs
## Description
 In addition to the pre-defined system KRIs  provided by Medidata, you can now view user-defined system KRIs in the custom KRIs .
 Users in your study environment can create and activate custom KRIs using Medidata's RBQM Configuration Manager. With RBQM Configuration Manager, you create KRIs by defining:
- A unique name for the custom KRI, 
- The data sets and variables  you want to perform calculations on, and 
- The type of calculations you want performed on the data sets and variables:
- Count  – Calculates the total number of entries in the selected data set. The Count calculation is only available at the data set level. 
- Count Values  – Calculates the count of patients in the study that meet a specified criteria based on the selected variable. 
- Mean  – Calculates the the mean value of a numeric data field based on the selected variable.  
- Rate  – Calculates the rate of entries in the selected data set over time. The Rate calculation is only available at the data set level. 
- Rate Values  – Calculates the percentage of patients in the study that meet a specified criteria based on the selected variable. 
- Standard Deviation  – Calculates the amount of dispersion or variance in a set of observed values based on the selected variable. 
 When activated, a custom KRI's data gets consumed, analyzed, calculated, and rendered in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table.
## Affected Roles
- Risk managers 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 Defining and tracking custom KRIs helps your organization target and track unique and specific facets of your study that you want to monitor for risk. 
## User Impact
 You do not create or manage custom KRIs in Medidata Detect. Rather, you or other users in your study environment can create and manage custom KRIs in a separate Medidata app, RBQM Configuration Manager.
 However, when activated in RBQM Configuration Manager, you can view custom KRIs and their associated KRI values in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table just as you would for system KRIs.
## Special Considerations
- System KRIs are always available and activated in the Key Risk Indicators table, even if no custom KRIs are defined or activated. 
- System KRIs and Custom KRIs with errors display as grayed out with no KRI values in the Key Risk Indicators table.

===== PAGE: view_and_track_user-defined_custom_percentage_kris | View and Track User-Defined Custom Percentage KRIs =====
## View and Track User-Defined Custom Percentage KRIs
## Description
 You can now view and track user-defined custom percentage KRIs.
 Users in your study environment can create and activate custom percentage KRIs using Medidata's RBQM Configuration Manager . With RBQM Configuration Manager, you create custom percentage KRIs by defining:
- A unique name and description for the custom percentage KRI. 
- The risk category  to target the KRI's risk analysis to a specific area of risk. 
- The expression used to query your study database to assess  if subjects meet certain conditions or criteria. 
 Medidata Detect produces an incidence analysis on the custom percentage KRI, which you can view  in Detect's Key Risk Indicators table  and Contributors list. 
## Affected Roles
- Risk managers 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 Custom percentage KRIs provide you greater control and flexibility of the specific data and metrics that you want Medidata Detect to analyze and report. Therefore, you can better target your study data analysis on areas that most require your attention to optimally monitor and investigate risk. 
## User Impact
 When the custom percentage KRI is activated in RBQM Configuration Manager, the KRI's data gets consumed, analyzed, calculated, and rendered in Medidata Detect's Key Risk Indicators table  and Contributors list. 
## Special Considerations
 The Key Risk Indicators table displays percentage KRIs with a KRI value of zero.

===== PAGE: view_comprehensive_audits_of_kri_and_qtl_configurations | View Comprehensive Audits of KRI and QTL Configurations =====
## View Comprehensive Audits of KRI and QTL Configurations
## Description
 Detect Configuration Manager's KRI Configurations module and QTL Configuration module now integrate with Audit Viewer so that you can view audit reports of KRI and QTL configurations . 
## Affected Roles
 Detect users assigned the Manage KRI Configuration and Manage QTL Configuration permissions.
## Advantages
 Audit reports:
- Provides Detect Configuration Admins with a clear history and coordination of KRI and QTL configuration changes made. 
- Enable sponsors to quickly and effectively show compliance with clear, comprehensive audit details of actions performed in KRI Configuration and QTL Configuration. 
- Provide sponsors with more oversight to ensure study data is monitored correctly. 
## User Impact
 You can click  next to the Detect Configuration Manager's Key Risk Indicators page header or Quality Tolerance Limits page header. When  you click , the KRIs Audit Report or QTLs Audit Report appears, respectively, in Audit Viewer on a separate tab. In Audit Viewer, you can see the audit history of the KRI or QTL configurations and modifications in your study environment. 
## Knowledge Hub Updates
 The Medidata Detect Knowledge Hub provides new and updated content to support this feature: 
- Generate KRI Configuration Audit Reports 
- Generate QTL Configuration Audit Reports 
## Special Considerations
 You can only view actions created against sites that you have access to.
 Audits only report actions performed as of the Detect Configuration Manager 2023.1.0 release. Actions performed before the 2023.1.0 release are not audited.
 The Audit Viewer report may show a configured KRI or QTL's details separated across several records in the list.
 You may see multiple records for a KRI or QTL creation, because the metadata and configuration are coming from different tables.

## View Current and Historical QTL Value Trends
## Description

- QTL value behavior based on number of study patients. 
## Affected Roles
- Study managers 
- Medical monitors

- Identify as well as prevent or mitigate systematic issues early on in the study that may: 
- Threaten subject safety or study efficacy. 
- Invalidate the reliability of the study findings. 
- Determine the impact of mitigating actions made on a QTL's target study parameter.

- Live – View each QTL's status based on the new QTL calculation approach - considering expectation, threshold, and upper limit. 
- Patients – View each QTL's performance (observed value compared to expectation, threshold, and limit) against the number of patients from the target population at the time (dates only) the QTL was run. 
- Time – View each QTL's performance (observed value compared to expectation, threshold, and limit) over time, where timepoints are QTL data run datestamps.  
 To learn more, see About Quality Tolerance Limits .

===== PAGE: view_event_incidence_at_the_site-_and_study-level | View Event Incidence at the Site- and Study-level =====
## View Event Incidence at the Site- and Study-level
## Description
 The Event Incidence Plot is a scatter plot that displays your study's patient-reported events and the rate the events occurred at the site- and study-level. 
 You can use the Event Incidence Plot to analyze:
- Which specific event terms were reported as experienced by patients within a domain at the site level. 
- How many patients at a specific site reported an event term compared to all patients at the site. This is also known as the incidence rate. 
- The incidence rate for reported event terms at each individual site compared to the overall study event incidence rates. 
- Which sites are considered  statistically  normal, outliers, or extreme outliers in terms of probability of having the event occur. 
## Affected Roles
- Central monitors 
- Data managers 
- Medical monitors 
## Advantages
 By analyzing event terms in your study, you can:
- Identify whether sites are tracking events correctly. For example, whether a site is over or underreporting adverse events. 
- View event trending patterns. For example, if a large number of patients at a site experience headaches. 
- Detect correlation between events. For example, if a large number of patients at a site experience URTI and increased heart rate. 
- Identify sites that have significantly higher or lower incidence rates for individual events compared to overall study event incidence rates. 
 Based on your findings, you can determine appropriate corresponding actions such as to:
- Investigate sites to ensure proper protocols and procedures are being followed. 
- Discontinue the drug. 
## User Impact
 You can access the Event Incidence Plot on the Event Incidence Plot page. To learn more, see  Event Incidence Plot . 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: view_historical_data_snapshots_in_detect | View Historical Data Snapshots in Detect =====
## View Historical Data Snapshots in Detect
## Description
 Medidata Detect provides a list of historical data snapshots. You can select a data snapshot to enter History View mode to see how the data looked throughout Detect when that the snapshot occurred.
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 Viewing historical data snapshots provides a smoother, more convenient way to audit studies and reconcile the data and actions made between snapshots.
## User Impact
 The Schedule tab in the left-hand menu is now renamed to History tab.
 The History page provides a historical list of all previous data snapshots in your study environment. If you click a snapshot in the list, you can navigate to any Detect page to view what the data points and issues looked like when the snapshot occurred.
 While in History View, a blue banner displays at the top of all Detect pages. The banner indicates the date the historical snapshot's data refresh occurred. For example:
 You can click Exit History View in the blue banner to revert to the latest data snapshot.
## Special Considerations
- History View mode displays the actions that occurred in the immediate data snapshot following the snapshot date you selected to view. For example, say you selected to view a data snapshot with a date of 17 Oct 2020 and the following data snapshot took place on 22 Oct 2020. In such case, History View mode displays the data in Detect as of 17 Oct 2020, but shows the actions made in Detect up until 22 Oct 2020. 
- While in History View mode:
- Data is read-only. 
- The Error Plots page > Summary section > Actions column does not display. 
- The Event Incidence Plot page > Summary section > Actions column does not display. 
- You cannot deep link into Issue Management. 
- You cannot update track review data. 
- Track reviews and issues created are those that occurred against the selected historical snapshot or previous snapshots. That is, the created dates may be after the snapshot date, but before the following snapshot. 
- On the Issues slide-out panel, the Assignee column and Status column do not display. 
- On the Issues slide-out panel, the Is Closed column displays.
 Note : If the issue was resolved after the date of the snapshot being viewed, then Is Close has a value of No. If the resolved date occurred before the date of the snapshot in view, then Is Close has a value of Yes.

- Site Monitors 
## Advantages
 In previous Medidata Detect releases, at any given time you were   only able   to see current KRI values .
 Now Medidata Detect keeps a record of historical data so you can evaluate how the KRI values change over time and how a given site or country's KRI values relate to the overall study data.
 Tracking KRI data over time also helps you determine whether you are correctly managing issues and that any mitigating actions you have taken are resulting in a positive outcome.
## User Impact
 On the KRIs page, you can c lick any cell in the Key Risk Indicators table , and then click the Trend Graph button above the table. 
 Tip : Click image to enlarge.
 Clicking the Trend Graph button displays the selected KRI's historical trending data in a separate modal. 
 On the KRI trend graph, you can: 
- Hover your cursor   over a specific data   point on the graph to view:
- The KRI snapshot date. 
- The KRI value at the selected site or country. 
- The KRI value for all sites or countries in the study. 
- Specify a custom date range to display on the graph by:
- Using the From and To fields, or 
- Clicking and dragging your mouse over a specific area on the bottom graph. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: view_under-_and_overreporting_event_trends_at_the_site_and_country_level | View Under- and Overreporting Event Trends at the Site and Country Level =====
## View Under- and Overreporting Event Trends at the Site and Country Level
## Description
 The Under-Over Reporting Events Plot is a multi-view funnel plot that displays the site- and country-level reported rate of:
- Adverse events over time in months. 
- Concomitant medications compared to the combined number of reported adverse events and ongoing medical history events. 
- Medical history events compared to total number of enrolled patients. 
 The Under-Over Reporting Events Plot simultaneously overlays each site or country data point against funnel lines, which represent the normalized study-wide reported event data thresholds at the:
- Upper 99th percentile 
- Upper 95th percentile 
- Mean 
- Lower 95th percentile 
- Lower 99th percentile 
 The site or country's data point position relative to the funnel lines indicates whether the event reporting rate is considered normal, an outlier, or extremely outlier.
 You can use the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot to identify event reporting non-compliance at the site or country level.
## Affected Roles
 Central monitors
## Advantages
 By analyzing event reporting rates, you can Identify whether sites are reporting events correctly. For example, whether a site is over or underreporting adverse events, concomitant medications, and medical history. 
 Based on your findings, you can determine appropriate corresponding actions such as to:
- Create an issue in Issue Management. 
- Investigate sites to ensure proper protocols and procedures are being followed. 
- Provide training or corrective actions to the site. 
- Discontinue the drug. 
## User Impact
 You can access the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot on the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot page. To learn more, see Under-Over Reporting Events Plot .
## Knowledge Space Updates
 The Centralized Statistical Monitoring Knowledge Space provides new and updated content to support this feature/enhancement: 
- Under-Over Reporting Events Plot 
- Access and View the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot 
- Investigate Data Using the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot 
## Special Considerations
 For the most accurate level of event reporting analysis, we recommend using Detect Configuration Manager's   Event Configuration Analysis   page to map your preferred adverse event, concomitant medication, and medical history terms. 
 To output the concomitant medication analysis on the Under-Over Reporting Events Plot, you must map adverse event, concomitant medication, and medical history terms in Detect Configuration Manager's   Event Configuration Analysis   page 
 To view Medidata testing documentation for this release, refer to the  Medidata Validation Portal .

===== PAGE: visualizations__additional_aggregations_available_for_all_charts | Visualizations: Additional Aggregations Available For All Charts =====
## Visualizations: Additional Aggregations Available For All Charts
## What Is New?
 You can now add aggregations to the X and Y axis such as minimum, maximum, and mode values, for all visualizations except tabular charts. For bar charts, you can also add a median line.
 You can now view a median line on Data Surveillance > Visualizations > Bar Charts that represents a visual reference of the aggregations done in the bar chart configuration. If you click the Add median line option, the bar chart includes a median line.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 All study team members. 
## Workflow Process
 No impact to workflow process.
## Other Applications
 No impact to other applications.
## How Do I Benefit?
 Data managers can perform better statistical analysis with minimum, maximum, and mode aggregations, viewing the visual representation in charts, and using the data from the summary tables across study data. With the median line, you can easily locate medium values for data represented in bar charts and take action as required.
## Where Do I See the Change?
 On the Data Surveillance > Visualizations page > if you click Create Visualizations, then select any chart type (except tabular charts), and drag and drop Y-axis variables, you can then select Min, Max, Mode options to add aggregations as per these mathematical operations.
- Min – For example, if you select Min for Age by Site variable, then the chart Y axis shows the calculated minimum age for each site. If you select Min for Age by Site by Sex, the chart shows calculated minimum age for each by sex. The minimum value also appears in the summary table.  
- Max – For example, if you select Max for Age by Site variable, then the chart Y axis shows the calculated maximum age for each site. If you select Max for Age by Site by Sex, the chart shows calculated maximum age for each by sex. The maximum value also appears in the summary table. 
- Mode – For example, if you select Mode for Site variable, then the chart Y axis shows the age value that occurs the most out of all the patients at any given site. The mode value also appears in the summary table. 
 You can now view a median line on Data Surveillance > Visualizations > Bar Charts that represents a visual reference of the aggregations done in the bar chart configuration. If you click the Add median line option, the bar chart includes a median line.

 Use the following links to find new and updated content in support of the enhancement:
- Creat, Edit, and Delete Visualizations

===== PAGE: visualizations__chart_categorical_study_data_counts_using_tabular_visualizations | Visualizations: Chart Categorical Study Data Counts Using Tabular Visualizations =====
## Visualizations: Chart Categorical Study Data Counts Using Tabular Visualizations
## What Is New?
 Data Surveillance > Visualizations includes a new chart type, tabular visualizations, that you can use to obtain counts or percentages of categorical study data. Tabular visualizations aggregate data by summing or averaging multiple dataset variables in a table format created using Data Connect Transformations . The chart shows data in rows and columns with information summarized (aggregated) at the intersection points. For example, the percentage of patients experiencing the AE at the preferred term level, and the associated seriousness.
 Note : You must have at least one Tabular Visual type collection  in Data Connect to create tabular visualizations in Data Surveillance.
## What Is the Impact?
## Users/Roles
 Data Managers, and users with the Manage Visualizations building block in Data Surveillance, and Manage Data Connect Collections and Manage Transformation Projects building blocks in Data Connect.
## Workflow Process
 The workflow process is as follows:
## Other Applications
 You must have at least one Tabular Visual type collection in Data Connect to create tabular visualizations in Data Surveillance.
## How Do I Benefit?
 With tabular visualizations, data managers can segment populations of interest and identify patient groups for further investigation. Investigating counts or percentages of required parameters in study data enables data managers to:
- Understand treatment efficacy by comparing outcomes and treatments. 
- Evaluate compliance looking at rates of completion and adherence to medication. 
- Explore differential subgroup responses based on demographic or baseline characteristics. 
- Examine how well groups meet primary and secondary endpoints. 
- Analyze AE trends relative to outcomes, treatments, or other effect states.

 On the Data Surveillance > Visualizations page, if you click Add visualization, a new  chart type appears on the New Visualizations page. If you click the tabular chart, the Visualization page shows the following:

===== PAGE: warning_message_displays_for_profile_designers_with_partial_site_or_country_access | Warning Message Displays for Profile Designers with Partial Site or Country Access =====
## Warning Message Displays for Profile Designers with Partial Site or Country Access
## Description
 Profile Designers with partial or no access to sites or countries see a warning message when accessing the Design page > Profiles tab. If you have the correct access, no warning message appears.
## Affected Roles
 Patient Profile Designers.
## Advantages
 Using the IDs displayed in warning messages, patient profile designers can contact support to arrange the correct access.
## User Impact
 See Description.

===== PAGE: warning_messages_to_help_you_avoid_unintentional_data_loss | Warning Messages to Help You Avoid Unintentional Data Loss =====
## Warning Messages to Help You Avoid Unintentional Data Loss
## Description
 Risk Management 2022.2.0 introduces warning messages when you add, edit, or delete a risk or a Critical Data, Critical Process, or Risk Categorization template. This helps prevent unintentional data loss if you change your mind or select the X , Cancel , or Delete options by mistake. 
## Affected Roles
 All.
## Advantages
 If you click the X , Cancel , or Delete buttons in error, this could lead to unintentional data loss. The addition of a warning message helps you avoid the accidental click of X , Cancel , or Delete. 
## User Impact
 Warning messages appear when there is a risk of unintentional data loss. The messages alert you to cancel or confirm an action. The warning messages appear when you: 
- Create, edit, or delete a risk or a risk category associated with a study. 
- Navigate between the Add New Risk category and Select Risk category tabs when adding a risk category. 
- Delete or modify an existing risk associated with Critical Data, Critical Processes, Risk Categorizations, or Risk Categorization templates. 
- Click Cancel while creating or editing Critical Data, Critical Processes, or Risk Categorization templates. Clicking Cancel closes the page, and data entered in the template is lost. 
- Update the Add Review frequency when adding a new risk to a Critical Data, Critical process, or Risk Categorization template. 
- Update the Target Review Date and Review Status when reviewing or editing a risk associated to a Critical Data, Critical process, or Risk Categorization template. 
- Update the Last Reviewed by and Mark Reviewed fields when reviewing a risk associated to a Critical Data, Critical process, or Risk Categorization template. 
- Add Review Status, Frequency, and Review Dates in the Risk Inventory. 
- Update the Risk Status to Closed. You can no longer edit other fields on the Risk Review form. 
- Close or transfer a risk. 
## Knowledge Space Updates
 None.
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: wide_table_variable_color_configuration_functionality_restored | Wide Table Variable Color Configuration Functionality Restored =====
## Wide Table Variable Color Configuration Functionality Restored
## Description
 In the Medidata Patient Profiles 2020.1.0 release, the wide table timeline option to configure the color of variable data points was removed to improve integration with other Medidata products. The ability to configure the color of variable data points in wide table timelines is restored and available for use again. 
## Affected Roles
- Unblinded Patient Profiles Designer 
- Blinded Patient Profiles Designer 
## Advantages
 You can configure variable data points to display in the timeline in the color of your choosing to make profiles easier to scan and read. 
## User Impact
 On the Design page > Elements tab:   When working in Wide Tables,  the TABLE OPTIONS tab > Timeline Options > Color options for functionality is re-enabled. You can once again configure the color of the variable data points in wide tables that display in timelines. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: wide_tables_allow_positioning_of_graph_and_table | Wide Tables Allow Positioning Of Graph And Table =====
## Wide Tables Allow Positioning Of Graph And Table
## Description
 You can configure wide tables to display tables, graphs, or both for data elements. You can configure wide tables to position graphs and tables above or below the data element. You can also configure specific data variables in wide tables to display in tables, graphs, or in both.  
## Affected Roles
 All. 
## Advantages
 Showing data elements in graph and table format provides facilitates better insight into specific data points in profile designs. 
## User Impact
 When you are working on wide tables on the Design page > Elements tab > Table Options> Graph Options> Table and Graph, you can select Show Both , Table Only or Graph Only . Depending on the selection, wide tables display the graph or table or both for data elements. 
- If you do not select Show Both ,  Table Only  or  Graph Only , then Table Only is the default option. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only tables display for the element. 
- If you select Table Only , graph options become disabled. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only tables display for the element. 
- If you select Graph Only , graph options become enabled. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, only graphs display for the element. 
- If you select Show Both , graph options become enabled. If you then switch to Table Only , graph options become disabled and become enabled when you switch to Graph Only . 
- If you select Show Both , and then click the vertical ellipsis in a data variable's name,  Show only in Table ,  Show only in Graph , or Show in Both options display . 
- If you select  Show only in Table ,  displays indicating that the variable does not display in graphs. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable only displays in tables for the patient. 
- If you select  Show only in Graph ,   displays indicating that the variable does not display in tables. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable only displays in graphs for the patient. 
- If you select  Show in Both or select neither  Show only in Table , nor  Show only in Graph , no additional icon displays near the data variable's name. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable displays both in graphs and tables for the patient. 
- If you do not select Show Both ,  Table Only , or  Graph Only , then Table Only is the default option. On viewing profiles on the Profiles page, the variable displays in tables for the patient. 
- If you select Show Both ,  
- and then set  Table Position to Above Graph , the table appears above the graph while viewing profiles on the Profiles page. 
- and then set  Table Position to Below Graph , the table appears below the graph while viewing profiles on the Profiles page. 
- The Visit Date Column  option now appears under Graph Options. 
## Special Considerations
 None.

===== PAGE: wide_tables_display_conditions_restored | Wide Tables Display Conditions Restored =====
## Wide Tables Display Conditions Restored
## Description
 In Patient Profiles 2020.2.0, the Conditional Options feature has been reinstated for transposed and wide tables. 
## Affected Roles
 All
## Advantages
 Restoring wide and transported table conditional options ensures you can identify patients who have specific conditions or fulfil a set criteria. 
## User Impact
 The Design page > Elements tab includes the following changes: 
- The Add Element > Table button displays the Transposed Table option when clicked. 
- When working in Wide Tables: 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options section displays. 
- When working in Transposed Tables: 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Graph Options > Red Border if Value Outside Shaded Range check box displays. 
- When working in Wide and Transposed Tables: 
- The TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options section displays.  
- If you define upper and lower limit variables in the Normal Range section, and then if you set up a variable outside the defined range, a " Conditional highlighting is disabled when High and Low Indicators are turned on" message appears. 
- If you define upper and lower limit variables in the Normal Range section, then TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Highlight Conditions are disabled. Otherwise, they are enabled. 
- If you use TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Highlight Conditions section, the Normal Range section is disabled. Otherwise, it is enabled. 
- If you use TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Highlight Conditions section, and then if you set up a variable outside the defined range, a " High and Low indicators are disabled when Conditional highlighting is turned on" message appears. 
- If you use the TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Display Conditions, you can click Add to select variables to create an expression that determines if specific elements in a table are shown or hidden. You can add one or two display conditions. 
- If you use the TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Highlight Conditions, you can click Add to select variables to create an expression that determines if specific elements in a table are shown or hidden. You can add one or two highlight conditions. 
- If you use the TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Display Conditions, you can click Add to select variables to create an expression that determines if view specific rows in a table are shown or hidden. You can add one or two display conditions. 
- If you use the TABLE OPTIONS tab > Conditional Options > Highlight Conditions, you can click Add to select variables to create an expression that determines if specific rows in a table are shown or hidden. You can add one or two highlight conditions. 
## Special Considerations
 None.
